'''Cherami Leigh Kuehn'''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dualshockers.com/fortnite-fans-are-convinced-a-huge-marvel-actor-is-the-voice-of-paradigm/|title=Fortnite Fans are convinced a huge Marvel actor is the voice of Paradigm|last=Knight|first=Kyle|website=Dualshockers|date=June 6, 2022|access-date=February 16, 2025|archive-date=August 24, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230824090106/https://www.dualshockers.com/fortnite-fans-are-convinced-a-huge-marvel-actor-is-the-voice-of-paradigm/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/1023599760/ | title=18th annual Collin Theatre Center Award winners | newspaper=[[McKinney Courier-Gazette]] | date=May 27, 2010 | accessdate=February 16, 2025 | page=6A }}</ref> (born July 19, 1988)<ref name="Birthday">Birthday references:
* {{cite tweet|author=Funimation|user=Funimation_ANZ|number=1284646673755635712|title=Happy birthday to the amazingly talented Cherami Leigh!|date=July 19, 2020|access-date=February 17, 2025}}
* {{cite web|url=https://lionsbanebooking.com/project/cherami-leigh/|title=Cherami Leigh|publisher=Lionsbane Booking Agency|access-date=February 16, 2025}}</ref> is an American actress. She has provided voices for a number of English-language versions of [[anime]] series and video games.

==Early life and education==
Leigh began acting at the age of six.<ref name="resume"/> Leigh studied the [[Meisner technique]] with Nancy Chartier from the age of nine.<ref name="resume"/> As a child actress, she played Gretchen in ''[[Finding North]]'', Marcia in ''[[Temple Grandin (film)|Temple Grandin]]'', young [[LeAnn Rimes]] in ''[[Holiday in Your Heart]]'', Stacy Anderson in ''The President's Man'' and appeared on ''[[Walker, Texas Ranger]]'' multiple times.<ref name="resume"/>

She attended [[Hebron High School (Texas)|Hebron High School]] in Carrollton and studied theater at [[Collin College]], a public community college in [[Plano, Texas]].<ref name="resume"/>

==Career==
She also worked for [[Radio Disney]] as a DJ with voice-over promotions and commercials for [[ABC Radio (United States)|ABC Radio]] for 10 years.<ref name="resume"/> In 2013, she moved to [[Los Angeles]] where she continued voice-work and began taking on live-action roles.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dallas.culturemap.com/news/entertainment/12-18-13-cry-movie-clay-luther-new-filmmakers-series-anthology-film-archives/#slide=0|title=Filmmaker packs debut feature with Dallas talent and takes on Big Apple|work=culturemap.com|date=December 18, 2013|access-date=February 14, 2017|archive-date=February 14, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170214184928/http://dallas.culturemap.com/news/entertainment/12-18-13-cry-movie-clay-luther-new-filmmakers-series-anthology-film-archives/#slide=0|url-status=live}}</ref>

of Strike Witches characters#Yoshika Miyafuji|Yoshika Miyafuji]] in ''[[Strike Witches]]'', [[Is This a Zombie?#Eucliwood Hellscythe|Eucliwood Hellscythe]] in ''[[Is This a Zombie?]]'', [[Japanese In video games, she voices Rottytops in the ''[[Shantae]]'' series, Gaige the Mechromancer in the ''[[Borderlands (series)|Borderlands]]'' series, Arianrhod in ''[[The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel IV]]'', Minerva in ''[[The Walking Dead: The Final Season]]'', Rhea in ''[[Fire Emblem: Three Houses]]'', [[List of Danganronpa characters#Danganronpa Another Episode: Ultra Despair Girls|Komaru Naegi]] in ''[[Danganronpa Another Episode: Ultra Despair Girls]]'', [[Makoto Niijima]] in ''[[Persona 5]]'', Cotton Cookie in Cookie Run: Kingdom, and the Female V in ''[[Cyberpunk 2077]]'' for which she was nominated for a [[British Academy Games Award for Performer in a Leading Role|BAFTA Award for Performer in a Leading Role]].

==Personal life==

{{short description|Mexican professional wrestler and actor}} {{about|the wrestler|the TV series|Blue Demon (TV series)|the 2004 film|Blue Demon (film)}} {{missing information|more detail on the person's life, and career|date=April 2018}} {{Use mdy dates|date=February 2019}} {{Infobox person | name = Blue Demon | birth_name = Alejandro Muñoz Moreno | image = Luchador Blue Demon en Blue Demon y las invasoras (1969).jpg | caption = Blue Demon in ''Blue Demon y las invasoras'' (1969) | birth_date = {{birth date|1922|10|12}} | birth_place = [[García, Nuevo León]], Mexico | children = [[Blue Demon Jr.]] (adopted) | spouse = Gregoria Moreno | death_date = {{death date and age|2000|12|16|1922|4|24}} | death_place = [[Mexico City]], Mexico | burial_place = Parque Memorial Gayosso
[[Naucalpan|Naucalpan de Juárez]] | module = {{Infobox professional wrestler | child=yes | ring_names = {{Unbulleted list|Tosco Muñoz|Blue Demon ("Demonio Azul"){{cite web|url=https://www.cagematch.net/?id=2&nr=3217|title=Blue Demon|access-date=August 11, 2017|work=Cagematch.net}}}} | height = {{convert|1.69|m|ftin|0|abbr=on}} | weight = {{convert|77|kg|lb|abbr=on}} | trainer = [[Rolando Vera (wrestler)|Rolando Vera]] | debut = March 31, 1948 | retired = August 27, 1989 }} }} '''Alejandro Muñoz Moreno''' (October 12, 1922 – December 16, 2000), better known by the [[ring name]] '''Blue Demon''' (''Demonio Azul'' in [[Spanish language|Spanish]]), was a Mexican film [[actor]] and [[professional wrestler]]. Blue Demon is considered a legend of [[professional wrestling in Mexico]], partially from starring in a series of ''[[Lucha films]]'' between 1961 and 1979, often alongside in-ring rival [[El Santo]]. His in-ring career began in 1948 and stretched for 41 years until his retirement in 1989. Throughout his career Muñoz never lost a ''[[Lucha de Apuestas]]'' match and retired without exposing his face to the public; he would later be buried in his signature blue and silver mask. In his 41-year career he won the [[NWA World Welterweight Championship]] twice, the [[Mexican National Welterweight Championship]] three times and the [[Mexican National Tag Team Championship]] with long time tag team partner [[Black Shadow (wrestler)|Black Shadow]]. He also won the hair of [[Cavernario Galindo]] and the masks of Espectro II, Matemático, and most notably, the mask of [[Rayo de Jalisco Sr.|Rayo de Jalisco]]. Near the end of his career Muñoz introduced [[Blue Demon Jr.]] to the wrestling world, who despite being promoted as the son of Blue Demon, did not actually share a blood connection to Muñoz; he was later claimed to be the "adopted son". Muñoz's actual son owns the trademarks to the name "Blue Demon", while Blue Demon Jr. owns the trademark to the "Blue Demon Jr." name. [[Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre]] (CMLL) honors the legacy of Blue Demon by holding the ''[[Leyenda de Azul]]'' ("The Blue Legend") tournament at irregular intervals. He was chosen for the [[Wrestling Observer Newsletter Hall of Fame]] by Dave Meltzer in 1996 as part of the inaugural HOF selection. ==Early life== {{Professional wrestling sidebar}}Alejandro Muñoz Moreno was born October 12, 1922, in [[García, Nuevo León]], Mexico.{{cite book | author= Madigan, Dan | title= Mondo Lucha a Go Go: the bizarre& honorable world of wild Mexican wrestling | publisher= HarperCollins Publishers | year= 2007 | chapter = Los Enmascarados (the masked men): El Demonio Azul (the Blue Demon) | pages = 79–90| isbn=978-0-06-085583-3}} He was the child of farmers and was the fifth of twelve children. At a young age, Alejandro dropped out of school and moved to [[Monterrey]], where his uncle gave him a job working on the [[Ferrocarriles Nacionales de México|National Railroad]]. His co-workers gave him the nickname 'Manotas', referring to his large, powerful hands.{{cite book|author=Harris M. Lentz III|title=Obituaries in the Performing Arts, 2000: Film, Television, Radio, Theatre, Dance, Music, Cartoons and Pop Culture|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9XjGCwAAQBAJ&pg=PA28|date=June 1, 2001|publisher=McFarland|isbn=978-0-7864-1024-8|pages=28}} ==Professional wrestling career== A chance meeting with the famous Mexican wrestler [[Rolando Vera (wrestler)|Rolando Vera]] piqued his interest in [[Lucha Libre]], Vera even offering to tutor him and help him start a career. He began wrestling without a mask in [[Laredo, Texas]]. His first match was against Chema Lopez on March 12, 1948. Adopting the mask and persona of The Blue Demon, he headed back to Mexico to start a full-time in-ring career. His first appearance as The Blue Demon was in [[Mexico City]] in September 1948, where he fought Benny Arcilla. Blue Demon began his career in the ring as a [[Heel (professional wrestling)|rudo]] (a bad guy).{{cite book | author= Various | title= Lucha Libre: Masked Superstars of Mexican Wrestling | publisher= Distributed Art Publishers, Inc. | year= 2005 | chapter = El Demonio Azul / Blue Demon | pages = 162–186| isbn=968-6842-48-9}} {{cite news | author = L.L. Staff | title = Lucha Libre: Conoce la historia de las leyendas de cuadrilátero | work = Blue Demon (1922 - 2000) | location = [[Mexico]] | id = Grandes Figuras de la Lucha Libre | page = 11 | year = 2008|language = es}} From there, he formed a tag team with another masked [[Lucha libre|luchador]] named The Black Shadow, and the two became known as ''Los Hermanos Shadow'' (The Shadow Brothers). In 1952, the famous wrestler [[El Santo]] beat and unmasked [[Black Shadow (wrestler)|Black Shadow]] in the ring, which triggered Blue's decision to become a [[Face (professional wrestling)|técnico]] (a good guy) in the ring, and a legendary feud between Blue Demon and El Santo was started. The storyline feud between the two culminated with Blue Demon defeating El Santo in a well-publicized series of matches in 1952 and 1953. In 1953, Blue won the [[NWA World Welterweight Championship]] from Santo, and held it until 1958. Their rivalry never entirely abated in later years (although they co-starred in a number of Mexican horror films) since Santo always remembered his defeat at the Blue Demon's hands. During the 1960s, one of Blue Demon's rivals was el Rayo de Jalisco. In 1988, the year he retired, Blue Demon defeated Jalisco in a [[Professional wrestling match types#Luchas de apuestas|mask vs. mask match]], taking the mask of another of Mexico's wrestling legends.John F. Molinaro, ''The Top 100 Pro Wrestlers of All Time'', (Winding Stair Press: 2002), page 195.{{cite news | author = Enciclopedia staff | title = Enciclopedia de las Mascaras | work = Rayo de Jalisco | location = [[Mexico]] | id = Tomo IV | page = 6 | date = October 2007| language = es}} Blue Demon retired from the ring in 1989, aged 67, at the [[Monterrey Arena]], where he appeared in a final match, teaming up with his adoptive son, [[Blue Demon Jr.]] ==Acting career== Blue Demon first appeared in cameos in a couple of [[lucha film|luchador films]] released in 1961–1962, "The Killers of Lucha Libre" and "Fury in the Ring", in which he was one of several wrestlers more or less in the background. But in 1964, Enrique Vergara, the producer of the then-successful Santo movies, decided to diversify by allowing the 42-year-old Blue Demon to star in a series of luchador films of his own. The plots of the Blue Demon films are thought to be extremely similar to those of Santo's films. Santo was asking for a salary increase at the time and Vergara wanted to cultivate a second movie star.{{cite book|author=Robert Cotter|title=The Mexican Masked Wrestler and Monster Filmography|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=C7rwCQAAQBAJ&pg=PA96|date=April 21, 2008|publisher=McFarland|isbn=978-1-4766-0419-0|pages=96}}{{cite book|author=Doyle Greene|title=Mexploitation Cinema: A Critical History of Mexican Vampire, Wrestler, Ape-Man and Similar Films, 1957–1977|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ci1zBgAAQBAJ&pg=PA86|date=May 29, 2012|publisher=McFarland|isbn=978-1-4766-0072-7|pages=85–86}} From 1964 to 1979, Blue Demon starred in a total of 25 action/horror/science fiction films. Of those 25 films, Santo co-starred with him in nine of them. In three of his films, Blue Demon starred as the leader of a squadron of masked superheroes known as ''Los Campeones Justicieros'' (The Champions of Justice). Membership in the Champions included such legendary Mexican wrestling figures as Blue Demon, [[Mil Máscaras]], [[Tinieblas]], [[Rayo de Jalisco]], [[El Médico Asesino]], El Fantasma Blanco, El Avispon Escarlata and Superzan. In 1989, Blue Demon was the subject of a feature-length Mexican documentary entitled ''Blue Demon, the Champion'' (1989). ==Death== Muñoz died just before noon on Saturday, December 16, 2000.{{cite web|url=http://www.canoe.com/SlamWrestlingInternational/mexico_timeline-can.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20021117013853/http://www.canoe.com/SlamWrestlingInternational/mexico_timeline-can.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 17, 2002|title=SLAM! Wrestling International -- 2000: The Year-In-Review Mexico|access-date=August 11, 2017|work=[[Canoe.com]]}} He suffered a fatal [[myocardial infarction|heart attack]] on a park bench near a subway kiosk while on his way home from his regular morning training session at The ''Blue Demon Instituto Atletico'', where he was teaching others his fighting skills. Although an attempt was made to get him to a hospital, he was unable to be revived. He was 78 years old. Blue Demon was buried wearing his trademark blue mask, which was never removed in public as he always kept his true identity a secret. ==Legacy== Blue Demon is considered one of the biggest legends of ''lucha libre'' second only to El Santo in terms of popularity and influence both in and outside of Mexico. The distinctive blue and silver mask of Blue Demon and Blue Demon Jr. is known worldwide and is an instantly recognizable symbol of Lucha Libre. On Wikipedia, The mask icon is used as part of some professional wrestling related tags and notices.{{efn|Displayed above is the Wikipedia Icon featuring Blue Demon's mask.}} On October 27, 2000, CMLL held their first ever ''[[Leyenda de Azul]]'' ("The Blue Legend") tournament in honor of Blue Demon.{{cite web | url=http://www.prowrestlinghistory.com/supercards/mexico/emll/blue.html#2000 | title= Leyenda de Azul 2000 | date= October 27, 2000 | access-date= June 11, 2010 | publisher= ProWrestlingHistory.com}}{{cite news | author = Box y Lucha staff | title = 2000 Especial! | work = Box y Lucha Magazine | pages= 2–20 | id = issue 2488 | date = January 9, 2001 | language = es}} The winner of the tournament receives a championship belt that features Blue Demon as well as a plaque with a Blue Demon mask on it. The tournament has been held on a semi-regular basis ever since, The tournament was first endorsed by Blue Demon Jr., and later endorsed by Muñoz' son. Alfredo Muñoz, after Blue Demon Jr. stopped working for CMLL.From Copa In 2002, Blue Demon was ranked at 28 of the greatest professional wrestler of all time in the book ''The Top 100 Wrestlers of All Time'' by John Molinaro, edited by [[Dave Meltzer]] and [[Jeff Marek]].{{Cite book|last=Molinaro|first=John|year=2003|title=The Top 100 Wrestlers of All Time|publisher=Winding Stair Press |isbn=1-55366-305-5}} Starting in November 2015 [[Televisa]] and [[Sony Pictures Television]] began airing the first season of the [[Blue Demon (TV series)|Blue Demon]] [[television series]] featuring a fictionalized version of the early days of his career in the ring and personal life.{{cite web|title=Blue Demon es más que una simple historia de lucha libre|url=http://sipse.com/entretenimiento/blue-demon-serie-transmision-plataforma-blim-230992.html|website=sipse.com|date=November 18, 2016 |access-date=16 January 2017|language=es}}{{cite web|title=Aseguran que Televisa tiene que 'reciclar' locaciones por crisis (FOTOS)|url=http://mundohispanico.com/entretenimiento/aseguran-que-televisa-tiene-que-reciclar-locaciones-por-crisis-fotos|website=mundohispanico.com|access-date=16 January 2017|language=es|archive-date=December 18, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161218131514/http://mundohispanico.com/entretenimiento/aseguran-que-televisa-tiene-que-reciclar-locaciones-por-crisis-fotos|url-status=dead}} The third season of the series debuted on April 14, 2017, bringing the episode count to 65.{{cite web|title=¡Cada vez falta menos! [[El Satánico]] |debut = {{dts|1995|10|18}} |retired = }} '''Renato Ruíz Cortes''' (born May 9, 1977), better known by his [[ring name]] '''Averno''' ([[English language|English]]: "[[Hades|Hell]]"), is a Mexican [[Professional wrestling|professional wrestler]]. He is signed to [[Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre]] (CMLL), where is a member of the ''[[Los Infernales]]'' stable and the current [[NWA World Historic Light Heavyweight Championship|NWA World Historic Light Heavyweight Champion]] in his first reign. He debuted for CMLL in 1995 as '''Rencor Latino''' ("Latin Hostility"), but did not achieve any significant success until adopting the ring name Averno in 2001 and joining ''Los Infernales''. A founding member of [[Los Hijos del Infierno|''Los Hijos del Averno'']] alongside [[Mephisto (wrestler)|Mephisto]] and [[Ephesto]], Averno was a one-time [[CMLL World Middleweight Championship|CMLL World Middleweight Champion]], [[NWA World Middleweight Championship|NWA World Middleweight Champion]], [[NWA World Historic Middleweight Championship|NWA World Historic Middleweight Champion]], [[Mexican National Welterweight Championship|Mexican National Welterweight Champion]] and [[Mexican National Trios Championship|Mexican National Trios Champion]], [[List of CMLL World Trios Champions|two-time]] [[CMLL World Trios Championship|CMLL World Trios Champion]], and [[List of CMLL World Tag Team Champions|three-time]] [[CMLL World Tag Team Championship|CMLL World Tag Team Champion]]. Ruíz left CMLL in April 2014 and joined rival promotion [[Lucha Libre AAA Worldwide]] (AAA) the following month, where he was a one-time [[AAA World Tag Team Championship|AAA World Tag Team Champion]] and [[AAA World Trios Championship#Title history|three-time]] [[AAA World Trios Championship|AAA World Trios Champion]]. He left AAA in early 2021 and returned to CMLL that same year, where he has since won the [[CMLL World Light Heavyweight Championship]] and the 2023 ''[[CMLL Torneo Nacional de Parejas Increíbles|Torneo Nacional de Parejas Increíbles]]'' with [[Místico]]. Averno has also wrestled for [[Total Nonstop Action Wrestling]] (TNA), where he won the [[2008 TNA World X Cup Tournament|2008 World X Cup]] as part of [[Team Mexico]], [[New Japan Pro-Wrestling]] (NJPW) and [[Major League Wrestling]] (MLW). ==Personal life== Renato Ruíz Cortes was born on May 9, 1977, in [[Mexico City]].{{Cite web|title=Rudos – Averno|url=http://www.fuegoenelring.com/wrestlers_full_rudo.php?wrestlers_id=59|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110711054029/http://www.fuegoenelring.com/wrestlers_full_rudo.php?wrestlers_id=59|archive-date=July 11, 2011|access-date=October 17, 2009|website=Fuego en el Ring|language=es}} The son of [[Professional wrestling|professional wrestler]] Rodolfo Ruíz, he began training for a professional wrestling career under his father, who by then had retired from in-ring competition and worked as a referee and trainer,{{Cite web|last=Rolando Marrón Vélez|first=Jorge|date=September 7, 2025|title=Muere Rodolfo Ruiz, histórico luchador y réferi del CMLL; padre de Averno y parte de una dinastía legendaria|url=https://www.clarosports.com/lucha-libre/fallece-rodolfo-ruiz-historico-luchador-y-referi-del-cmll-padre-de-averno-y-parte-de-una-dinastia-legendaria/|access-date=September 29, 2026|website=[[Claro Sports]]|language=es}} as well as [[El Satánico]], Felipe Ham Lee and [[Shadito Cruz]]. However, his father did not want him to become a wrestler and suggested he focus on his studies, intentionally making their training sessions brutal as a result; Ruíz recalled leaving the gym in tears two or three times.{{Cite web|last=Mojica|first=Rodrigo|date=November 9, 2022|title='Mi papá me cargaba la mano, me hacía llorar'; Averno la sufrió en su formación|url=https://www.mediotiempo.com/lucha-libre/cmll/averno-revela-su-padre-fue-duro-entrenamientos-ser-luchador-sin-mascaras|access-date=September 29, 2026|website=MedioTiempo|language=es}} == Professional wrestling career == === Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre (1995–2014) === ==== Rencor Latino (1995–2001) ==== Ruíz made his in-ring debut on October 18, 1995, teaming with his father in a loss to [[Cassandro]] and Guerrero Star. Using the [[ring name]] Rencor Latino ("Latin Hostility"), he started out as a [[Face (professional wrestling)|''técnico'']] (good guy) in the lower ranks of [[Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre]] (CMLL), eventually winning his first ''[[Lucha de Apuestas]]'' ("bet match") on June 19, 1998, by unmasking Apolo Chino following a midcard [[feud (professional wrestling)|feud]].{{cite news|title=Enciclopedia de las Mascaras|work=Rencor Latino|location=[[Mexico City]], [[Mexico]]|id=Tomo IV|pages=16|date=October 2007|language=es}} On February 27, 1999, he lost to Masato Yakushiji in a match to determine the inaugural [[CMLL World Lightweight Championship|CMLL Japan Super Lightweight Champion]].{{Cite book|last=Will|first=Gary|title=Wrestling Title Histories|last2=Duncan|first2=Royal|publisher=Archeus Communications|year=2000|isbn=0-9698161-5-4|page=388}} At the [[CMLL 66th Anniversary Show]] on September 24, Latino, [[Violencia]] and [[Virus (wrestler)|Virus]] lost to [[Starman (wrestler)|Starman]], Super Astro and [[Tony Rivera]].{{Cite web|date=September 24, 1999|title=66th Anniversary Show|url=https://www.prowrestlinghistory.com/supercards/mexico/emll/anniversary75.html#66|access-date=September 19, 2008|publisher=ProWrestlingHistory.com}} On August 4, 2000, at the ''[[Entre Torre Infernal]]'' ("In the Infernal Tower") [[pay-per-view]], Latino defeated veteran [[Arturo Beristain|El Hijo del Gladiador]] in a ''Lucha de Apuestas'' to win his mask after being the final two wrestlers in a ''[[torneo cibernetico]]''. In early 2001, he underwent minor surgery on his left hand, but did not miss a significant amount of time out of the ring.{{Cite magazine|last=Spillane|first=Mike|date=February 2001|title=The Mexico Report|magazine=[[Pro Wrestling Illustrated]]|publisher=London Publishing Co.|page=91|issue=157|issn=1043-7576}} At [[Juicio Final (2001)|''Juicio Final'']] ("Final Judgement") on March 30, he, [[Arkangel de la Muerte]] and [[Veneno (wrestler)|Veneno]] lost to [[Mephisto (wrestler)|Astro Rey Jr.]], [[El Felino]] and [[Pantera (wrestler)|Pantera]].{{Cite web|last=Johnson|first=Mike|date=March 30, 2026|title=3/30 this day in history: Ric Flair loses retirement match at WrestleMania 24, WWF completes WCW purchase and more|url=https://www.pwinsider.com/article/92706/330-this-day-in-history-ric-flair-loses-retirement-match-at-wrestlemania-24-wwf-completes-wcw-purchase-and-more.html?p=1|access-date=September 30, 2026|website=Pro Wrestling Insider}} ==== ''Los Infernales'' (2001–2006) ==== {{main|Los Infernales}} [[File:Averno-CMLL.jpg|thumb|Ruíz wearing a half Averno/half Rencor Latino mask in 2005|317x317px]] In the summer of 2001, [[El Satánico]], who was feuding with former ''[[Los Infernales]]'' ("The Infernals") stablemates [[Último Guerrero]], [[Rey Bucanero]] and [[Toscano (wrestler)|Tarzan Boy]], recruited him to be a part of the new incarnation of ''Los Infernales'' and feud with the splinter group. During a televised segment, Satánico used his supposed "satanic powers" to turn Latino into one of his "minions", a [[Heel (professional wrestling)|''rúdo'']] (bad guy) character known as "Averno" ("Hell"), and Astro Rey Jr. into Mephisto. Ruíz' previous identity was publicly acknowledged, as he occasionally wrestled wearing a special half Averno and Rencor Latino mask.{{cite news|author=Enciclopedia staff|title=Enciclopedia de las Mascaras|work=Averno|location=[[Mexico City|Mexico City, Mexico]]|id=Tomo I|page=12|date=July 2007|language=es}}{{Cite news|date=January 13, 2002|title=2001 Especial!|work=[[Box y Lucha]]|pages=2–28|language=es|issue=2540}} When Tarzan Boy was injured and unable to wrestle, Bucanero and Guerrero recruited [[Antonio Gómez Medina|Máscara Mágica]] to even the numbers. The storyline between the two factions culminated when all seven wrestlers fought in a [[steel cage match]] at the [[CMLL 68th Anniversary Show]] on September 28, where the winning side would gain the rights to the ''Los Infernales'' name.{{Cite magazine|last=Spillane|first=Mike|date=July 2001|title=The Mexico Report|magazine=[[Pro Wrestling Illustrated]]|publisher=London Publishing Co.|page=75|issue=249|issn=1043-7576}} In the end, Satánico pinned Mágica to gain the rights and his mask. On June 23, 2002, ''Los Infernales'' won the [[Mexican National Trios Championship]] from [[Olímpico]], [[Mr. Niebla]] and [[Ephesto|Safari]], which they lost to ''La Familia de Tijuana'' ([[Psicosis|Nicho el Millonario]], [[Halloween (wrestler)|Halloween]] and [[Damián 666]]) on September 27. Shortly after, Averno and Mephisto [[Glossary of professional wrestling terms#Turn|turned]] on Satánico and split from the group, venturing out on their own.{{Cite news|date=January 5, 2004|title=Número Especial - Lo mejor de la lucha libre mexicana durante el 2003|work=[[Súper Luchas]]|language=es|issue=240}} On September 3, 2004, Averno defeated [[Zumbido]] to win the vacant [[NWA World Middleweight Championship]]. On January 1, 2005, Averno lost the title to [[Místico]], from then on being positioned as his rival or [[Foil (narrative)|foil]]; their rivalry and matches received critical acclaim.{{Cite magazine|last=Spillane|first=Mike|date=October 2005|title=The International Report|magazine=[[Pro Wrestling Illustrated]]|publisher=[[Kappa Publishing Group]]|page=56|issue=300|issn=1043-7576}}{{Cite web|last=Ocampo|first=Ernesto|date=January 7, 2007|title=Místico contra Averno: Déjà vu|url=https://superluchas.com/mistico-contra-averno-deja-vu/|access-date=July 9, 2009|website=[[Súper Luchas]]|language=es}} At [[Homenaje a Dos Leyendas (2005)|''Homenaje a Dos Leyendas'']] ("Homage to Two Legends") on March 18, Averno, Mephisto and Bucanero defeated [[Atlantis (wrestler)|Atlantis]], [[Blue Panther]] and [[Negro Casas]].{{Cite news|last=Ocampo|first=Jorge|date=March 21, 2005|title=El Perro se va triunfante|work=[[Súper Luchas]]|pages=5–8|language=es|issue=101}} On April 1, Averno and Mephisto defeated Atlantis and Blue Panther to win the CMLL World Tag Team Championship. In early 2006, Averno and Mephisto retained the title twice against Místico and [[Black Warrior (wrestler)|Black Warrior]], the latter after Warrior turned on Místico.{{Cite magazine|last=Spillane|first=Mike|date=July 2006|title=The International Report|magazine=[[Pro Wrestling Illustrated]]|publisher=[[Kappa Publishing Group]]|page=128|issue=309|issn=1043-7576}}{{Cite news|date=December 23, 2006|title=Lo Mejor de la Lucha Libre Mexicana duranted el 2006|work=[[Súper Luchas]]|pages=2–6|language=es|issue=192}} Their 377-day reign ended in a loss to Místico and Casas on April 14. On September 17, Averno defeated Casas for the [[CMLL World Middleweight Championship]]. At the [[CMLL 73rd Anniversary Show]] on September 29, he, [[Alex Koslov]] and Mephisto defeated [[El Felino]], [[El Sagrado]] and [[Último Dragón]]. ==== ''Los Hijos del Averno'' (2006–2014) ==== {{main|Los Hijos del Averno}} In December, Averno, Mephisto and [[Ephesto]] formed ''[[Los Hijos del Infierno|Los Hijos del Averno]]'' ("The Sons of Hell"), initially known as ''La Triada del Terror'' ("The Trio of Terror").{{cite news|first=Arturo|last=Rosas Plata|title=Hombre sin ... When the commission declared the title vacant after a match ended in a double disqualification, the two teams fought for the vacant title on May 23,{{Cite web|date=May 7, 2008|title=Confían Averno y Mephisto en recuperar título de parejas del CMLL|url=https://www.mediotiempo.com/lucha-libre/confian-averno-mephisto-recuperar-titulo-parejas-cmll|access-date=July 9, 2009|website=MedioTiempo|language=es}} which Místico and Garza won.{{cite news|first=Arturo|last=Rosas Plata|title=Místico y Garza, de nuevo campeones|work=Ovaciones|publisher=Editorial Ovaciones, S. Pepe Mendieta | debut = {{dts|1985|7|11}} | retired = | family = [[Blue Demon]] (adoptive father) }} '''Blue Demon Jr.''' (born July 19, 1966) is a Mexican [[professional wrestler]]. He is the adopted son of the original [[Blue Demon]] and is the first Mexican and second masked wrestler to win the [[NWA World Heavyweight Championship]] thus making him a one-time [[Professional wrestling championship#World championships|world champion]]. His government name has never been officially disclosed to the public, as is often the case with masked wrestlers in Mexico where their on-stage personas are kept separate from their personal lives.{{cite book | author= Madigan, Dan | title= Mondo Lucha Libre: the bizarre & honorable world of wild Mexican wrestling | publisher= HarperCollins Publishers | year= 2007 | chapter = Okay... what is Lucha Libre?|pages=29–40|isbn=978-0-06-085583-3}} ==Professional wrestling career== ===United Wrestling Association (1984–1989)=== ===CMLL (1989–1995)=== ===Lucha Libre AAA Worldwide (1996–2001)=== In [[Lucha Libre AAA Worldwide]] (AAA) he formed the team ''Los Juniors'' with [[La Parka (AAA)|La Parka Jr.]], Mascara Sagrada Jr. and [[Perro Aguayo Jr.]] On April 18, 1999, in [[Zapopan, Jalisco]] they won the [[Mexican National Atómicos Championship]] by defeating ''Los Vatos Locos'', a team of [[Charly Manson]], May Flowers, [[Nygma (wrestler)|Nygma]] and Picudo. On September 17, 1999, in [[Mexico City|Mexico City, D.F.]] they lost the championship to ''[[Los Vipers]]'', a team of [[Histeria (wrestler)|Histeria]], [[Maniaco]], [[Mosco de la Merced II]] and [[Psicosis II]]. ===National Wrestling Alliance (2008–2010)=== [[File:El Hijo De Santo vs Blue Demon Jr.jpg|right|thumb|200 px|Blue Demon Jr. (behind, in blue costume) versus [[El Hijo del Santo]]]] On October 25, 2008, Demon Jr. became the first Mexican professional wrestler, as well as first masked luchador to win the [[NWA World Heavyweight Championship]] when he defeated champion [[Adam Pearce]]. His win was also the first time the title changed hands in [[Mexico]], although not with [[Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre|CMLL]] as would have been the case before the mid-1980s (It happened in Blue Demon Jr.'s own promotion: NWA Mexico). Pearce protested the loss with the NWA as his arm was under the bottom rope when he passed out from Blue Demon Jr's [[Boston crab#Single leg Boston crab|Single leg Boston crab]]. Blue Demon Jr. managed to hold on to the championship for 505 days before dropping it back to Pearce in a triple-threat match also involving [[Phill Shatter]] on March 14, 2010, at NWA New Beginnings.{{cite web|url=https://pwinsider.com/article/45909/new-nwa-champion-crowned.html?p=1| title=New NWA Champion crowned|access-date=2010-03-14|publisher=Pro Wrestling Insider}} ===Pro Wrestling Revolution (2010–2013)=== Demon Jr. defeated Oliver John at an NWA Mexico event at the Lucha Libre Expo in Mexico City on July 23, 2010, to capture the Pro Wrestling Revolution (PWR) Heavyweight Championship. On May 11, 2013, [[El Hijo del Santo]] and his rival, Blue Demon Jr., joined forces to win the Pro Wrestling Revolution Tag Team Championship after defeating [[Brian Cage]] and [[Derek Sanders]]{{cite web|url=https://superluchas.com/elhijodelsanto-y-bluedemonjr-son-los-nuevos-campeones-en-pareja-de-pwrrevolution/|title=¡@ElHijodelSanto y @BlueDemonjr son los Nuevos Campeones en Pareja de @PWRevolution!|first=William|last=Beltrán|date=May 12, 2013}} On September 6, 2012, Blue Demon Jr. lost the PWR World Heavyweight Championship to [[Carly Colón]] in a match that also involved [[La Parka II]]. On November 13, 2013, Blue Demon Jr. disbanded NWA Mexico and became officially affiliated with PWR.{{cite web|url=http://www.prowrestling-revolution.com/2013/11/13/pro-wrestling-revolution-welcomes-new-partner/|title=Pro Wrestling Revolution welcomes new partner|date=2013-11-13|access-date=2013-11-14|work=Pro Wrestling Revolution|archive-date=September 15, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180915225829/http://www.prowrestling-revolution.com/2013/11/13/pro-wrestling-revolution-welcomes-new-partner/|url-status=dead}} ===Lucha Underground (2014–2015)=== In August 2014, Blue Demon Jr. was announced as one of five AAA wrestlers to star in the [[El Rey (network)|El Rey]] network's new television series ''[[Lucha Underground]]''.{{cite web | url = http://www.f4wonline.com/more/more-top-stories/101-mexico/38664-el-rey-network-announces-more-details-of-aaa-lucha-libre-project | title = El Rey Network announces more details of AAA Lucha Libre project | date = August 27, 2014 | access-date = August 28, 2014 | work = [[Dave Meltzer#Wrestling Observer Newsletter|Wrestling Observer Newsletter]] | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140905015135/http://www.f4wonline.com/more/more-top-stories/101-mexico/38664-el-rey-network-announces-more-details-of-aaa-lucha-libre-project | archive-date = September 5, 2014 }} Blue Demon Jr. wrestled in the first match of the debut episode of ''Lucha Underground'' on October 29, defeating [[Chavo Guerrero Jr.]]{{cite web|last1=Peeples|first1=Jeremy|title=Lucha Underground TV report: Prince Puma (Ricochet) vs. Johnny Mundo (John Morrison)|url=http://www.f4wonline.com/more/more-top-stories/101-mexico/39646|publisher=Wrestling Observer|access-date=November 2, 2014|date=October 29, 2014}} In the LU storyline, Blue Demon Jr. was hospitalized due to vicious after-match attacks by both Mil Muertes and Chavo Guerrero Jr. following Demon's loss to Mil Muertes in the November 5 main event match. Upon his return, he attacked Chavo and later in a face-to-face meeting with Chavo blocked another attack and emerged triumphant after laying Chavo out. On July 8, 2015, Demon turned ''rudo'' attacking Texano Jr. ===Return to AAA (2013–present)=== Blue Demon Jr. returned to AAA on March 3, 2013, challenging [[El Texano Jr.]] to a match for the [[AAA Mega Championship]].{{cite web|url=https://superluchas.com/confirmado-bluedemonjr-vs-texano-jr-por-el-megacampeonato-aaa-en-rey-de-reyes-2013/|title=Confirmado: @BlueDemonjr vs. Texano Jr. por el MegaCampeonato AAA en Rey de Reyes 2013|last=Beltrán|first=William|date=March 3, 2013|access-date=March 4, 2013|work=[[Súper Luchas]]|language=es}} The match took place on March 17 at ''[[Rey de Reyes (2013)|Rey de Reyes]]'' and saw El Texano Jr. retain his title. '''Richard Durock''' (January 18, 1937 – September 17, 2009)<ref name="indiana">{{cite news |last1=Blasko |first1=Erin |title=South Bend Native, Actor Fondly Recalled |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-south-bend-tribune-dick-durock-1937/185739655/ |work=The South Bend Tribune |date=September 24, 2009 |location=South Bend, IN |page=B1 |access-date=November 27, 2025 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref><ref name="ref2" /> was an American [[actor]] and [[Double (occupation)#Stunt double|stuntman]] who appeared in over eighty films and over seven hundred television episodes. He played the [[DC Comics]] superhero, [[Swamp Thing]], in both the feature films ''[[Swamp Thing (1982 film)|Swamp Thing]]'' (1982) and ''[[The Return of Swamp Thing]]'' (1989), and the 1990–1993 [[Swamp Thing (1990 TV series)|''Swamp Thing'' TV series]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dreadcentral.com/news/33729/rob-zombie-offers-updates-on-werewolf-women-of-the-s-s-and-tyrannosaurus-rex/|title=Rob Zombie Offers Updates on Werewolf Women of the S.S. and Tyrannosaurus Rex|last=unclecreepy|date=14 May 2012|website=Dread Central}}</ref> He stood an imposing 6'6".

== Biography ==
Durock played a rival Hulk-like creature on the television series ''[[The Incredible Hulk (1978 TV series)|The Incredible Hulk]]'', in a two-part episode titled "The First".<ref>{{cite news |title=The Incredible Hulk |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/enterprise-journal-dick-durock-1937-200/185686285/ |work=Enterprise-Journal |date=March 8, 1981 |location=McComb, MS |page=31 |access-date=November 26, 2025 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Price |first1=Matthew |title=Swamp Thing Actor Relates Past Roles |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-daily-oklahoman-dick-durock-1937-20/185686082/ |work=The Daily Oklahoman |date=January 25, 2008 |location=Oklahoma City, OK |page=77 |access-date=November 26, 2025 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref> Durock also appeared in the Clint Eastwood films ''[[The Enforcer (1976 film)|The Enforcer]]'' (1976) and ''[[Any Which Way You Can]]'' (1980) as well as ''[[Doc Savage: The Man of Bronze]]'' (1975), and ''[[Falcon Crest]]'' in 1983 in the second-season finale as a henchman for The Cartel.  Durock also made a brief appearance in [[Rob Reiner]]'s film ''[[Stand by Me (film)|Stand by Me]]'' as a county fair pie-eating champion.

== Personal life ==
Durock was born in [[South Bend, Indiana]], to Serbian mother Sadie (Medich) and David Durock.<ref name="ref2">{{cite news|title=Richard Durock|publisher=South Bend Tribune|date=2009-09-24|url=http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/southbendtribune/obituary.aspx?n=richard-durock&pid=133380233|access-date=2009-09-24}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UDZpAAAAMAAJ&q=%22ANOTHER+INDIANA+SERB+MAKES+IMPRESSIVE+STRIDES+IN+TELEVISION+AND+MOTION+PICTURES%22|title=Serb World|date=17 March 1982|publisher=Neven Publishing Corporation|via=Google Books}}</ref> He resided in [[Southern California]] and appeared at [[fan convention]]s.

== Death ==
Durock died of [[pancreatic cancer]] at his home in [[Oak Park, California]] on September 17, 2009. He was a veteran of the [[United States Marine Corps]].<ref name="indiana" />

Later, she became a member of I'm Enterprise. In 1998, she debuted as a voice actress in the video game ''etude prologue -Shaking heart-'' as Tadami Saeki. From the beginning of her debut, she plays the role of a teenage girl mainly from her childhood, using her voice quality. Later, she was appointed as a juvenile character, such as [[List of Twelve Kingdoms characters#Kingdom of Tai inhabitants|Taiki]] in ''[[Twelve Kingdoms]]'' and [[Alphonse Elric]] in ''[[Fullmetal Alchemist]]'' series. She took charge of various characters. Kugimiya has also voiced several tsundere heroines, including [[List of The Familiar of Zero characters#Louise|Louise]] in ''[[The Familiar of Zero]]'' series, and [[List of Hayate the Combat Butler characters#Nagi Sanzenin|Nagi Sanzenin]] in ''[[Hayate the Combat Butler]]''. '''Mihaly''' "'''Michu'''" '''Meszaros''' ([[Hungarian language|Hungarian]]: '''Mészáros Mihály''', {{ipa|hu|ˈmeːsaːroʃ ˈmihaːj}}; 1 October 1939 – 12 June 2016)<ref name=telegraphobit/> was a Hungarian and American actor, circus performer/entertainer, and stuntman. He was {{convert|2|ft|9|in|m}} tall and weighed 25 pounds.<ref name=breezeobit/> He was best remembered as a performer with [[Ringling Bros. and Barnum & Bailey Circus]] and for his role in the [[NBC]] sitcom ''[[ALF (TV series)|ALF]]'' in 1986. He appeared in many films in the late 1980s and early 1990s and also appeared opposite [[Michael Jackson]] in a [[Pepsi]] commercial<ref name=nolaobit/> and in the [[Ozzy Osbourne]] music video for "[[No More Tears|Time After Time]]" in 1992. His last appearance was in ''Death to Cupid'' (2015).

==Biography==
===Early life===
Meszaros was born in a small village outside [[Budapest]] and was the seventh of nine siblings.<ref name=breezeobit>{{Cite news | url=https://www.dailybreeze.com/2016/06/13/michu-meszaros-33-inch-tall-circus-performer-and-actor-who-played-alf-dies-in-torrance/ | title='Michu' Meszaros, 33-inch-tall circus performer and actor who played 'Alf' dies in Torrance | first=Larry | last=Altman | work=[[Daily Breeze]] | date=June 13, 2016}}</ref> He attended a school of circus arts and performed in the circus since age nine, working two or three shows a day, five days a week.<ref name=breezeobit/> He performed in the Liebel Family Circus and toured Eastern Europe.<ref name=legacy/> However, a government agent from the [[Hungarian People's Republic]] followed him to make sure he did not [[Defection|defect]], and the government took most of his money.<ref name=breezeobit/>

===Career===
Circus producers [[Irvin Feld]] and [[Kenneth Feld]] had heard of Meszaros, and, after locating him in 1973, signed him to a contract and made arrangements to bring him to the U.S. and have him star in the [[Ringling Bros. and Barnum & Bailey Circus]] as the "smallest man in the world".<ref name=telegraphobit>{{cite news| url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/obituaries/2016/07/01/mihaly-michu-meszaros-smallest-man--obituary/ | title=Mihaly 'Michu' Meszaros, 'smallest man' – obituary |  work=[[The Daily Telegraph]] | date=1 July 2016 | url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref name=nolaobit>{{Cite web | url=https://obits.nola.com/us/obituaries/nola/name/michu-meszaros-obituary?pid=180327059 | title=Michu Meszaros Obituary | work=[[The Times-Picayune/The New Orleans Advocate]] | date=June 14, 2016 | via=[[Legacy.com]]}}</ref>

In 1980, Meszaros, along with his Hungarian guard, defected to the U.S.<ref name=breezeobit/> He became a [[resident alien]] in 1984.<ref name=breezeobit/>

As a circus performer, he performed an act with [[poodle]]s, in which the poodles, standing on their hind legs, appeared much taller than Meszaros, delighting children in the crowd.<ref name=nolaobit/>

In the Grand Spectacle performance of 1982 and 1983, Meszaros portrayed a character known as the Marshal of Marshmallow Gulch, resplendent in a well-tailored white, silver and gold costume encrusted with [[rhinestone]]s, along with a ten-gallon [[cowboy hat]] and silver [[cowboy boot]]s.<ref name=telegraphobit/>

In the 1980s, [[Hawthorne, California]], where he resided, named the shortest street in that city "Michu Lane" in his honor.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/1987/06/13/a-street-called-michu/ | title=A Street Called Michu | work=[[The Sun Sentinel]] | location=Ft. Lauderdale | date=13 June 1987 | url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref name=breezeobit/>

For the first season of the ''[[ALF (TV series)|ALF]]'' television series, in 1986, Meszaros donned a costume whenever a full-body shot was needed for scenes of the alien walking, running, or standing. However, in most cases, upper-body shots of a mechanical puppet were used instead as the costume was uncomfortable. Meszaros had no lines in the show and was let go after two years.<ref name=breezeobit/>

Meszaros became a U.S. citizen in 1990.<ref name=breezeobit/><ref name=hrobit>{{Cite news | url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/michu-meszaros-dead-alf-actor-902332/ | title=Michu Meszaros, Who Played the Alien ALF on TV, Dies at 76 | first=Mike | last=Barnes | work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] | date=June 13, 2016}}</ref>

==Death==
Meszaros died in June 2016 at Providence Little Company of Mary Medical Center in [[Torrance, California]], after a [[stroke]] at his home that left him in a coma for several days. He had overcome another stroke eight years earlier and was dealing with several health issues.<ref name=breezeobit/><ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.cnn.com/2016/06/13/entertainment/alf-actor-dies/index.html | last=Melas | first=Chloe  | title=Mihaly 'Michu' Meszaros, actor who played 'ALF,' dies at 76 | work=[[CNN]] | date=13 June 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.brainerddispatch.com/lifestyle/arts-and-entertainment/alf-actor-michu-meszaros-dies-at-76 | title='Alf' Actor Michu Meszaros Dies at 76 | agency=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] | work=[[Brainerd Dispatch]] | date=June 13, 2016}}</ref><ref name=legacy>{{Cite web | url=https://www.legacy.com/news/celebrity-deaths/notable-deaths/article/michu-meszaros-1939-2016?preview=7305531 | title=Michu Meszaros Obituary | work=[[Legacy.com]] | date=14 June 2016}}</ref>

In October 2018, his memorial service was held at the [[Dearly Departed Tours & Artifact Museum]], owned and operated by author and historian Scott Michaels. Meszaros’ remains had been inurned and on public display along with items from his life and career until the museum closed in 2021. In September 2023, a crowdfunding campaign was launched by Michaels and "Dearly Departed", in order to raise funds for a  formal, more appropriate interment.<ref>{{Cite AV media | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c_vVb9KqOKE | title=The Little Man Inside ALF is Unburied - Michael Jackson's Best Man! | date=September 7, 2023 | via=[[YouTube]]}}</ref> This was successful, and Meszaros was ultimately interred at [[Valhalla Memorial Park]] in April 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=travsd |date=2024-04-05 |title=This Friday in Hollywood: Michu Gets Memorialized |url=https://travsd.wordpress.com/2024/04/05/this-friday-in-hollywood-michu-gets-memorialized/ |access-date=2025-07-04 |website=(Travalanche) |language=en}}</ref>

{{Short description|New Zealand actor (1940–2012)}} {{Use dmy dates|date=September 2016}} {{Use Australian English|date=September 2016}} {{Infobox person |name=Jonathan Hardy |image=Jonathan Hardy.gif |birth_date={{birth date|1940|9|20|df=yes}} |birth_place=[[Wellington]], [[New Zealand]] |death_date={{death date and age|2012|7|30|1940|9|20|df=yes}} |death_place=[[Southern Highlands (New South Wales)|Southern Highlands]], [[New South Wales]], Australia |education= New Zealand Players' Drama School
[[London Academy of Music and Dramatic Art]] |occupation=Actor, writer, director |years_active = 1966–2012 |partner= David Letch }} '''Jonathan Hardy''' (20 September 1940 – 30 July 2012) was a New Zealand-Australian film and television actor, writer and director.{{Cite web|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/entertainment/news/article.cfm?c_id=1501119&objectid=10823485|title=Kiwi actor Jonathan Hardy dies aged 71|date=31 July 2012|website=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |access-date=19 August 2017}} ==Early life and education== Hardy was born in [[Wellington]], [[New Zealand]] on 20 September 1940, to cavalry officer Captain Burnby Hardy and Mary Hardy (nee Philpott). His father was killed by a sniper in [[Crete]] that same year, and his mother died when Hardy was only 19.{{Cite web |title= Jonathan Hardy: Actor, Writer |url= https://www.nzonscreen.com/profile/jonathan-hardy/biography |access-date=13 September 2025 |website= www.nzonscreen.com}} He began his training at the New Zealand Players' Drama School. He then traveled to Britain, where he studied at the [[London Academy of Music and Dramatic Art]] (LAMDA) and was a gold medal student.{{Cite web |last=Juddery |first=Mark |date=9 September 2012 |title=Versatile actor carved out a remarkable career |url=http://www.smh.com.au/comment/obituaries/versatile-actor-carved-out-a-remarkable-career-20120902-2587o.html |access-date=16 August 2017 |website=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]]}} He also spent time doing vocal study in Spain. ==Career== Hardy's acting career lasted for over 40 years, from 1966 to 2012. ===Theatre=== Hardy preferred to work on the stage. Following his studies in the UK, he attracted interest from the [[Royal Shakespeare Company]] and the [[Royal National Theatre]] where he secured contracts,{{Cite web |last=Juddery |first=Mark |date=9 September 2012 |title=Versatile actor carved out a remarkable career |url=http://www.smh.com.au/comment/obituaries/versatile-actor-carved-out-a-remarkable-career-20120902-2587o.html |access-date=16 August 2017 |website=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]]}} as well as the [[Bristol Old Vic]] and several regional theatres. He returned to his home in New Zealand in a touring production of ''[[The Comedy of Errors]]'' with the [[Royal Shakespeare Company]] in 1966, and remained to help expand the country's early theatre industry.{{cite news |date=31 July 2012 |title=ATC mourns actor Jonathan Hardy |newspaper=Voxy.co.nz |url=http://www.voxy.co.nz/entertainment/atc-mourns-actor-jonathan-hardy/5/130505 |access-date=1 August 2012}} Hardy relocated to Australia in 1972, but also returned to New Zealand regularly throughout the mid 1980s,{{cite web|url= https://thebigidea.nz/stories/tribute-jonathan-hardy |title= Tribute: Jonathan Hardy |website= www.thebigidea.nz |date= 31 July 2012}} to perform as a guest actor with [[Auckland Theatre Company]], including playing [[Willy Loman]] in a production of ''[[Death of a Salesman]]''. He headed the [[Melbourne Theatre Company|Melbourne Theatre Company’s]] youth wing for two years. In 1978 he appeared in the premiere stage production of [[Kenneth G. Ross]]'s Australian play ''[[Breaker Morant (play)|Breaker Morant]]'', presented by the [[Melbourne Theatre Company]] at the [[Melbourne Athenaeum|Athenaeum]] theatre, in [[Melbourne, Victoria, Australia]], on Thursday, 2 February 1978.{{Cite web |url=https://www.ausstage.edu.au/pages/event/5970 |title=Breaker Morant |website=[[AusStage]] |access-date=19 August 2017}} The play was subsequently adapted into a film, for which Hardy co-wrote the script, earning him a 1981 [[Academy Awards]] nomination for Best Adapted Screenplay. Hardy then became Artistic Director of Auckland's [[Mercury Theatre, Auckland|Mercury Theatre]], a role he undertook for five years. He also played [[Captain Ahab]] in ''[[Moby Dick—Rehearsed]]'' and appeared in [[Gallipoli]] saga ''Once on Chunuk Bair''. Hardy had long engagements with major theatre companies in both [[Melbourne]] and [[Sydney]]. His roles ranged from a Christmas pantomime of ''Cinderella'', [[Shakespeare]], opera and topical plays such as ''And in the End: The Life and Death of John Lennon''. In his obituary, he is quoted by [[Mark Juddery]] as saying, "The actor is in control in the theatre... so the theatre is much more an actor's medium" and "Television is not anything but an actor's image... If my image happens to fit, then I do the job. Whereas on stage you can create an illusion, on television… it's pretty cliched." ===Film=== Hardy appeared in over 20 films, guest-starred in over 26 television series, and acted in many television movies and miniseries.{{Cite web |title=Jonathan Hardy |url=https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0362682/ |access-date=16 August 2017 |website=IMDb}} His early roles included the [[BBC]] children's time travel series ''[[Mandog]]'' in 1972, and a small role in the London-set Australian comedy feature ''[[The Adventures of Barry McKenzie]]'' that same year. His film work continued with the 1976 [[Fred Schepisi]] feature ''[[The Devil's Playground (1976 film)|The Devil's Playground]]'', for which he was nominated for an [[Australian Film Institute]] award. He also starred in [[George Miller (filmmaker)|George Miller]] dystopian action classic ''[[Mad Max (film)|Mad Max]]'' in 1979, and appeared in ''[[The Sullivans]]'' TV movie spin-off ''[[The Sullivans|The John Sullivan Story]]'' that same year.{{cite web|url= https://www.nzonscreen.com/profile/jonathan-hardy/screenography |title= Jonathan Hardy Screenography |website= www.nzonscreen.com |date= 18 September 2025}} At Italy's {{ill|MystFest|it|vertical-align=sup}}, Hardy was the co-winner of Best Artistic Contribution for his role in 1982 horror film ''[[The Scarecrow (1982 film)|Scarecrow]]''. He later appeared in ''[[Mr. Reliable]]'' aka ''My Entire Life'' (1996) alongside [[Colin Friels]] and [[Jacqueline McKenzie]], and the [[Baz Luhrmann]] musical epic ''[[Moulin Rouge!]]'' (2001), in which he played the character of the 'Man in the Moon', for whom [[Plácido Domingo]] supplied the singing voice. He won a [[New Zealand film and television awards|New Zealand Film and TV Award]] in 2001, for his performance in 2000 short film ''Camping with Camus''. He then appeared in the 2003 feature ''[[Ned Kelly]]'', opposite [[Heath Ledger]] and [[Orlando Bloom]], playing 'The Great Orlando'. Hardy became best known to international audiences for providing the voice of diminutive alien ex-royal leader [[Dominar Rygel XVI]] in the science fiction series ''[[Farscape]]'' from 1999 to 2003, and its subsequent 2004 made-for-television film ''[[Farscape: The Peacekeeper Wars]]''. ''Farscape'' was filmed in [[Sydney]], Australia, but was a United States production. Although the series was unsuccessful in Australia, Hardy developed a cult following and made appearances at sci-fi conventions. Hardy's other television roles include Josef Goldman in ''Twenty Good Years'' in 1979, and the miniseries' ''[[Power Without Glory]]'' (1976) ''The Mackenzie Affair'' (1977) and ''[[Against the Wind (miniseries)|Against the Wind]]'' (1978). He made guest appearances in numerous television series including ''[[Rush (1974 TV series)|Rush]]'', ''[[Bluey (1976 TV series)|Bluey]]'', ''[[Young Ramsay]]'', ''[[The Truckies]]'', ''[[The Sullivans]]'', ''[[Prisoner (TV series)|Prisoner]]'', ''[[Under the Mountain (miniseries)|Under the Mountain]]'', ''[[Butterfly Island]]'', ''[[Rafferty's Rules]]'', ''[[G.P.]]'', ''[[Mission: Impossible (1988 TV series)|Mission: Impossible]]'', ''[[E Street (TV series)|E Street]]'', ''[[The Flying Doctors]]'', ''[[A Country Practice]]'', ''[[The Adventures of Skippy]]'', ''[[Snowy River: The McGregor Saga]]'', ''[[Fire (TV series)|Fire]]'', ''[[Medivac (TV series)|Medivac]]'', ''[[Twisted Tales (Australian TV series)|Twisted Tales]]'', ''[[All Saints (TV series)|All Saints]]'', ''[[State Coroner (TV series)|State Coroner]]'', ''[[Above the Law (TV series)|Above the Law]]'', ''[[The Secret Life of Us]]'', ''[[Stingers (TV series)|Stingers]]'', ''[[MDA (TV series)|MDA]]'' and ''Magical Tales''. Along with [[David Stevens (screenwriter)|David Stevens]] and [[Bruce Beresford]], Hardy co-wrote the screenplay for the film ''[[Breaker Morant (film)|Breaker Morant]]'', for which he received an [[Australian Film Institute]] Award (1980), and was nominated for an [[Academy Award]] (1981).{{Cite web |title=Jonathan Hardy – Awards |url=https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0362682/awards? |access-date=19 August 2017 |website=IMDb}} He also wrote and directed the movie ''[[Backstage (1988 film)|Backstage]]'', starring the [[Grammy]] nominated pop vocalist [[Laura Branigan]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0094700/ |title=Backstage (1988) |website=IMDb |access-date=19 August 2017}} His screen directing career however, failed to take off. '''Richard Steven Horvitz'''{{efn|Horvitz has occasionally been credited as Rico Bonet, Richard Stults, or Richard Wood.}} (born July 29, 1966)<ref>{{cite web | title=Horvitz, Richard Steven 1966– | website=Encyclopedia.com | date=1966-07-29 | url=https://www.encyclopedia.com/education/news-wires-white-papers-and-books/horvitz-richard-steven-1966 | access-date=2025-08-09 | archive-date=June 12, 2024 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240612202624/https://www.encyclopedia.com/education/news-wires-white-papers-and-books/horvitz-richard-steven-1966 | url-status=live }}</ref> is an American actor, comedian and voice director. He is best known for his voice work in animation and video games. His voice credits include the original [[Alpha 5 (Power Rangers)|Alpha 5]] on ''[[Mighty Morphin Power Rangers]]'', ''[[Power Rangers Zeo]]'' and ''[[Power Rangers Turbo]]'', Razputin Aquato in ''[[Psychonauts]]'', Kaos in ''[[Skylanders]]'', Billy and his father Harold in ''[[Grim & Evil]]'' and ''[[The Grim Adventures of Billy & Mandy]]'', Grey Matter in ''[[Ben 10 (2005 TV series)|Ben 10]]'', Rodney in ''[[Squirrel Boy]]'', Daggett in ''[[The Angry Beavers]]'', Zim in ''[[Invader Zim]]'', Orthopox in ''[[Destroy All Humans!]]'', the Zoni in ''[[Ratchet & Clank]]'', Bumble in ''[[Kinectimals]]'', the Space Weaver in ''[[Broken Age]]'', Kanchomé in ''[[Zatch Bell!]]'', and [[List of Hazbin Hotel and Helluva Boss characters#Moxxie|Moxxie]] in ''[[Helluva Boss]]''.

==Early life==
Horvitz was born in [[Los Angeles]], [[California]]. His father Louie, a planning engineer for [[Rocketdyne]] for over 35 years, was [[Jewish American|Jewish]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/legacyremembers/louie-horvitz-obituary?pid=183947951 | title=Louie Horvitz Obituary (1921–2017) – Legacy Remembers | website=[[Legacy.com]] | access-date=June 12, 2024 | archive-date=June 15, 2024 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240615031338/https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/legacyremembers/louie-horvitz-obituary?pid=183947951 | url-status=live }}</ref> His maternal grandfather was born in [[Cuba]], and his mother's family is from [[Mérida, Yucatán|Mérida, Mexico]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sJzACtUqM3k | title=Voice Actors React to Assumptions (@ProZD, @SarahNatochenny1 , Richard Horvitz) | website=[[YouTube]] | date=July 31, 2024 | at=33:48 | quote="I'm half Latino. [...] My mom's family was from Mérida, Mexico. And my grandfather was from Cuba." | access-date=September 26, 2024 | archive-date=September 25, 2024 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240925154850/https://www.youtube.com/watch?si=Rbxc89TIKxFF6zdm&v=sJzACtUqM3k&feature=youtu.be | url-status=live }}</ref> His older brother, [[Louis J. Horvitz]], is a television director and producer. As a child, Horvitz was inspired by [[Flip Wilson]], [[Tom Jones (singer)|Tom Jones]], and [[Don Adams]], doing impressions of them.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://lancasteronline.com/features/entertainment/richard-horvitz-voice-of-invader-zim-and-other-characters-speaking-at-zenkaikon/article_06167b64-d340-11e4-a5ff-07696390df59.html | title=Richard Horvitz, voice of Invader Zim and other characters, speaking at Zenkaikon | date=25 March 2015 | access-date=June 12, 2024 | archive-date=June 12, 2024 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240612204128/https://lancasteronline.com/features/entertainment/richard-horvitz-voice-of-invader-zim-and-other-characters-speaking-at-zenkaikon/article_06167b64-d340-11e4-a5ff-07696390df59.html | url-status=live }}</ref>

==Career==
===Acting===
[[File:Richard Horvitz JACON 2009 Orlando Florida.png|thumb|Horvitz with an autographed ''[[Invader Zim]]'' picture in May 2009]]
Horvitz first appeared in a 1976 [[Freshen Up]] gum commercial, which led to other commercial appearances and several [[hand model]]ing jobs. After a brief stint in an off-Broadway production of ''[[Oliver!]]'', he went on to make appearances on television series such as ''[[Kids Incorporated]]'' and ''[[Safe at Home (TV series)|Safe at Home]]'', and films such as ''[[Summer School (1987 film)|Summer School]]'', ''[[How I Got into College]]'', and ''[[Deadly Weapon]]''.<ref>{{cite news|title=Richard S Horvitz Filmography|url=https://www.nytimes.com/movies/person/33340/Richard-S-Horvitz/filmography|access-date=25 November 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131219175342/https://www.nytimes.com/movies/person/33340/Richard-S-Horvitz/filmography|department=Movies & TV Dept.|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=2013|archive-date=December 19, 2013}}</ref> From 1988 to 1991, he starred as Howie for two seasons in the syndicated television sitcom ''[[The Munsters Today]]''.

===Voice acting===
[[File:Richard Steven Horvitz Photo Op GalaxyCon Richmond 2020.jpg|thumb|Horvitz in 2020]]
Starting in 1993, Horvitz changed the focus of his career to voice acting, starting with the voice of Alpha 5 in the live-action series ''[[Mighty Morphin Power Rangers]]''. From there, he had several other voice roles in such animated series as ''[[The Angry Beavers]]'' (as Daggett), ''[[Invader Zim]]'' (as Zim),<ref>{{cite web|last=Bogos|first=Steven|title=Jack Black Heads Broken Age's Voice Acting Cast|url=http://www.escapistmagazine.com/news/view/127384-Jack-Black-Heads-Broken-Ages-Voice-Acting-Cast|work=Escapist magazine|access-date=25 November 2013|date=2 September 2013}}</ref> ''[[Kim Possible]]'' (as Aviarius), ''[[Dave the Barbarian]]'' (as Ned Frischman), ''[[Zatch Bell!]]'' (as Kanchomé), ''[[The Grim Adventures of Billy & Mandy]]'' (as Billy and his father Harold),<ref>{{cite web|last=Hackett|first=Keisha|title=Richard Horvitz to join Rikki Simons at Invader Zim Q&A|url=http://www.sun-sentinel.com/teenlink/fl-tl-richard-horvitz-20130703,0,3307971.story|work=Teen Link/Florida Sun-Sentinel|access-date=25 November 2013|date=July 3, 2013|archive-date=December 3, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203001308/http://www.sun-sentinel.com/teenlink/fl-tl-richard-horvitz-20130703,0,3307971.story|url-status=dead}}</ref> ''[[Ben 10 (2005 TV series)|Ben 10]]'' (as Grey Matter), ''[[Squirrel Boy]]'' (as Rodney), and ''[[Shorty McShorts' Shorts]]'' (as Dudley). He also co-wrote the ''Grim Adventures of Billy & Mandy'' episode "Keeper of the Reaper" alongside his wife Kristen Lazarian.

After his stint as Alpha 5 ended, Horvitz went on to voice a few monsters in other ''[[Power Rangers]]'' series and was also the voice of Alpha 7 in the ''[[Power Rangers Wild Force]]'' episode "Forever Red". He voiced the main characters of Raz in the ''[[Psychonauts]]'' series and Orthopox in the ''[[Destroy All Humans!]]'' series. He has also voiced various [[Non-player character|NPCs]] in ''[[EverQuest II]]'', the Berserker Darklings in ''[[The Darkness (video game)|The Darkness]]'', Bumble in ''[[Kinectimals]]'', and Kaos in ''[[Skylanders: Spyro's Adventure]]''.<ref>{{cite web|last=Williams|first=Katie|title=Double Fine shows off Broken Age's voice-acting lineup|url=http://www.pcgamer.com/2013/09/04/double-fine-shows-off-broken-ages-voice-acting-lineup/|work=[[PC Gamer]]|access-date=25 November 2013|date=4 September 2013|archive-date=August 24, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140824100033/http://www.pcgamer.com/2013/09/04/double-fine-shows-off-broken-ages-voice-acting-lineup/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Horvitz voiced Green Grapes in the [[Fruit of the Loom]] commercials and has acted on stage, including in [[Jeffrey Hatcher]]'s ''Mrs. Mannerly''.<ref>{{cite web|last=Regan|first=Tatum|title=Mrs. Mannerly (Theater Review)|url=http://www.edgeboston.com/index.php?ch=entertainment&sc=theatre&sc2=reviews&sc3=theatre_reviews&id=139024|work=Edge Boston|access-date=25 November 2013|date=Nov 20, 2012|archive-date=December 3, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203030949/http://www.edgeboston.com/index.php?ch=entertainment&sc=theatre&sc2=reviews&sc3=theatre_reviews&id=139024|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Horvitz also voices Moxxie and serves as a voice director in the adult animated web series ''[[Helluva Boss]]''. He also played the roles of Alpha 8 and Alpha 9 in the [[Netflix]] special ''[[Mighty Morphin Power Rangers: Once & Always]]'', which celebrated the 30th anniversary of the ''Power Rangers'' franchise.<ref name="Thapa screenrant">{{Cite web |last=Thapa |first=Shaurya |date=April 10, 2023 |title=Mighty Morphin Power Rangers: Once & Always Cast & Character Guide |url=https://screenrant.com/mighty-morphin-power-rangers-once-always-cast-character-guide/ |access-date=January 9, 2024 |website=ScreenRant |language=en |archive-date=April 29, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230429032453/https://screenrant.com/mighty-morphin-power-rangers-once-always-cast-character-guide/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Gomez |first=Patrick |title=Original 'Power Rangers' stars reunite for 30th anniversary Netflix special |url=https://ew.com/tv/original-power-rangers-netflix-reunion-special-first-look-exclusive-video-photos/ |date=17 January 2023 |access-date=13 March 2023 |website=EW.com |language=en |archive-date=January 17, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230117150704/https://ew.com/tv/original-power-rangers-netflix-reunion-special-first-look-exclusive-video-photos/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Horvitz speaks fluent [[Spanish language|Spanish]], though he has stated he does not perform Spanish-language voice work.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 31, 2024 |title=Voice Actors React to Assumptions (@ProZD, @SarahNatochenny1 , Richard Horvitz) |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sJzACtUqM3k& |website=[[YouTube]] |at=34:18 |quote="Even though I can speak Spanish fluently, I don't do it. I just don't read for it."}}</ref>

===Comedy===
In 2001, Horvitz was in the [[sketch comedy]] group The MoHos with [[Fred Willard]], created by Willard's wife Mary Lovell.<ref name="richardhovitz"/> He and Willard would sometimes perform on various talk shows including ''[[Jimmy Kimmel Live!]]'' and ''[[The Tonight Show with Jay Leno]]''. Horvitz also appeared in an episode of ''[[Saturday Night Live]]'' in the short segment "Bear City" and briefly appeared on ''[[Tosh.0]]''.<ref name="richardhovitz">{{Cite web|url=https://www.richardhorvitz.com/blog/my-story|title=My story|date=17 July 2019|access-date=September 13, 2020|archive-date=October 22, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191022015746/https://www.richardhorvitz.com/blog/my-story|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Horvitz married playwright and screenwriter Kristen Lazarian on February 9, 1996. They currently live in [[Los Angeles]] and have three sons.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.kristenlazarian.com/bio|title=Kristen Lazarian: Playwright/Screenwriter – BIO|access-date=May 15, 2020|archive-date=August 11, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200811025641/http://kristenlazarian.com/bio|url-status=dead}}</ref>

{{Short description|American actor and writer (born 1943)}} {{distinguish|Shaun Wallace}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=March 2026}} {{Infobox person | name = Wallace Shawn | image = Wallace Shawn Jay Kelly-37 (cropped).jpg | caption = Shawn in 2025 | other_names = | birth_name = Wallace Michael Shawn | birth_date = {{Birth date and age|1943|11|12}} | birth_place = [[New York City]], U.S. | education = [[Harvard University]] ([[Bachelor of Arts|AB]])
[[Magdalen College, Oxford]] | occupation = {{hlist|Actor|essayist|writer}} | years_active = 1965–present | notable_works = [[Wallace Shawn on screen and stage]] | partner = [[Deborah Eisenberg]] (1972–present) | father = [[William Shawn]] | relatives = [[Allen Shawn]] (brother) }} '''Wallace Michael Shawn''' (born November 12, 1943){{Cite web|last=Reeves|first=Dan|url=https://nsjonline.com/article/2025/11/famous-birthdays-this-week-nov-6-to-nov-12/|title=Famous birthdays this week: Nov. 6 to Nov. 12|work=[[North State Journal]]|date=November 6, 2025|access-date=March 3, 2026|archive-date=December 13, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251213075020/https://nsjonline.com/article/2025/11/famous-birthdays-this-week-nov-6-to-nov-12/|url-status=live}} is an American actor, essayist, and writer. He is known for playing Vizzini in ''[[The Princess Bride]]'' (1987), Mr. Hall in ''[[Clueless]]'' (1995), and Dr. John Sturgis in ''[[Young Sheldon]]'' (2017–2024), and for voicing [[List of Toy Story characters#Rex|Rex the Dinosaur]] in the [[Toy Story (franchise)|''Toy Story'' franchise]] (1995–2026). Shawn also appeared in ''[[The Bostonians (film)|The Bostonians]]'' (1984), ''[[Prick Up Your Ears]]'' (1987), ''[[Scenes from the Class Struggle in Beverly Hills]]'' (1989), ''[[Vanya on 42nd Street]]'' (1994), ''[[The Haunted Mansion (2003 film)|The Haunted Mansion]]'' (2003), ''[[The Incredibles]]'' (2004), ''[[Southland Tales]]'' (2006), ''[[The Double (2013 film)|The Double]]'' (2013), and ''[[Marriage Story]]'' (2019). He appeared in six [[Woody Allen]] films including ''[[Manhattan (1979 film)|Manhattan]]'' (1979), ''[[Radio Days]]'' (1987), and ''[[Rifkin's Festival]]'' (2020). His television work includes recurring roles as Arnie Ross in ''Taxi'' (1978-1983), Jeff Engels in ''[[The Cosby Show]]'' (1987–1991), [[Grand Nagus Zek]] in ''[[Star Trek: Deep Space Nine]]'' (1993–1999), Cyrus Rose in ''[[Gossip Girl]]'' (2008–2012), and Father Frank Ignatius in ''[[Evil (American TV series)|Evil]]'' (2022–2024). Shawn is also a playwright; his plays include the [[Obie Award]]–winning ''[[Aunt Dan and Lemon]]'' (1985), ''[[The Designated Mourner]]'' (1996), ''Grasses of a Thousand Colors'' (2008), and ''[[What We Did Before Our Moth Days]]'' (2026). With [[Andre Gregory]], he wrote and starred in the 1981 drama ''[[My Dinner with Andre]]''. He played the title role in ''[[A Master Builder]]'' (2013), a film adaptation of [[Henrik Ibsen]]'s [[The Master Builder|1892 play]].{{cite web|url=http://archrecord.construction.com/news/2014/08/140801-Film-Review-A-Master-Builder.asp|title=Film Review: A Master Builder|last=Ciampaglia|first=Dante A.|date=August 1, 2014|work=[[Architectural Record]]|access-date=November 12, 2014|archive-date=September 25, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150925111838/http://archrecord.construction.com/news/2014/08/140801-Film-Review-A-Master-Builder.asp|url-status=dead}} [[Haymarket Books]] published his books ''Essays'' (2009) and ''Night Thoughts'' (2017). ==Early life and education== Shawn was born in New York City to a [[Jews|Jewish]] family.{{cite magazine|last1=Orel|first1=Gwen|url=http://tabletmag.com/jewish-arts-and-culture/15038/bag-of-tricks|title=Bag of Tricks|magazine=Tablet Magazine|date=September 3, 2009|access-date=March 28, 2015|archive-date=April 25, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180425032154/http://www.tabletmag.com/jewish-arts-and-culture/15038/bag-of-tricks|url-status=live}}{{cite news|last1=Nathan|first1=John|date=7 April 2009|title=Interview: Wallace Shawn. He makes Woody look pretty, but he's a pop culture icon|work=The Jewish Chronicle|url=https://www.thejc.com/life/interview-wallace-shawn-rr3dduu8|access-date=2 November 2020|archive-date=October 22, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231022060614/https://www.thejc.com/culture/interviews/interview-wallace-shawn-1.8709|url-status=live}}{{cite web |author1=((Jewish United Fund)) |author1-link=Jewish United Fund |date=2016 |title=Celebrities: Wallace Shawn |url=https://www.juf.org/celebrities/celebrity.aspx?id=10902 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191106101400/https://www.juf.org/celebrities/celebrity.aspx?id=10902 |archive-date=6 November 2019 |website=[[Jewish United Fund]]}}{{cite web|url=http://jewishvoiceforpeace.org/content/advisory-board|title=Councils, Staff and Board of Jewish Voice for Peace|work=Jewish Voice for Peace|access-date=December 22, 2017|archive-date=July 24, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110724050918/http://jewishvoiceforpeace.org/content/advisory-board|url-status=dead}} His parents were journalist Cecille (née Lyon) and [[William Shawn]], the longtime editor of ''[[The New Yorker]]''.
