Shawn grew up on [[Manhattan]]'s [[Upper East Side]].{{cite web| url=https://www.harvardmagazine.com/2011/02/famous-comedian-dangerous-playwright#:~:text=He%20grew%20up%20on%20Manhattan%27s,have%20collaborated%20on%20an%20opera| title=Profile of actor and playwright Wallace Shawn | Harvard Magazine| date=February 22, 2011| access-date=May 12, 2024| archive-date=August 7, 2024| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240807193616/https://www.harvardmagazine.com/2011/02/famous-comedian-dangerous-playwright#:~:text=He%20grew%20up%20on%20Manhattan%27s,have%20collaborated%20on%20an%20opera| url-status=live}} He attended [[The Collegiate School]] on Manhattan's West Side before transferring to [[The Putney School]], a private liberal arts high school in [[Putney, Vermont]]. After high school, he studied [[history]] at [[Harvard University]], graduating in 1965 with a [[Bachelor of Arts]]. He then studied [[philosophy, politics and economics]], as well as Latin, at [[Magdalen College, Oxford]], originally intending to become a diplomat. He traveled to India as an English teacher on a [[Fulbright]] program.{{Cite news|date=23 December 2021|title=Fulbright Program Celebrates 75 Years of Impact|work=States News Service}} ==Career== {{see also|Wallace Shawn on screen and stage}} ===Playwright=== Shawn's early plays, such as ''[[Marie and Bruce]]'' (1978), portrayed emotional and sexual conflicts in an [[Theatre of the Absurd|absurdist]] style, with language both lyrical and violent. In a conversation with [[Andre Gregory]], parts of which were used to create ''[[My Dinner with Andre]]'', Shawn said these plays depicted "my interior life as a raging beast." Critical response was extremely polarized: some critics hailed Shawn as a major writer, while [[John Simon (critic)|John Simon]] called ''Marie and Bruce'' "garbage" and Shawn "one of the unsightliest actors in this city."{{cite news |url=http://theater.nytimes.com/2011/04/06/theater/reviews/in-marie-and-bruce-wallace-shawn-paints-misery-review.html |title=There's Room for Everyone Aboard a Marital Misery Tour |first=Ben |last=Brantley |date=April 5, 2011 |work=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=January 5, 2017 |archive-date=June 17, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130617040959/http://theater.nytimes.com/2011/04/06/theater/reviews/in-marie-and-bruce-wallace-shawn-paints-misery-review.html |url-status=live }} His 1977 play ''A Thought in Three Parts'' caused controversy in London when the production was investigated by a [[vice squad]] and attacked in Parliament after allegations of pornographic content.{{cite web|url=http://www.whistlerinthedark.com/productions/DanandLemon.html |title=Aunt Dan and Lemon |website=Whistler in the Dark |date=2011 |access-date=July 29, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120323133414/http://www.whistlerinthedark.com/productions/DanandLemon.html |archive-date=March 23, 2012 |url-status=usurped}} Shawn received an [[Obie Award]] for playwrighting in 1975, for ''Our Late Night''.1975 Obie Awards https://www.obieawards.com/events/1970s/year-75/ {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230609085045/https://www.obieawards.com/events/1970s/year-75/ |date=June 9, 2023 }} [[File:Wallace Shawn.jpg|left|thumb|302x302px|Shawn in 2005]] Shawn's later plays are more overtly political, drawing parallels between his characters' psychology and the behavior of governments and social classes. Among the best-known of these are ''[[Aunt Dan and Lemon]]'' (1985) and ''[[The Designated Mourner]]'' (1997). Shawn's political work has invited controversy, as he often presents the audience with several contradictory points of view. He has called ''Aunt Dan and Lemon'' a cautionary tale against [[fascism]]. Shawn's monologue ''The Fever'', originally meant to be performed for small audiences in apartments, depicts a person who becomes sick while struggling to find a morally consistent way to live when faced with injustice, and harshly criticizes the United States' record in supporting oppressive [[anti-communist]] regimes. In 1997, Shawn discussed the political nature of ''Aunt Dan and Lemon'', ''The Fever'' and ''The Designated Mourner'' in an interview in which he talked extensively about the thematic connections among them, as well as his own views on [[Marxist]], [[communist]] and [[socialist]] politics, their relevance to [[American liberalism]], and how governmental and individual responsibilities for finding solutions to the dichotomy between rich and poor in the world take hold in his characters.{{cite web|last=McGrath|first=Patrick|date=Spring 1997|title=Wallace Shawn by Patrick McGrath|url=http://bombsite.com/issues/59/articles/2063|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160406140744/http://bombmagazine.org/article/2063/|archive-date=April 6, 2016|access-date=July 29, 2014|website=Bomb Magazine}} ''Aunt Dan and Lemon'' earned Shawn his second Obie Award for playwrighting in 1986,Obie Awards [http://www.obieawards.com/events/1980s/year-86/ "1986 Winners"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180306082529/http://www.obieawards.com/events/1980s/year-86/ |date=March 6, 2018 }} and ''The Fever'' won an Obie for Best American Play in 1991.Obie Awards, [http://www.obieawards.com/events/1990s/year-91/ "1991 Winners"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180721192250/http://www.obieawards.com/events/1990s/year-91/ |date=July 21, 2018 }} Three of Shawn's plays have been adapted into films: ''The Designated Mourner'' (basically a film version of [[David Hare (dramatist)|David Hare]]'s stage production), ''Marie and Bruce'' and ''The Fever''. [[Vanessa Redgrave]] stars in ''[[The Fever (2004 film)|The Fever]]'' (2004),{{cite web |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/review-television-fever-dc-idUSN1230003820070612 |title=Redgrave laid low by HBO's heavy "Fever" |website=[[Reuters]] |date=June 12, 2007 |first=Ray |last=Richmond |access-date=January 5, 2017 |archive-date=July 21, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180721192054/https://www.reuters.com/article/review-television-fever-dc-idUSN1230003820070612 |url-status=live }} which first aired on [[HBO]] on June 13, 2007.{{Cite news |last=Kahn |first=Robert |date=2007-07-08 |title=Fast Chat: Vanessa Redgrave |work=Newsday |pages=c-3}} Shawn has also written political commentary for ''[[The Nation]]'', and in 2004 he published the one-issue-only progressive political magazine ''Final Edition'', which featured interviews with and articles by [[Jonathan Schell]], [[Noam Chomsky]], [[Mark Strand]] and [[Deborah Eisenberg]]. Shawn is credited as translator of [[Bertolt Brecht]]'s ''[[The Threepenny Opera]]'', which opened at [[Studio 54]] in [[Manhattan]] on March 25, 2006. He appeared briefly in voiceover during "Song about the Futility of Human Endeavor". He published his first nonfiction work, ''Essays'', on September 1, 2009. It is a collection of essays that express his perceptions of politics and other aspects of his life.{{Cite journal |last=Jameson |first=A.D |date=2010 |title=Wallace Shawn. Essays. |journal=The Review of Contemporary Fiction |volume=30 |issue=2 |pages=167+ |via=Gale Literature}} ===Acting=== Shawn's involvement with theater began in 1970 when he met [[Andre Gregory]], who has since directed several of his plays. As a stage actor, he has appeared mostly in his own plays and other projects with Gregory. He made his film debut in 1979, playing [[Diane Keaton]]'s ex-husband in [[Woody Allen]]'s ''[[Manhattan (1979 film)|Manhattan]]'' and an insurance agent in [[Bob Fosse]]'s ''[[All That Jazz (film)|All That Jazz]]''. His best-known film roles include Earl in ''[[Strange Invaders]]'' (1983) and Mr. Hall in ''[[Clueless]]'' (1995). After seeing his performance in ''[[My Dinner with Andre]]'' (1981), casting director Janet Hirshenson was so fond of his delivery of the word "inconceivable" that she cast him as Vizzini in ''[[The Princess Bride]]'' (1987), for whom the word is a catchphrase. Other roles include Baron Von Westphalen in ''[[Southland Tales]]'', Cyrus Rose on ''[[Gossip Girl]]'', Marty in ''[[Vegas Vacation]]'' (1997), and Ezra in ''[[The Haunted Mansion (2003 film)|The Haunted Mansion]]'' (2003).{{Cite news|last=Morris|first=Wesley|date=2007-11-16|title=Out on the edge, scavenging among 'Southland Tales|work=Boston Globe}}{{Cite news|last=Itzkoff|first=Dave|date=2008-11-17|title=Wallace Shawn on 'Gossip Girl'? It's Not Inconceivable: The Arts/Cultural Desk |work=New York Times}}{{Cite news|last=Chaney|first=Jen|date=2003-11-28|title='The Haunted Mansion' A Familiar Fun House|newspaper=Washington Post}} [[File:Wallace Shawn 2014 (cropped).jpg|thumb|288x288px|Shawn in 2014]] His rare non-comedic film roles include two collaborations with [[Andre Gregory]] and [[Louis Malle]]: the semi-autobiographical dialogue ''[[My Dinner with Andre]]'', and a combined production-and-backstage-drama of ''[[Uncle Vanya]]'' titled ''[[Vanya on 42nd Street]]''. Shawn quite often appears on television, where he has appeared in many genres and series. He has had recurring roles as the [[Grand Nagus Zek]] on ''[[Star Trek: Deep Space Nine]]'', Stuart Best on ''[[Murphy Brown]]'', Jeff Engels on ''[[The Cosby Show]]'', Dr. Howard Stiles on ''[[Crossing Jordan]]'', Arnie Ross on ''[[Taxi (TV series)|Taxi]]'', Charles Lester on both ''[[The Good Wife]]'' and ''[[The Good Fight]]'', a reprisal of his role as Mr. Hall on ''[[Clueless (TV series)|Clueless]]'' (based on the film), and Father Frank Ignatius on ''[[Evil (American TV series)|Evil]]''. He appeared in the 1985 music video for [[Chaka Khan]]'s "This Is My Night". On February 4, 2010, Shawn appeared as Alan Rubin on ''[[The Daily Show with Jon Stewart]]''. ''[[A Master Builder]]'' opened in New York City in June 2014. In 2018, he joined the cast of ''[[Young Sheldon]]'' in the recurring role of Meemaw's boyfriend and Sheldon's physics professor, Dr. John Sturgis.{{cite web|title=Wallace Shawn returns as Dr. Sturgis [[California Institute of the Arts]] | occupation = Puppeteer | years_active = 1974–present }} '''Allan Trautman''' (born May 25, 1955) is an American [[puppeteer]], best known for his work with [[The Jim Henson Company]]. ==Early life== He is originally from [[Brooklyn]], [[New York (state)|New York]]. Trautman has a B.A. in Physics and Drama from [[Arts and Sciences at Washington University in St. Louis]].{{Cite web |last=Hamilton |first=Denise |date=November 3, 1997 |title=Puppeteer Pulls Strings of His Future |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1997-nov-03-fi-49843-story.html |access-date= |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}} He later obtained an MFA in Acting from the [[California Institute of the Arts]] in 1978.{{Cite web |last=Lotze |first=Katharine |date=September 27, 2016 |title=Talking with his hands |url=https://signalscv.com/2016/09/talking-with-his-hands/ |access-date= |website=Santa Clarita Valley Signal |language=en-US}} ==Career== He had his first job as a puppeteer during college working on [[The Letter People]]. Trautman spent two summers performing at the [[Colorado Shakespeare Festival]].{{cite journal|last=Turner|first=Jerry|title=Colorado Shakespeare Festival|journal=Shakespeare Quarterly|date=Summer 1980|volume=31|issue=2|pages=249–251|jstor=2869549|doi=10.2307/2869549}}{{cite journal|last=Wickstrom|first=Gordon|title=Colorado Shakespeare Festival|journal=Shakespeare Quarterly|date=Spring 1979|volume=30|issue=2|pages=226–229|jstor=2869315|doi=10.2307/2869315}} He stayed in Los Angeles after graduation and performed with [[Sid and Marty Krofft]]. In 1985, he portrayed The Tarman, one of the lead zombies of the "Return of The Living Dead" film series, often considered one of the most iconic zombies in film. He would return to the role for two of the film's sequels in 1986 and 2005, respectively. Trautman began working with the Muppets in 1990 on ''[[Muppet*Vision 3D]]'', which played at [[Disney's Hollywood Studios]] from 1991 to 2025, and [[Disney California Adventure]] from 2001 to 2014. {{short description|Japanese-American actress (born 1966)}} {{Use American English|date=December 2022}} {{Use mdy dates|date=December 2022}} {{family name hatnote|[[Tomita]]|lang=Japanese}} {{Infobox person | name = Tamlyn Tomita | image = Andres Useche and Tamlyn Tomita (cropped).jpg | caption = Tomita in 2010 | birth_name = Tamlyn Naomi Tomita | birth_date = {{birth date and age|1966|1|27}} | birth_place = [[Okinawa (city)|Okinawa City]], [[United States Civil Administration of the Ryukyu Islands|Ryukyu Islands]] (now [[Japan]]) | education = [[University of California, Los Angeles]] | occupation = Actress | years_active = 1986–present | spouse = Daniel Blinkoff
({{abbr|m.|married}} 2021) }} '''Tamlyn Naomi Tomita''' (born January 27, 1966){{cite web |title=Tamlyn Tomita |url=https://www.tcm.com/tcmdb/person/192816%7C0/Tamlyn-Tomita/#overview |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180524050326/http://www.tcm.com/tcmdb/person/192816%7C0/Tamlyn-Tomita/#overview |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 24, 2018 |website=[[Turner Classic Movies]] |access-date=August 27, 2022}} is a Japanese-American actress. She made her screen debut as [[Kumiko (character)|Kumiko]] in ''[[The Karate Kid Part II]]'' (1986) and reprised the character for the streaming series ''[[Cobra Kai]]'' (2021). She is also well known for her role as [[The Joy Luck Club (novel)#Waverly Jong|Waverly]] in ''[[The Joy Luck Club (film)|The Joy Luck Club]]'' (1993). Additional films include ''[[Come See the Paradise]]'' (1990), ''[[Picture Bride (film)|Picture Bride]]'' (1994), ''[[Four Rooms]]'' (1995), ''[[Robot Stories]]'' (2003), ''[[The Day After Tomorrow]]'' (2004) and ''[[Gaijin 2: Love Me as I Am]]'' (2005). Tomita also has played several recurring roles on television series, including ''[[24 (TV series)|24]]'', ''[[Glee (TV series)|Glee]]'', ''[[Teen Wolf (2011 TV series)|Teen Wolf]], [[Eureka (2006 TV series)|Eureka]],'' and ''[[How to Get Away with Murder]]''. She starred on the [[Epix]] drama series ''[[Berlin Station (TV series)|Berlin Station]]'' (2016), and in 2017 began starring in the ABC medical drama ''[[The Good Doctor (American TV series)|The Good Doctor]]''. In 2020, she had a recurring role in ''[[Star Trek: Picard]]''. She also released a solo album "Sweet Surprise" exclusively in Japan. ==Early life and education== Tamlyn Tomita, a second generation Japanese-American ([[nisei]]), was born January 27, 1966,{{cite web|title=Celebrity birthdays for the week of Jan. 22-28|website=The Associated Press|date=January 17, 2023|accessdate=January 27, 2023|url=https://apnews.com/article/entertainment-country-music-tv-celebrity-birthdays-teddy-gentry-07ff63620f848616f7521abdbd6706da}} on a U.S. military base in [[Okinawa (city)|Okinawa]] and grew up in [[Los Angeles]].{{cite magazine |url=https://ew.com/article/1991/01/25/close-tamlyn-tomita/ |title=Close-up on Tamlyn Tomita -- We talk to the actress from ''Come See the Paradise'' |access-date=January 6, 2021 |last=Adato |first=Alison |date=January 25, 1991 |magazine=Entertainment Weekly }}{{cite web |url=https://youtube.com/watch?v=qGiRtLT0P00 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211212/qGiRtLT0P00| archive-date=December 12, 2021|url-status=live|title=Tamlyn Tomita Reveals Her Parents' Love Story |work=Kababayan Weekly|via=[[YouTube]] |access-date=May 10, 2020}}{{cbignore}} Her Japanese-American father was in an [[Internment of Japanese Americans|internment camp]] during [[World War II]]. He met her mother while stationed in [[Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa]] between the [[Korean War|Korean]] and [[Vietnam War]]s. Her mother was of half-[[Ryukyuan people|Native Okinawan]] and half-[[Filipinos|Filipino]] descent, born in [[Manila]] and emigrated to Okinawa after [[World War II]]. Her father became a [[LAPD]] officer upon returning to Los Angeles. Tomita graduated from [[Granada Hills High School]]{{cite magazine |url=https://news.yahoo.com/reprise-her-karate-kid-role-204635077.html |title='Good Doctor' Star Tamlyn Tomita Says "Stop Treating Me As A Woman: Treat Me As An Equal" |access-date=January 7, 2021 |last=Block |first=Jenny |date=April 23, 2018 |magazine=swaay.com }} and attended [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA), where she studied history and planned to become a history teacher.{{cite magazine |url=https://news.yahoo.com/reprise-her-karate-kid-role-204635077.html |title=To reprise her 'Karate Kid' role in 'Cobra Kai,' Tamlyn Tomita had some ground rules |access-date=January 4, 2021 |last=Yamato |first=Jen |date=January 1, 2021 |magazine=Los Angeles Times }} While a junior at UCLA, she participated in [[Nisei Week]], where she was crowned its 1984 queen.{{cite magazine |url=https://niseiweek.org/queen-court/#past-courts |title=Past Queens & Courts |access-date=January 7, 2021 |magazine=[[Nisei Week]] }}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} She and several other Japanese-American girls were asked by Helen Funai, the 1963 pageant queen, to audition for the role of Kumiko in ''[[The Karate Kid II]]''.{{cite magazine |url=https://caamedia.org/blog/2017/10/30/talking-with-tamlyn-tomita-the-actress-dishes-on-independent-cinema-and-whitewashing/ |title=Talking with Tamkyn Tomita: The Actress Dishes on Independent Cinema and Whitewashing |access-date=January 7, 2021 |date=October 30, 2017 |magazine=[[Center for Asian American Media]] }} She promised her parents that she would finish college, and then explore acting. ==Career== ===Film=== After ''[[The Karate Kid Part II]]'' (1986), Tomita had major roles in a number of [[independent movie]]s. Her biggest role was in the 1990 drama film ''[[Come See the Paradise]]''.{{cite web|url=https://ew.com/article/1991/01/25/close-tamlyn-tomita/|title=Tamlyn Tomita|work=EW.com|access-date=27 December 2014|archive-date=December 27, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141227222024/http://www.ew.com/ew/article/0,,313112,00.html|url-status=live}} In 1993, she co-starred opposite [[Ming-Na Wen]] in the [[ensemble cast]] drama ''[[The Joy Luck Club (film)|The Joy Luck Club]]'' and the next year she had a role in the 1994 independent film ''[[Picture Bride (film)|Picture Bride]]''. In 1995 Tomita appeared alongside [[Antonio Banderas]] in the [[Robert Rodriguez]]-directed segment of the [[Vignette (literature)|vignette]] [[anthology]] comedy ''[[Four Rooms]]''.{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1995/12/26/movies/film-review-hellish-guests-in-kinky-spats-in-four-rooms.html|title=FILM REVIEW;Hellish Guests in Kinky Spats in 'Four Rooms'|newspaper=The New York Times |date=26 December 1995|access-date=27 December 2014|last1=Maslin |first1=Janet }} In the 21st century, Tomita has had roles in other independent films and co-starred in several major Hollywood productions, including playing Janet Tokada in ''[[The Day After Tomorrow]]''. In 2005, she starred in the Brazilian drama film ''[[Gaijin 2: Love Me as I Am]]'' and also had a leading role in the independent film ''[[Robot Stories]]'' in 2003. She was also in ''[[Only the Brave (2006 film)|Only the Brave]]'' about the [[Japanese American]] segregated fighting unit, the [[442nd Regimental Combat Team]] of World War II, which included two other ''Karate Kid'' stars, [[Yuji Okumoto]] and [[Pat Morita]].{{cite web |url=http://konakitchen.com/meet-yuji/ |title=Meet Yuji Okumoto |access-date=2021-01-06 |publisher=konakitchen.com }} ===Television=== Tomita appeared as a character named Ming Li on the [[NBC]] daytime soap opera ''[[Santa Barbara (TV series)|Santa Barbara]]'' from May to September 1988.{{cite web|url=http://santabarbara-online.com/mingli2.htm|title=Ming Li|website=santabarbara-online.com|access-date=24 October 2017}} In 1994, she guest-starred in the first episode of season 3 of ''[[Highlander: The Series]]''. In 2008, she made her return to daytime soaps with a recurring role on ABC's ''[[General Hospital]]''.{{cite news|url=http://daytimeconfidential.com/2008/04/25/general-hospital-tamlyn-tomita-cast-as-kate-howard-rival/|title=General Hospital: Tamlyn Tomita Cast As Kate Howard Rival|work=Daytime Confidential|access-date=27 December 2014}} In 2012, she had another recurring role on NBC's ''[[Days of Our Lives]]''. From 1996 to 1997, Tomita was a regular cast member in the short-lived [[UPN]] drama series, ''[[The Burning Zone]]''. In 1993, she appeared in the pilot movie for ''[[Babylon 5]]'' as Lt. Commander Takashima, second-in-command of the titular space station, but she declined the opportunity to continue as a cast member of the subsequent series. During her career she has guest starred on shows such as ''[[Seven Days (TV series)|Seven Days]]''; ''[[Quantum Leap (1989 TV series)|Quantum Leap]]''; ''[[Living Single]]''; ''[[Murder, She Wrote]]''; ''[[Chicago Hope]]''; ''[[Will & Grace]]''; ''[[Nash Bridges]]''; ''[[The Shield]]''; ''[[Strong Medicine]]''; ''[[Stargate SG-1]]''; ''[[Stargate: Atlantis]]''; ''[[The Mentalist]]''; ''[[Private Practice (TV series)|Private Practice]]''; ''[[True Blood]]''; ''[[Zoo (American TV series)|Zoo]]''; ''[[Tour of Duty (TV series)|Tour of Duty]]''; ''[[Criminal Minds]]''; and many other dramas and comedies. She had longer term recurring roles on ''[[Crossing Jordan]]'', ''[[JAG (TV series)|JAG]]'', ''[[24 (TV series)|24]]'', ''[[Eureka (2006 TV series)|Eureka]]'', ''[[Heroes (American TV series)|Heroes]]'', ''[[Law & Order: LA|Law & Order: Los Angeles]]'', ''[[Glee (TV series)|Glee]]'', ''[[Teen Wolf (2011 TV series)|Teen Wolf]]'', ''[[Resurrection (U.S. TV series)|Resurrection]]'', ''[[How to Get Away with Murder]]'', and ''[[Chasing Life]]''. In 2016, Tomita played a series regular role on the [[Epix]] drama series ''[[Berlin Station (TV series)|Berlin Station]]''. From 2017 to 2019 she was a [[recurring character]] on the [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]] medical drama ''[[The Good Doctor (American TV series)|The Good Doctor]]''.{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2017/09/the-good-doctor-tamlyn-tomita-promoted-series-regular-abc-drama-freddie-highmore-1202174900/|title='The Good Doctor': Tamlyn Tomita Upped To Series Regular On ABC Drama|first=Denise|last=Petski|date=22 September 2017|access-date=24 October 2017}} Tomita began a recurring role as the Vulcan/Romulan hybrid Commodore Oh on the [[CBS All Access]] [[web television]] series ''[[Star Trek: Picard]]'' in 2020. In 2021, she reprised her 1980s role as [[Kumiko (character)|Kumiko]] for two episodes in Season 3 of ''[[Cobra Kai]]'', a television sequel to the ''[[The Karate Kid (franchise)|Karate Kid]]'' films.{{cite magazine |url=https://www.etonline.com/cobra-kai-tamlyn-tomita-on-returning-as-kumiko-more-than-30-years-after-karate-kid-exclusive-158658 |title='Cobra Kai': Tamlyn Tomita on Returning as Kumiko More Than 30 Years After 'Karate Kid' (Exclusive) |access-date=2021-01-07 |last=Ng |first=Phillana |date=2021-01-07 |magazine=Entertainment Tonight }}{{cite magazine |url=https://datebook.sfchronicle.com/movies-tv/tamlyn-tomita-returns-to-karate-kid-world-for-season-three-of-cobra-kai |title='Karate Kid II' kicked off Tamlyn Tomita's career. Now she's back, 34 years later, in 'Cobra Kai.' |access-date=2021-01-04 |last=Meeks |first=Karen |date=2020-12-31 |magazine=San Francisco Chronicle }} == Personal life == Tomita has been married twice. '''Richard Alan Baker''' (born December 8, 1950) is an American actor and retired [[Prosthetic makeup|special make-up effects]] creator.<ref name="filmref" /> He is mostly known for his creature designs and effects. Baker has won the [[Academy Award for Best Makeup and Hairstyling|Academy Award for Best Makeup]]<!--The award did not include hairstyling until 2012. Do not add it here as it was not called "hairstyling" at the time of Baker's nominations.--> a record seven times from a record eleven nominations, beginning with his win in the first year of the category's existence, for the 1981 [[comedy horror|horror comedy]] ''[[An American Werewolf in London]]''.<ref name="oscars">{{cite web |url=https://www.oscars.org/collection-highlights/rick-baker |title=Rick Baker |publisher=[[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] |access-date=April 24, 2018}}</ref>

==Early life==
Baker was born on December 8, 1950, in [[Binghamton, New York]], to Doris ([[maiden and married names|née]] Hamlin), a bank teller, and Ralph B. Baker, a professional artist. He and his family moved to [[Covina, California]] when he was less than one year old.<ref name="filmref">{{cite web |url=http://www.filmreference.com/film/85/Rick-Baker.html |title=Rick Baker Biography (1950-) |publisher=Film Reference}}</ref><ref name="fatman">{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aSrNG1ctTKk |title=The Legendary Rick Baker! |date=September 24, 2019 |publisher=[[YouTube]] |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211214/aSrNG1ctTKk |archive-date=December 14, 2021 |url-status=live}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

==Career==
As a teenager, Baker began creating artificial body parts in his own kitchen.{{citation needed|date=May 2012}} He also appeared briefly in the fan production ''The Night Turkey'', a one-hour, black-and-white video parody of ''[[The Night Stalker (1972 film)|The Night Stalker]]'' (1972), directed by [[William Malone (director)|William Malone]].{{citation needed|date=May 2012}} Among Baker's first professional jobs was assisting [[prosthetic makeup]] effects veteran [[Dick Smith (make-up artist)|Dick Smith]] on the 1973 film ''[[The Exorcist]]''.<ref name="oscars" /><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.latimes.com/local/obituaries/la-me-dick-smith-20140801-story.html |title=Dick Smith dies at 92; 'Exorcist' makeup man won Oscar for 'Amadeus' |last=Nelson |first=Valerie J. |date=July 31, 2014 |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |access-date=February 8, 2020}}</ref> While working on ''The Exorcist'', Baker was hired by director [[Larry Cohen]] to design and create a [[mutant]] infant for Cohen's 1974 film ''[[It's Alive (1974 film)|It's Alive]]''.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Rick Baker: The Wonder Years Part Three |last=Martin |first=R. H. |date=August 1984 |magazine=[[Fangoria]] |publisher=[[Starlog|Starlog Group, Inc.]] |issue=37 |pages=31–32 |issn=0164-2111}}</ref>

At the [[54th Academy Awards]], Baker received the inaugural [[Academy Award for Best Makeup and Hairstyling|Academy Award for Best Makeup]]<!--The award did not include hairstyling until 2012. Do not add it here as it was not called "hairstyling" at that time or for Baker's later nominations.--> for his work on ''[[An American Werewolf in London]]'' (1981).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/makeup-artist-howard-j-smit-87280/ |title=Makeup artist Howard J. Smit dies |last=Barnes |first=Mike |date=August 4, 2009 |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |access-date=August 12, 2009}}</ref> Subsequently, he has been nominated for Best Makeup ten more times, winning on seven occasions, both records in his field.  <ref name="oscars" /> His other Oscars came from ''[[Harry and the Hendersons]]'', ''[[Ed Wood (film)|Ed Wood]]'', ''[[The Nutty Professor (1996 film)|The Nutty Professor]]'', ''[[Men in Black (1997 film)|Men In Black]]'', ''[[How the Grinch Stole Christmas (2000 film)|How The Grinch Stole Christmas]]'' and ''[[The Wolfman (film)|The Wolfman]]''.<ref name=oscarwinsandnominations>{{cite web|url=https://www.widescreenings.com/list-rick-baker-oscar-nominations.html|title=List of Rick Baker Oscar nominations, wins|publisher=widescreenings.com|accessdate=January 22, 2026}}</ref> Baker was also brought in by ''An American Werewolf in London'' [[John Landis]] to the music video ''[[Michael Jackson's Thriller (music video)|Thriller]]'' (1983), where Baker created the [[werecat]] creature [[Michael Jackson]] transforms into and multiple zombies that dance alongside Jackson.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://bloody-disgusting.com/editorials/3526115/came-80s-enduring-legacy-john-landis-rick-baker-michael-jacksons-thriller/ |title=[It Came From the '80s] The Enduring Legacy of John Landis, Rick Baker, and Michael Jackson's "Thriller" |last=Navarro |first=Meagan |date=October 29, 2018 |publisher=[[Bloody Disgusting]] |access-date=October 29, 2018}}</ref>

[[File:Rick Baker at Saturn Awards (cropped).jpg|thumb|150px|Baker at the [[37th Saturn Awards]] in 2011]]

In 2008, he was awarded a [[Doctor of Humane Letters|Doctorate of Humane Letters]] from the [[Academy of Art University]] in [[San Francisco]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://newsfeed.academyart.edu/2009/10/oct-30-academy-to-preview-nova%E2%80%99s-%E2%80%9Cbecoming-human%E2%80%9D-%E2%80%94-students-modeled-recreations-of-neanderthal-physiology/ |title=Academy of Art University to Preview NOVA's "Becoming Human" — Students Modeled Recreations of Neanderthal Physiology |date=October 25, 2009 |work=academyart.edu |publisher=[[Academy of Art University]] |access-date=October 25, 2009 |archive-date=February 2, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140202234556/http://newsfeed.academyart.edu/2009/10/oct-30-academy-to-preview-nova%e2%80%99s-%e2%80%9cbecoming-human%e2%80%9d-%e2%80%94-students-modeled-recreations-of-neanderthal-physiology/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> Baker also contributes commentaries to the [[web series]] ''[[Trailers from Hell]]'' for [[Trailer (promotion)|trailers]] about horror and science fiction films.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://trailersfromhell.com/gurus/baker-rick/ |title=Rick Baker |work=[[Trailers from Hell]] |access-date=December 21, 2016}}</ref> Baker claims that his work on ''[[Harry and the Hendersons]]'' (1987) is one of his proudest achievements, for which he won his second Oscar.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://movies.about.com/od/interviews/a/rickbaker062806.htm |title=Rick Baker on CGI, Changes in the Industry |last=Murray |first=Rebecca |date=July 18, 2006 |publisher=[[Dotdash Meredith|About.com]] |access-date=September 8, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080604092051/http://movies.about.com/od/interviews/a/rickbaker062806.htm |archive-date=June 4, 2008 |url-status=dead}}</ref> On October 3, 2009, he received the [[Jack Pierce (make-up artist)|Jack Pierce]] Lifetime Achievement Award at the Chiller-Eyegore Awards.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dreadcentral.com/news/13725/dread-central-at-the-2009-chiller-eyegore-awards-and-halloween-horror-nights/ |title=Dread Central at the 2009 Chiller-Eyegore Awards and Halloween Horror Nights |last=Barton |first=Steve |date=October 3, 2009 |publisher=[[Dread Central]] |access-date=October 3, 2009}}</ref>

On November 30, 2012, Baker received the 2485th star of the [[Hollywood Walk of Fame]]. The star is located in front of the Guinness World Records Museum.<ref name="2485th">{{cite web |url=https://patch.com/california/hollywood/rick-baker-to-receive-walk-of-fame-star |title=Rick Baker to Receive Walk of Fame Star |last=Baguio |first=Lindsey |date=November 14, 2012 |publisher=Hollywood Patch |access-date=November 27, 2012}}</ref>

On May 28, 2015, Baker announced his retirement, saying: "First of all, the [[Computer-generated imagery|CG]] stuff definitely took away the animatronics part of what I do. It's also starting to take away the makeup part. The time is right, I am 64 years old, and the business is crazy right now. I like to do things right, and they wanted cheap and fast. That is not what I want to do, so I just decided it is basically time to get out. I would consider designing and consulting on something, but I don't think I will have a huge working studio anymore."<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://ew.com/article/2015/05/28/rick-baker-retires-auctions-collection/ |title=Rick Baker, special effects and make-up designer for 'Thriller,' to retire and auction off his collection |last=Dornbush |first=Jonathan |date=May 28, 2015 |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |access-date=May 28, 2015 |archive-date=May 29, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150529032807/http://www.ew.com/article/2015/05/28/rick-baker-retires-auctions-collection |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://collider.com/make-up-legend-rick-baker-is-retiring/ |title=Make-Up Legend Rick Baker Is Retiring; Cites Studios Wanting "Cheap and Fast" Over Quality |last=Chitwood |first=Adam |date=May 28, 2015 |work=[[Collider (website)|Collider]] |access-date=May 28, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.slashfilm.com/537876/rick-baker-retiring/ |title=Visual Effects Legend Rick Baker Is Retiring From Filmmaking |last=Fischer |first=Russ |date=May 28, 2015 |work=[[/Film]] |access-date=May 28, 2015}}</ref>

In 2018, when Baker's daughter Veronica was working at [[DC Comics]], he was approached by DC to design a collectible display bust. He agreed on the condition of total creative freedom; working with his long-time mold maker Rob Freitas, he created a bust of [[Joker (character)|The Joker]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Morrison |first=Matt |date=October 23, 2018 |title=Exclusive: How Rick Baker's the Joker Bust Was Crafted [Time-Lapse Video] |work=[[Screen Rant]] |url=https://screenrant.com/rick-baker-joker-bust/ |access-date=July 3, 2022}}</ref>

==Acting roles==
Baker played the [[King Kong|title role]] in the [[King Kong (1976 film)|1976 remake of ''King Kong'']]. He had initially only been hired to create an ape suit that would fill in for scenes where it was not practical to use a life-sized mechanical version of Kong that had been designed by [[Carlo Rambaldi]], but problems with Rambaldi's creation resulted in Baker playing Kong on-screen for almost all of the film.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.denofgeek.com/movies/the-struggles-of-king-kong-76/ |title=The Struggles of King Kong '76 |last=Lambie |first=Ryan |date=March 10, 2017 |work=[[Den of Geek]] |access-date=March 10, 2017}}</ref> In the [[King Kong (2005 film)|2005 remake]], he had a cameo as the pilot and gunner (with director [[Peter Jackson]]) who shot down Kong. He has also made cameo appearances in: [[Michael Jackson]]'s music video ''[[Michael Jackson's Thriller (music video)|Thriller]]'' (1983) as "Zombie Opening the Crypt"; ''[[Into the Night (1985 film)|Into the Night]]'' (1985) as a drug dealer with a business card; ''[[Men in Black II]]'' (2002) as "MIB Passport Control Agent", an MIB agent helping provide aliens with disguises; ''[[Men in Black 3]]'' (2012) as "Brain Alien"; ''[[The Wolfman (2010 film)|The Wolfman]]'' (2010) as "Gypsy Man / First Killed"; [[The Strain (TV series)|''The Strain'']] as a convenience store customer (2014, Episode 8, uncredited) and ''[[Rings (2017 film)|Rings]]'' (2017) as a flea market vendor.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000711/#actor |title="Rick Baker - Actor Filmography" |publisher=[[IMDb]] |access-date=May 3, 2017}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Baker is married; he was previously married to Elaine Melba Parkyn for ten years. He met his second wife, hairstylist Silvia Abascal, while they were both working on ''[[Into the Night (1985 film)|Into the Night]]'' (1985).<ref name="fatman" /> Baker and Abascal had their first daughter 1989 and their second in 1993.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://werewolf-news.com/2018/10/rick-bakers-daughters-rebecca-and-veronica-become-a-new-american-werewolf-her-victim-for-halloween/ |title=Rick Baker's daughters Rebecca and Veronica become a new American Werewolf & her victim for Halloween |last=Quinton |first=Angela |date=October 31, 2018 |work=Werewolf News |access-date=October 31, 2018}}</ref>

{{nihongo|Tomo|トモちゃん|Tomo-chan}}{{cite tweet|number=250614276975370240|user=Mari_navi|title=@sugitaLOV 動揺するトモちゃんペロペロ（笑）|date=September 25, 2012}}{{cite tweet|number=255291325795139586|user=Mari_navi|title=@sugitaLOV やややややめろよトモちゃん！恥ずかしいだろう！！！|date=October 8, 2012}} | agent = {{plainlist| *Myuras (1998–2001) *Atomic Monkey (2001–2020) *AGRS (2020–present){{cite web|script-title=ja:杉田智和 新会社設立 及び 同社へ所属移管のお知らせ|url=http://www.atomicmonkey.jp/jp/archives/3727|access-date=2020-04-01|date=April 2020 }} }} | website = {{URL|https://agrs.co.jp/}} }} {{Nihongo|'''Tomokazu Sugita'''|杉田 智和|Sugita Tomokazu|born October 11, 1980}} is a Japanese [[Voice acting in Japan|voice actor]] and [[author]].{{Cite web|script-title=ja:株式会社AGRS|url=https://agrs.co.jp/|website=株式会社AGRS|language=ja|access-date=2020-05-04}} He mainly plays young men and is characterized by his "deep bass voice,"{{cite book|year=2013|title=Nikkei Entertainment Anime Special Voice Actor Bible|page=107|publisher=[[Nikkei Business Publications]]|isbn=978-4-8222-7576-1}} and he often performs ad-libs and imitations.{{cite web|url=https://tower.jp/artist/321514/%E6%9D%89%E7%94%B0%E6%99%BA%E5%92%8C|script-title=ja:杉田智和詳細|work=Tower Records|access-date=2017-12-10}} He is best known for his roles as [[Gintoki Sakata]] in ''[[Gintama]]'' and [[Joseph Joestar]] in ''[[JoJo's Bizarre Adventure (TV series)|JoJo's Bizarre Adventure]].'' {{TOC limit}} ==Career== Sugita was born in [[Ranzan, Saitama]]. When he was in elementary school and watched the TV anime ''[[Dragon Quest: The Adventure of Dai]]'', he noticed that the character Hyunckel had a much lower voice than he had imagined from reading the original manga, and thought he was "still cool," but the moment he said his special move, Sugita realized that it was the same voice as Phoenix Ikki from ''[[Saint Seiya]]'' ([[Hideyuki Hori]]).{{Cite book|year=2014|title=Nikkei Entertainment! Anime Special Voice Actor Bible 2015|publisher=[[Nikkei Business Publications]]|page=48|isbn=978-4-8222-7595-2}} In junior high school, he was a member of the tennis club and served as the head of the club, while in high school, he joined the [[Shorinji Kempo]] club (1-dan).{{Cite web|url=http://www.atomicmonkey.jp/jp/amprofile/sugita.html|script-title=ja:杉田 智和=|publisher=Atomic Monkey|access-date=2013-05-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130218084240/http://www.atomicmonkey.jp/jp/amprofile/sugita.html|archive-date=2013-02-18|url-status=dead}} When he was a child, he wanted to be a temple priest, and in high school he wanted to be a home economics teacher, a confectioner, or a designer. At the time, when he thought about writing a script for a stage performance at a school event and added sound effects and background music to a recording of his own voice, his older brother heard it and suggested that he try to find a job that made use of his voice and speech, which led him to become a voice actor. While still in high school, he won the Myuras & [[Animage]] Award at the Voice Actor Spring School sponsored by the Japan Narration Actor Institute, and entered the Myuras Actors School (now the Vocal and Dance Division of the Japan Narration Actor Institute), while at the same time belonging to the Myuras entertainment agency.{{Cite web|url=https://anime.eiga.com/person/11078/|script-title=ja:杉田智和：声優情報 – アニメハック|access-date=2019-07-23}} At the age of 17, he made his voice acting debut as a gift announcement narrator for ''[[Kamen Rider (1971 TV series)|Kamen Rider]]'' on [[SKY PerfecTV!]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.tv-tokyo.co.jp/plus/anime/entry/2019/018883.html|script-title=ja:「銀魂」銀さん役の杉田智和が登場！"面白くない"過去話を告白：声優ケンユウ倶楽部|publisher=テレ東プラス|date=2019-02-04|access-date=2019-07-23}} In 1999, when he was a prep school student, he got his first regular role in an anime production with ''[[Cybuster]]'', and continued his voice acting career while studying until he graduated from university. After the dissolution of Myuras in 2001, he joined Atomic Monkey after a period of freelancing, and made his first leading role playing [[List of Chobits characters|Hideki Motosuwa]] in the anime series ''[[Chobits]]''. Sugita played the leading roles in both ''[[Gintama]]'' ([[Gintoki Sakata]]) and ''[[Haruhi Suzumiya|The Melancholy of Haruhi Suzumiya]]'' ([[Kyon]]), greatly increasing his fame. In 2009, he won the Best Actor in supporting role award at the [[3rd Seiyu Awards]].{{cite news|title=3rd Annual Seiyū Award Winners Officially Announced (Updated)|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2009-03-07/3rd-annual-seiyu-award-winners-officially-announced|website=[[Anime News Network]]|date=March 7, 2009|access-date=March 4, 2014}} In October 2013, he won the Male Voice Actor Award at the "[[Newtype]] x Machi★Asobi Anime Awards 2013", and his role in ''[[Gargantia on the Verdurous Planet]]'', Chamber K6821, also won the Mascot Character Award.{{cite web|url=https://webnewtype.com/special/animeaward/2013/|title=Newtype Anime Awards 2013|publisher=WebNewtype|access-date=2019-07-23|archive-date=July 23, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190723123758/https://webnewtype.com/special/animeaward/2013/|url-status=dead}} In 2010, he starred in a live-action film ''[[Wonderful World (2010 film)|Wonderful World]]'', alongside [[Mamoru Miyano]], [[Tomokazu Seki]], [[Rikiya Koyama]], [[Yuka Hirata]], [[Showtaro Morikubo]] and [[Daisuke Namikawa]].""{{cite news|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2009-12-08/namikawa-directs-1st-film/live-action-wonderful-world|title=Namikawa Directs 1st Film: Live-Action ''Wonderful World''|date=December 8, 2009|website=[[Anime News Network]]|access-date=January 30, 2010}} On April 1, 2020, Sugita left Atomic Monkey, the company he had been affiliated with for many years, and established AGRS Inc. with Kai Itō, a lawyer well versed in the entertainment industry, as an advisor and himself as the representative director. ==Personal life== Sugita's [[mongrel]] dog, "Naoji" ({{lang|ja|直司}}), was adopted by his father from the original owner. He has once taken a commercial for [[4gamer]] with his dog.{{cite web |script-title=ja:【杉田智和】4GamerのCM【マフィア梶田】 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NDIanP0jEMI |via=YouTube | date=May 7, 2013 |language=en}} Naoji died on 6 September 2018.{{cite web |script-title=ja:実家から直司が亡くなったとの連絡を受けました。享年17歳。彼ほど世界中に愛された雑種犬はいないと思います。ありがとうございました。|url=https://twitter.com/sugitaLOV/status/1037556719969128449 |via=Twitter |language=ja}} His favorite colors are black and silver. {{nihongo|'''Hideo Ishikawa'''|石川 英郎|Ishikawa Hideo|born December 13, 1969}} is a Japanese [[Voice acting in Japan|voice actor]] and [[narrator]] from [[Hyōgo Prefecture]], Japan. He is currently affiliated with [[Aoni Production]]. He is known for being the voice of Kicchō Fukuda in ''[[Slam Dunk (manga)|Slam Dunk]]'', [[Jūshirō Ukitake]] in ''[[Bleach (TV series)|Bleach]]'', [[Auron (Final Fantasy)|Auron]] in ''[[Final Fantasy X]]'', [[Itachi Uchiha]] in ''[[Naruto]]'', [[Squall Leonhart]] in the ''[[Final Fantasy]]'' and ''[[Kingdom Hearts]]'' series, Pierre de Chaltier in ''[[Tales of Destiny]]'', and Ryoma Nagare in ''[[Getter Robo]]'' and ''[[Super Robot Wars]]''.

{{Nihongo|'''Hiroki Takahashi'''|高橋 広樹|Takahashi Hiroki}} is a Japanese actor, [[Voice acting in Japan|voice actor]], and singer. His major roles include [[List of The Prince of Tennis characters#Eiji Kikumaru|Eiji Kikumaru]] in ''[[The Prince of Tennis]]'', Tobias in ''[[Pokémon (TV series)|Pokémon]]'', [[List of School Rumble characters#Kenji Harima|Kenji Harima]] in ''[[School Rumble]]'', [[List of Hunter × Hunter characters#Hisoka Morow|Hisoka]] in ''[[Hunter × Hunter|Hunter × Hunter (1999)]]'', [[Katsuya Jonouchi]] in ''[[Yu-Gi-Oh! Duel Monsters]]'', and Takato Saijō in ''[[Dakaichi]]''. On video games, he voiced [[Ryu (Street Fighter)|Ryu]] in the ''[[Street Fighter]]'' series.

== Personal life ==
Takahashi is married to voice actress Aiko Aihashi. Their first son was born on June 24, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/interest/2016-06-24/voice-actors-hiroki-takahashi-aiko-aihashi-welcome-baby-boy/.103550|title=Voice Actors Hiroki Takahashi, Aiko Aihashi Welcome Baby Boy|website=[[Anime News Network]]|date=June 24, 2016|access-date=March 1, 2019}}</ref>

'''Lawrence Dobkin''' (September 16, 1919 – October 28, 2002) was an American [[television director]], character actor and [[television writer|screenwriter]] whose career spanned seven decades.

Dobkin was a prolific performer during the [[Old-time radio|Golden Age of Radio]]. He narrated the western ''[[Broken Arrow (1950 film)|Broken Arrow]]'' (1950). His film performances include ''[[Never Fear]]'' (1949), ''[[Sweet Smell of Success]]'' (1957), ''[[North by Northwest]]'' (1959) and ''[[Geronimo]]'' (1962). Before the closing credits of each episode of the  landmark [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]] television network series ''[[Naked City (TV series)|Naked City]]'' (1958–1963), he said, "There are eight million stories in the naked city.  This has been one of them."<ref name="Vallance2002">{{cite news| title=Obituary: Lawrence Dobkin: Prolific and Versatile Character Actor| work=[[The Independent]]| date=October 9, 2002| author=Vallance, Tom| location=London| url=http://www.saint.org/actor-lawrence-dobkin.htm| via=Saint.org}}</ref>

== Early years ==
Dobkin was born in [[Manhattan]], New York City to a Jewish family. His parents were Samuel Dobkin (1888–1948) and Frieda ({{née}} Feder, 1890–1984).<ref>{{cite web | title=Lawrence C Dobkin - Ancestry® | website=[[Ancestry.com]] | url=https://www.ancestry.com/genealogy/records/lawrence-c-dobkin-24-57hy3v }}</ref> Dobkin served in a radio propaganda unit of the [[United States Army Air Forces|U.S. Army Air Forces]] during [[World War II]].<ref>[https://www.rusc.com/old-time-radio/Lawrence-Dobkin.aspx?t=234 Lawrence Dobkins] rusc.com. Retrieved May 13, 2023.</ref>

==Radio==
{{More citations needed section|date=June 2023}}
Dobkin understudied on [[Broadway (theatre)|Broadway]].<ref name="slst">{{cite news |last1=Kimbrough |first1=Mary |title=Understudy Makes Good On Stage And In The Army |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/21755046/lawrence_dobkin/ |newspaper=[[St. Louis Star-Times]] |date=November 1, 1943 |page=12 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date = July 10, 2018}}</ref> When he returned to network radio he was one of five actors who played the detective [[Ellery Queen]] in ''[[The Adventures of Ellery Queen (radio program)|The Adventures of Ellery Queen]]''.<ref name="opa"/> In ''[[The New Adventures of Nero Wolfe]]'' (1950–1951), Dobkin played detective [[Archie Goodwin (character)|Archie Goodwin]] opposite [[Sydney Greenstreet]]'s [[Nero Wolfe]].

While playing Louie, [[Simon Templar|"The Saint"]]'s cab-driving sidekick on [[NBC Radio]] in 1951, he was asked to step into the lead role of Simon Templar to replace [[Tom Conway]] for a single episode —  making Dobkin one of the many actors to portray [[Leslie Charteris]]' literary creation.<ref name="Saint.org">{{cite web| url=http://www.saint.org/actor-lawrence-dobkin.htm | title=Lawrence Dobkin (Larry Dobkin)| website=Saint.org| access-date=2013-06-27}}</ref>

Other radio work included ''[[Escape (radio program)|Escape]]'' (1947–1954); ''[[Gunsmoke]]'' (1952–1961); ''[[Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]]'' (1956–1960); and the anthology series ''[[Lux Radio Theater]]''. "The few of us who are left," Dobkin said of his radio days not long before he died, "keep telling each other that we never had it so good."<ref name="Vallance2002"/>

He played Lieutenant Matthews on ''[[The Adventures of Philip Marlowe]]'', along with several other characters. Continuing to work as a [[voice actor]] throughout his career, Dobkin contributed to the [[video game]] ''[[Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six: Rogue Spear]]'' (1999).

==Television==
{{More citations needed section|date=June 2023}}
Dobkin began a prolific career in television in 1946, having worked as an actor, narrator and director. In 1953, he guest-starred on [[Alan Hale, Jr.]]'s short-lived [[CBS]] espionage series set in the [[Cold War]], ''[[Biff Baker, U.S.A.]]''. He was cast in a 1957 episode of the [[Television syndication|syndicated]] series ''The Silent Service'', in "The Ordeal of the S 38", based on true stories of the [[submarine]] division of the [[United States Navy]], in which he was the lead actor and was credited incorrectly as Lawrence Bodkin. He appeared also in the religion [[anthology series]], ''[[Crossroads (1955 TV series)|Crossroads]]'', based on experiences of American [[clergy]]men, and later on the [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]] religion drama, ''[[Going My Way (TV series)|Going My Way]]'', starring [[Gene Kelly]].

In the 1950s [[situation comedy]] ''[[I Love Lucy]]'' Dobkin played the roles of "Restaurant Man" in episode 66 ("Ricky and Fred Are TV Fans"), "Waiter" in episode 70 ("Equal Rights"), and "Counterfeiter" in episode 145 ("Paris at Last").<ref name=nite>{{cite book| title=Nick at Nite's Classic TV Companion| editor-first=Tom| editor-last=Hill| year=1996| publisher=Simon & Schuster| pages=264, 266, 289| url=https://archive.org/details/nickatnitesclass00hill/page/264/mode/2up?q=Dobkin| isbn=978-0-6848-1593-0}}</ref>

In the 1957-1958 television season, Dobkin played a director on the [[CBS]] [[sitcom]], ''[[Mr. Adams and Eve]]'', starring [[Howard Duff]] and [[Ida Lupino]] as fictitious married actors residing in [[Beverly Hills, California|Beverly Hills]], [[California]]. He guest-starred in 1958 in the first season of ABC's ''[[The Donna Reed Show]]''.

In 1957, Dobkin appeared in the third episode of the first season of the CBS Television western ''[[Have Gun – Will Travel]]'',  entitled "The Great Mohave Chase",  as the owner of water rights in the small western town of Mohave.

In the May 9, 1958 episode of the CBS Television western series ''[[Trackdown (TV series)|Trackdown]]'' entitled, "The End of the World", he portrays a con man named Walter Trump who promises to save a town from destruction by building a wall.

In 1960, Dobkin appeared as Kurt Reynolds in the episode "So Dim the Light" of the CBS [[anthology series]] ''[[The DuPont Show with June Allyson]]'', and as an escape artist on the run from a possible murder charge in ''[[Wanted: Dead or Alive (TV series)|Wanted: Dead or Alive]]''. That same year he played "Esteban Garcia" (a long time friend of Marshal Dillon where things go very wrong) in the TV Western ''[[Gunsmoke]]'', in the episode "Don Matteo" (S6E7). He appeared in the [[David Janssen]] crime drama series, ''[[Richard Diamond, Private Detective]]''. Dobkin appeared in four episodes of ''[[The Rifleman]]'' playing four different characters, including a heartfelt portrayal of General [[Philip Sheridan]] from the [[American Civil War]]. He appeared in an episode of ''[[The Tab Hunter Show]]'' in 1961. In 1964 he narrated the USIS documentary film about the Republican and Democrat conventions called "1964 The Conventions."

Often also cast as a villain, Dobkin portrayed [[gangster]] [[Dutch Schultz]] on ABC's ''[[The Untouchables (1959 TV series)|The Untouchables]]''. He appeared on the ABC/[[Warner Bros.]] crime drama, ''[[The Roaring 20s (TV series)|The Roaring 20s]]'' and in the [[NBC]] western with a modern setting, ''[[Empire (1962 TV series)|Empire]]''. He was cast as a mass murderer in the 1972 pilot for ABC's ''[[The Streets of San Francisco]]'', starring [[Karl Malden]]. He guest-starred on ABC's ''[[The Big Valley]]'', starring [[Barbara Stanwyck]].<ref name="Erickson">{{cite web | url=http://www.allmovie.com/artist/lawrence-dobkin-p87920 | title=Lawrence Dobkin | publisher=All Movie | access-date=2013-06-27 | author=Erickson, Hal}}</ref> He received an [[Emmy Award]] nomination for Outstanding Performance by an Actor in a Supporting Role in a Drama for his work on the ''[[CBS Playhouse]]'' episode, ''[[Do Not Go Gentle Into That Good Night (CBS Playhouse)|Do Not Go Gentle Into That Good Night]]'' (1967).<ref>{{cite web |title=Lawrence Dobkin |url=http://www.emmys.com/awards/nominations/award-search?search_api_views_fulltext=Lawrence+Dobkin&submit=Search&field_celebrity_details_field_display_name=&field_show_details_field_nominee_show_nr_title=&field_show_details_field_network=All&field_show_details_field_production_company=All&field_nominations_year=1949-01-01+00%3A00%3A00&field_nominations_year_1=2018-01-01+00%3A00%3A00&field_award_category=All |website=Academy of Television Arts & Sciences |access-date=11 July 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160411073759/http://www.emmys.com/bios/lawrence-dobkin |archive-date=April 11, 2016}}</ref> In 1991, Dobkin appeared in an episode of the television series ''[[Night Court]]'' as State Supreme Court Justice Welch.

In the ''[[Star Trek]]'' media franchise Dobkin directed the [[Star Trek: The Original Series|original series]] episode "[[Charlie X]]", and later portrayed the traitorous [[Klingon]] ambassador Kell on ''[[Star Trek: The Next Generation]]'' in the fourth-season episode [[The Mind's Eye (Star Trek: The Next Generation)|"The Mind's Eye"]].<ref>{{cite book|title=The Star Trek Encyclopedia|first1=Michael|last1=Okuda|first2=Denise|last2=Okuda|publisher=[[Pocket Books]]|year=1994|pages=47, 152|url=https://archive.org/details/startrekencycl00okud/mode/2up?q=dobkin|isbn=978-0-6718-8684-4}}</ref>

As a writer, Dobkin created the title character for the 1974 film and the 1977–1978 NBC series ''[[The Life and Times of Grizzly Adams]]''.

He began directing for television in 1960, and his work in this area included episodes 1, 9, 10, and 13 of ''[[The Munsters]]'' (1964),<ref>{{cite book|title=Nick at Nite's Classic TV Companion|pages=358–359, 361–363|quote=The episodes are numbered in the order they were broadcast which is not the same order in which they were filmed which notes that episode 2 was actually made first}}</ref> 16 episodes of ''[[The Waltons]]'' (1972–1981), and an episode of ''[[Sara (U.S. 1976 TV series)|Sara]]'' (1976). Dobkin also guest-starred on a 1983 episode of ''[[Knight Rider]]''.

==Films==
Dobkin's notable supporting film roles include ''[[Twelve O'Clock High]]'' (1949), ''[[The Day the Earth Stood Still (1951 film)|The Day the Earth Stood Still]]'' (1951),  ''[[Julius Caesar (1953 film)|Julius Caesar]]'' (1953), ''[[The Ten Commandments (1956 film)|The Ten Commandments]]'' (1956), ''[[The Defiant Ones (film)|The Defiant Ones]]'' (1958), ''[[Johnny Yuma (film)|Johnny Yuma]]'' (1966) and ''[[Patton (film)|Patton]]'' (1970). He had a cameo appearance in the 1954 sci-fi thriller ''[[Them!|Them]]''. In an uncredited performance in Alfred Hitchcock's ''[[North by Northwest]]'', Dobkin has a memorable line as an intelligence official who remarks on the plight of the hapless protagonist, on the run for murder after being mistaken for a person who doesn't exist: "It's so horribly sad. Why is it I feel like laughing?" {{Citation needed|date=February 2013}}

==Personal life==
On June 24, 1961, Dobkin married the actress [[Joanna Barnes]];<ref>{{cite news |title=Lawrence Dobkin, Joanna Barnes Marry |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/los-angeles-evening-citizen-news-lawrenc/191123436/ |work=Los Angeles Evening Citizen News |date=June 26, 1961 |location=Hollywood, CA |page=4 |access-date=February 12, 2026 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Joanna Barnes Wed to Lawrence Dobkin |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-blade-lawrence-dobkin-1919-2002/191123503/ |work=The Blade |date=June 26, 1961 |location=Toledo, OH |page=3 |access-date=February 12, 2026 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref> they had no children,<ref>{{cite news |title=Lawrence Dobkin Wants Divorce |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-houston-post-lawrence-dobkin-1919-2/191123532/ |work=The Houston Post |date=August 21, 1966 |location=Houston, TX |page=64 |access-date=February 12, 2026 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref> but he had one daughter, Debra Dobkin, by his first wife, Frances Hope Walker. Dobkin married the actress Anne Collings in 1970 and had two children: identical twin daughters, Kristy and Kaela.{{citation needed|date=January 2021}}

==Death==
On October 28, 2002, Dobkin died of heart failure at age 83 at his Los Angeles home.<ref name="opa">{{cite book |last1=Lentz |first1=Harris M. III |title=Obituaries in the Performing Arts, 2002: Film, Television, Radio, Theatre, Dance, Music, Cartoons and Pop Culture |date=2003 |publisher=McFarland |isbn=978-0-7864-5207-1 |pages=84–85 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Z3rGCwAAQBAJ&q=%22Lawrence+Dobkin%22&pg=PA84 |access-date=July 11, 2018 |language=en}}</ref>

'''Julianna McCarthy''' is an American actress.

==Biography and career==
McCarthy began her career on the New York stage and appeared on [[Broadway theatre|Broadway]] in ''[[Inherit the Wind (play)|Inherit the Wind]]'' (1955–1957), alongside her husband, [[Michael Constantine]]. She and Constantine married on October 5, 1953; they had two children, Thea Eileen and Brendan Neil, before they divorced in 1972.<ref>Smith, Harrison. "[https://www.newspapers.com/image/766212833/ Obituaries: Actor who starred in 'My Big Fat Greek Wedding']" (obituary of Michael Constantine). London, England: ''The Independent'', September 18, 2021, p. 44 (subscription required).</ref><ref>Fox, Margalit. "[https://www.newspapers.com/image/952310556/ Michael Constantine, father in 'My Big Fat Greek Wedding']" (obituary of Michael Constantine). Buffalo, New York: ''The Buffalo News'', September 10, 2021, p. B5 (subscription required).</ref>

In 1986, she appeared on stage as the character Berte at the James A. Doolittle Theater in [[Hollywood, Los Angeles]] in the [[Mark Taper Forum]] production of ''[[Hedda Gabler]]'', which was directed by Robert Egan. Starring Egan's then-wife, [[Kate Mulgrew]], as Hedda, the production also included [[Linda Purl]] as Mrs. Elvsted.<ref>Kreiswirth, Sandra. "[https://www.newspapers.com/image/607383651/ Taper's 'Hedda Gabler' has the look, lacks the fire]." Torrance, California: ''The Daily Breeze'', June 15, 1986, p. H7 (subscription required).</ref>

McCarthy was an original cast member of the [[soap opera]] ''[[The Young and the Restless]]'', starring as matriarch [[Liz Foster]] from 1973 to 1986.<ref>"[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1092811804/ News Q&A]." Portland, Oregon: ''The Oregonian'', May 28, 2013, p. A2 (subscription required).</ref> She reprised the role in 1993, 2003–2004,<ref>"[https://www.newspapers.com/image/270695970/ Soap Chat: Familiar faces are showing up]." Orlando, Florida: ''Orlando Sentinel'', January 5, 2003, p. X6 (subscription required).</ref> and 2008, returning for her most recent appearance in June 2010. While she was taken off of contract in late fall 1982{{Citation needed |date=August 2024}} and didn't make appearances for months, she was brought back on a recurring basis in time for the show's tenth anniversary, appearing semi-regularly for the next couple of years until her character moved to London. She was seen semi-regularly during the show's 30th anniversary when an ailing Liz revealed that her daughter, Jill, had been adopted. Her storyline concerned Jill's determination to find her birth parents. The character of Liz died in June 2010 on-screen.

McCarthy has also appeared in [[film|motion pictures]] including ''[[The Last American Virgin]]'', ''[[The Distinguished Gentleman]]'', ''[[The Frighteners]]'',<ref>"The Frighteners," in "[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1064639151/ Movie of the Day]." Blackburn, Lancashire, England: ''Lancashire Telegraph'', p. M35 (subscription required).</ref> ''[[Starship Troopers (film)|Starship Troopers]]'' and ''[[Ted Bundy (film)|Ted Bundy]]''.<ref name=bfi/>

She had a recurring role as [[List of Star Trek: Deep Space Nine characters#Mila|Mila]] in ''[[Star Trek: Deep Space Nine]]'', appearing in the episodes "[[Improbable Cause (DS9 episode)|Improbable Cause]]", "[[The Dogs of War (DS9 episode)|The Dogs of War]]" and the final episode, "[[What You Leave Behind (DS9 episode)|What You Leave Behind]]". McCarthy also had recurring roles in ''[[Paradise (American TV series)|Paradise]]'' and the 1991 remake of ''[[Dark Shadows (1991 TV series)|Dark Shadows]]'' as Mrs. Johnson, the housekeeper. In the show's flashbacks, she played the role of the calculating Collins relative Abigail.<ref>Novakovich, Lila. "Have you heard," in "[https://www.newspapers.com/image/734113557/ Soap Scene]." North Bay, Ontario, Canada: ''North Bay Nugget'', February 2, 1991, p. C6 (subscription required).</ref>

'''Michael David Donovan''' (June 12, 1953 – March 4, 2026) was a Canadian voice actor and director.
== Career ==
Donovan had an extensive voiceover career in both western and Japanese animation. His voice roles include Wes Weasley in ''[[Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog]]'', [[Guile (Street Fighter)|Guile]] and [[Zangief]] in ''[[Street Fighter (TV series)|Street Fighter]]'', [[Eggplant Wizard]] in ''[[Captain N: The Game Master]]'', and [[Sabretooth (character)|Sabretooth]] in ''[[X-Men: Evolution]]''. His anime roles include [[Master Roshi]] in ''[[Dragon Ball (TV series)|Dragon Ball]]'', [[Ryoga Hibiki]] in ''[[Ranma ½]]'', and [[Cye Mouri]] and [[Sage Date]] in ''[[Ronin Warriors]]''.<ref name="Anime News Network">{{Cite web |last=Mateo |first=Alex |date=August 7, 2026 |title=SAG-AFTRA Lists Voice Actor Michael Donovan's Death |url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2026-08-07/sag-aftra-lists-voice-actor-michael-donovan-death/.240382 |access-date=August 7, 2026 |website=[[Anime News Network]] |language=en}}</ref>

== Death ==
Donovan died on March 4, 2026, at the age of 72.<ref name="SAG-AFTRA Summer 2026 issue">{{Cite web |title=Summer 2026 magazine |url=https://digital.copcomm.com/i/1546062-summer-2026/79? |access-date=August 6, 2026 |website=SAG-AFTRA}}</ref><ref name="Anime News Network" />

{{Short description|American director, voice actor, comedian and YouTuber}} {{For|the visual effects artist who also did Star Wars roles|Matt Sloan (visual effects)}} {{BLP sources|date=August 2020}} {{Use American English|date=July 2022}} {{Use mdy dates|date=July 2022}} {{Infobox person | name = Matt Sloan | image = File:Matt Sloan Circa 2013.png | image_size = | caption = Sloan in 2013 | birth_name = | birth_date = {{birth date and age|mf=y|1973|3|24}} | birth_place = | death_date = | death_place = | occupation = {{hlist|Voice actor|director|writer|businessman|YouTuber}} | years_active = 1993–present }} '''Matt Sloan''' (born March 24, 1973)"[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QR6FvEvhnJo Welcome to the Basement - Marty (and Oscars)]", timecode 22:22, March 4, 2016. is an American voice actor, director, writer, and [[YouTuber]] from [[Madison, Wisconsin|Madison]], [[Wisconsin]].{{Cite news | url-access = registration | first = David | last = Callender | title = In a City Far, Far Away From Hollywood, the YouTube Tales of a Lesser Vader | url = https://www.nytimes.com/2007/10/15/business/media/15chad.html?_r=1&ref=business&oref=slogin | work = New York Times | date = 2007-10-15 | accessdate = 2007-10-15 | archive-date = 2013-09-29 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20130929114237/http://www.nytimes.com/2007/10/15/business/media/15chad.html?_r=1&ref=business&oref=slogin | url-status = live }}{{Cite news | title = Store Wars | url = http://www.metro.co.uk/weird/article.html?in_article_id=39011 | publisher = Metro.co.uk | date = 2007-02-26 | accessdate = 2007-10-15 | archive-date = 2008-09-10 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080910094201/http://www.metro.co.uk/weird/article.html?in_article_id=39011 | url-status = live }} He and his friend [[Aaron Yonda]] are notable as the co-creators of the web series ''[[Chad Vader: Day Shift Manager]]'', in which he voices the title character. Additionally, he appears in season one as the main antagonist, Clint. He later appeared in the first few episodes of the second series as Champion J. Pepper, Clint's father.{{Cite news | first = Ryan J. | last = Foleythe | title = Vader's brother: He's no Darth | url = http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=ST&s_site=dfw&p_multi=ST&p_theme=realcities&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=117760EA5DF46560&p_field_direct-0=document_id&p_perpage=10&p_sort=YMD_date:D&s_trackval=GooglePM | agency = Associated Press | date = 2007-02-22 | accessdate = 2007-07-07 | archive-date = 2011-06-10 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110610013441/http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=ST&s_site=dfw&p_multi=ST&p_theme=realcities&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=117760EA5DF46560&p_field_direct-0=document_id&p_perpage=10&p_sort=YMD_date:D&s_trackval=GooglePM | url-status = live }} Since ''Chad Vader'', he has gone on to voice [[Darth Vader]] in various ''[[Star Wars]]'' media as the sound double for [[James Earl Jones]]. He hosts a movie reviewing and discussion show on YouTube called ''Welcome to the Basement''{{Cite web |title=About |date=December 14, 2012 |url=http://welcometothebasementshow.com/about/ |accessdate=26 August 2020 |archive-date=28 January 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200128141628/http://welcometothebasementshow.com/about/ |url-status=live |website=Welcome to the Basement}} until April 2023 with his friend Craig Johnson as co-host, since then a rotating cast of friends and fellow improv performers. Furthermore, he leads regularly with Aaron Yonda in the web series ''Beer and Board Games''. ==''Star Wars''== As a voice actor, Sloan played [[Darth Vader]] in ''[[Soulcalibur IV]]''. Sloan went on to reprise his role as the voice of Darth Vader in the [[LucasArts]] [[video game]]s ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]'',{{cite news | title = The Game Has Changed | url = http://www.vanityfair.com/culture/features/2008/03/lucas200803?currentPage=2 | publisher = | date = 2008-02-05 | accessdate = 2008-02-06 | archive-date = 2013-09-23 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20130923062242/http://www.vanityfair.com/culture/features/2008/03/lucas200803?currentPage=2 | url-status = live |last=DiGiacomo|first=Frank|work=Vanity Fair}} and ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption]]''. He also appeared as the voice of Darth Vader during an episode of ''[[Deal or No Deal (U.S. game show)|Deal or No Deal]]''.{{cite episode |title=''Star Wars'' Winner Take All |series=Deal or No Deal |date=28 April 2008 |season=3 |number=61 |last=Mandel |first=Howie (host)}}{{cite web |last1=Knutsen |first1=Kristian |title="Chad Vader Training Video" series launched by Blame Society as prelude to TV hopes |url=https://isthmus.com/arts/movies/chad-vader-training-video-series-launched-by-blame-society-as-prelude-to-tv-hopes/ |website=Isthmus |publisher=Isthmus Community Media, Inc. |access-date=10 October 2024 |language=en-us |date=21 May 2008}} Sloan also played Vader for the comedy short promoting [[TomTom]] devices. He returned as Vader for ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]''. In 2012, Sloan voiced Darth Vader in both ''[[Lego Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Out]]'' and ''[[Kinect Star Wars]]''. In 2015, Sloan returned to voice Vader in ''[[Disney Infinity 3.0]]'', ''[[Star Wars Battlefront (2015 video game)|Star Wars Battlefront]], [[Star Wars Battlefront II (2017 video game)|Star Wars Battlefront II]]'' and multiple ''[[Lego Star Wars]]'' shorts and television series,{{Cite video game | title = [[Disney Infinity 3.0]] | year = 2015 | scene=Closing credits, 5:39 in, Featuring the Voice Talents of| developer=[[Avalanche Software]]}} as well as providing his voice for a sketch in the final episode of ''[[The Daily Show|The Daily Show with Jon Stewart]]''. ==Filmography== === Television=== {| class="wikitable sortable" |- ! [[University of California, Los Angeles]] ([[Master of Arts|M.A.]], Theatre Arts) | occupation = Actor | years_active = 1965–2007 | spouse = {{Marriage|[[Meredith Baxter]]
|1974|1989|end=div.}} | children = 3 }} '''David Edwin Birney''' (April 23, 1939 – April 27, 2022) was an American actor and director whose career included performances in both contemporary and classical roles in theatre, film, and television. He is noted for having played the title role in the television series ''[[Serpico (TV series)|Serpico]]''. He also starred in ''[[Bridget Loves Bernie]]'', an early 1970s TV series about an interfaith marriage that also starred [[Meredith Baxter]], whom he married after the series ended. He also portrayed Dr. Ben Samuels in ''[[St. Elsewhere]]'' from 1982 until 1983. ==Early life== Birney was born to an [[Irish Catholic]] family in [[Washington, D.C.]], on April 23, 1939. His father, Edwin, worked as a special agent for the [[Federal Bureau of Investigation|FBI]]; his mother, Jeanne (née McGee), was a housewife before becoming a real estate agent.{{cite news|title=David Birney, Who Starred in TV's 'Bridget Loves Bernie,' Dies at 83|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/05/02/arts/television/david-birney-dead.html|first=Richard|last=Sandomir| date=May 2, 2022| access-date=May 3, 2022| id={{Gale|A702389440}} | page=A26(L) | newspaper=[[The New York Times]]}} Birney attended schools in [[Brooklyn, Ohio]], and graduated from West High School in [[Cleveland]]. Named to the [[National Honor Society]], he lettered in basketball, football, and track. He held a [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] degree from [[Dartmouth College]] with "High Distinction" in English literature, English Honors. At the [[University of California, Los Angeles]], Birney earned an [[Master of Arts|M.A.]] in theatre arts, acting and directing, studying with Ralph Freud and William Melnitz. He held a teaching assistant fellowship and was awarded an honorary [[Ph.D.]] in Humanities from [[Southern Utah University]].{{cite web| title=Honorary Degree Recipients: 1987| url=https://www.suu.edu/trustees/honorary-degree-recipients.html| access-date=November 8, 2021| website=Southern Utah University}} ==Career== ===Stage=== While in the [[U.S. Army]], Birney won an All Army Entertainment contest and received the "[[Barter Theatre]] Award" in 1965. Since the award was an equity contract with the Company for an entire season, he consequently spent the next season with the [[Barter Theatre]], the State Theatre of Virginia, starring or appearing in fifteen shows, directing two others. In the following two years he went on to perform with a range of companies and productions, [[off-Broadway]] and in several regional repertory theatres. His New York debut was with [[Joseph Papp|Joe Papp]]'s [[New York Shakespeare Festival]] as Antipholus of Syracuse in [[William Shakespeare]]’s ''[[The Comedy of Errors]]''. Birney worked continually in the theatre performing leading roles with some of the most important theatres in the country. His stage credits included starring roles on Broadway in ''[[Amadeus (play)|Amadeus]]'', ''[[Benefactors (play)|Benefactors]]'',{{cite web|title=Actor David Birney in a scene fr. the replacement cast of the Broadway play "Benefactors." Aside from his title role in ''Bridget Loves Bernie'', Birney appeared frequently on television, building a career in TV movies, regular series and [[miniseries]]. He starred in such series as ''[[Live Shot]]'', ''[[Cannon (TV series)|Cannon]]'', ''[[St. Elsewhere]]'', ''[[The Adams Chronicles]]'', ''[[Glitter (American TV series)|Glitter]]'',{{cite news |last1=Rothenberg |first1=Fred |title='Happy Days' Makes Way for New Shows |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1356&dat=19840502&id=XQIzAAAAIBAJ&pg=6979,680327 |access-date=April 21, 2020 |newspaper=[[Star–Banner|Ocala Star-Banner]] |date=May 2, 1984 |page=16}} ''Serpico'',{{cite news |last1=Holsapple |first1=Barbara |title=McMurray Child on 'Missing' | department=Midnight Movies|via=Google Newspapers |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1144&dat=19860115&id=MhwhAAAAIBAJ&pg=1755,6312339 |access-date=April 21, 2020 |newspaper=[[The Pittsburgh Press]] |date=January 15, 1986 |page=C11}} ''[[Fantasy Island]]'', ''[[Hawaii Five-O (1968 TV series)|Hawaii Five-O]]'', ''[[McMillan & Wife]]'', ''[[The F.B.I. (TV series)|The F.B.I.]]'', and ''[[Murder, She Wrote]]''.{{cite news |title=New Years |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1310&dat=19881231&id=nPFVAAAAIBAJ&pg=2563,8114457 |access-date=April 21, 2020 |newspaper=[[The Register-Guard]] |date=December 31, 1988 |location=Eugene, Oregon |page=24}} He also starred in the episode "The Nomads" from the 1977 series ''[[Quinn Martin's Tales of the Unexpected]]'', known in the United Kingdom as ''Twist in the Tale''.{{cite web|url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/tales_of_the_unexpected_1977 |title=Tales of the Unexpected|website=Rotten Tomatoes|access-date=May 3, 2022}} His miniseries credits include ''[[Testimony of Two Men]]'', ''[[Jacqueline Susann's Valley of the Dolls|Valley of the Dolls]]'', ''[[Night of the Fox]]'', and ''[[Master of the Game (novel)#Adaptations|Master of the Game]]''. He also appeared in the TV series the Love Boat with his wife where he played an Italian escort to an American woman whose friend arranged the encounter. Birney also appeared in leading roles in many television films, including ''[[The Irish in America: Long Journey Home|Long Journey Home]]'' and ''[[Serpico (TV series)|The Deadly Game]]''. He also appeared in the soap operas ''[[The Best of Everything (TV series)|The Best of Everything]]'' and ''[[Love Is a Many Splendored Thing (TV series)|Love Is a Many Splendored Thing]]''.{{cite book| url=https://books.google.com/books?id=NUXIAgAAQBAJ&q=david+birney+love+is+a+many&pg=PA2121| title=Encyclopedia of Television| last=Newcomb| first=Horace| date=2014| publisher=Routledge| isbn=978-1-1351-9472-7| page=2121| via=Google Books}} ===Writing and directing=== Birney edited and adapted for the stage a two-character play based on some of [[Mark Twain]]’s shorter works and letters. The piece, ''Mark Twain's The Diaries of Adam and Eve'', was presented on the [[PBS]] series ''[[American Playhouse]]''.{{cite book| url=https://books.google.com/books?id=VYsavOLN8HQC&q=david+birney+adam+eve+pbs+american+playhouse&pg=PA118| title=Critical Companion to Mark Twain: A Literary Reference to His Life and Work| last=Rasmussen| first=R. Kent| publisher=Infobase Publishing| year=2014| isbn=978-1-4381-0852-0| page=118}} Developing the play subsequently for the stage, Birney directed and starred in productions for regional theatres such as the [[Hartford Stage]] (opening the Mark Twain Festival in Hartford), the [[Capital Repertory Theatre]], and on tour in performing arts centers across the country. A second play, ''A Christmas Pudding'', a Christmas collage of song, story and poetry of the season was published by [[Samuel French, Inc.]]{{cite web| title=David Birney| url=https://www.concordtheatricals.com/a/310/david-birney| website=Concord Theatricals| access-date=November 8, 2021}} ===Professional associations=== Birney served on the Large Theatre Panel of the [[National Endowment for the Arts]] and was a board member of the [[Foundation for Biomedical Research]]. He also served on the Theatre and Dance Panel of the Jacob Javits Fellowship Foundation. For Dartmouth College he served as a member of the Board of Overseers for the [[Hopkins Center for the Arts]]. He initiated and chaired the Class of '61 Legacy: The American Tradition in Performance, helping to create a substantial endowment dedicated to live performance at the Hopkins Center at Dartmouth College.{{cite web| title=The Arts at Dartmouth Awards Ceremony| url=https://hop.dartmouth.edu/sites/hop.prod/files/hop/content/production-season/resource-file/artsawards2020playbill-final.pdf| date=May 26, 2020| website=Dartmouth College Department of Theater| access-date=November 8, 2021}} For five years, Birney co-chaired the [[American Diabetes Association]], speaking and fund raising for the Association. He was an advisor for the Children’s Rights Council, a national nonprofit organization advocating access to both parents after divorce or separation. His contribution to classical theatre was recognized with Washington's Shakespeare Theatre's Millennium Award. ==Personal life== Birney married actress [[Meredith Baxter]] in 1974. They had starred together in the 1972–73 TV series ''[[Bridget Loves Bernie]]''. During their marriage, she was known as Meredith Baxter Birney. Together, they had three children: Kate, Mollie, and Peter. They divorced in 1989. In 2011, she said Birney emotionally and physically abused her during their marriage.{{cite news| title=Meredith Baxter Alleges Ex-Husband David Birney Abused Her| url=https://abcnews.go.com/Entertainment/actress-meredith-baxter-abused-husband-david-birney/story?id=13029302| last=James| first=Susan Donaldson| date=December 2, 2009| work=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]]| access-date=November 8, 2021}} He published a lengthy statement on his website disputing the allegations.{{cite web| title='Untied' A Statement| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110619120632/http://davidbirney.com/UntiedStatement.pdf| archive-date=June 19, 2011| url=http://davidbirney.com/UntiedStatement.pdf| url-status=usurped| website=DavidBirney}}{{cite news| title=David Birney Denies Abuse Claims by Meredith Baxter| url=https://people.com/celebrity/david-birney-denies-abuse-claims-by-meredith-baxter/| date=March 4, 2011| first=Mike| last=Fleeman| journal=[[People (magazine)|People]]| access-date=November 8, 2021}} ==Death== In the December 2017 edition of the ''Wide Wide World'' newsletter for [[Dartmouth College]] class of 1961 alumni, it was disclosed that Birney had been diagnosed with [[Alzheimer's disease]].{{cite journal| url=http://dartmouth.imodules.com/s/1353/images/gid7/editor_documents/newsletters/2017/december/1961_december_2017.pdf| date=December 2017| page=5| title=Green Cards| last=Bloom| first=Arthur| journal=Wide Wide World| access-date=November 8, 2021}} Birney died on April 27, 2022, four days after his 83rd birthday, at his home in [[Santa Monica, California]].
