[[Cyd Charisse]] (aunt) }} '''Nana Visitor''' ({{IPAc-en|n|ə|ˈ|n|ɑː}} {{respell|nə|NAH}};{{cite web|title=Star Trek Infinite Space: Nana Visitor & Rene Auberjonois Interview|via = YouTube|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cBNHwmz_pHA|access-date=November 12, 2023|date=September 28, 2011}} born '''Nana Tucker'''; July 26, 1957) is an American actress, best known for playing Major, later Colonel, [[Kira Nerys]] in the television series ''[[Star Trek: Deep Space Nine]]'' and Jean Ritter in the television series ''[[Wildfire (2005 TV series)|Wildfire]]''. ==Early life== Nana Tucker was born July 26, 1957, in New York City,{{cite web |url = http://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/nana-visitor/190655 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080203065144/http://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/nana-visitor/190655 |url-status = dead |archive-date = February 3, 2008 |title = Nana Visitor |work = [[TV Guide]] |access-date = September 7, 2011 }} the daughter of Nenette Charisse, a ballet teacher, and Robert Tucker, a choreographer; she is a niece of actress/dancer [[Cyd Charisse]].{{cite web |url = http://www.filmreference.com/film/4/Nana-Visitor.html |title = Nana Visitor Biography (1957–) |work = Film Reference. |access-date = August 12, 2013 }} ==Career== {{refimprove|section|date=October 2026}} Visitor began her acting career in the 1970s on the [[Broadway theatre|Broadway]] stage in such productions as ''[[My One and Only (musical)|My One and Only]]''.{{cite web|title=Nana Visitor|url=http://www.playbill.com/person/nana-visitor-vault-0000044934|work = Playbill |access-date=28 July 2018}} Her film debut (billed by her birth name, Nana Tucker) came in the 1977 horror film ''[[The Sentinel (1977 film)|The Sentinel]].'' On television, Visitor co-starred in the short-lived 1976 sitcom ''[[Ivan the Terrible (TV series)|Ivan the Terrible]]'' and from 1978 to 1982, had short-lived regular roles on three soap operas: ''[[Ryan's Hope]],'' ''[[The Doctors (soap opera)|The Doctors]],'' and ''[[One Life to Live]].'' Upon the suggestion of her older brother Paris, she adopted the stage name "Nana Visitor" in the early 1980s,{{cite web |url=https://vm.tiktok.com/ZMFop1s3m/ |format=TikTok |title=Star Trek Nana Visitor Talks about her stage name |accessdate=2023-01-13 }} and had her name legally changed to "Visitor" some time later.{{cite podcast| url= https://scpod.net/episodes/star-trek-deep-space-nines-nana-visitor-commander-kira-nerys| title= Star Trek Deep Space Nine's Nana Visitor| website=Spoiler Country| last1=Regan|first1=Kenric|last2=Horsley|first2=John| date=28 July 2020| time=00:20:00| access-date=13 November 2024}}{{cite podcast| url= https://patreon.com/posts/113868024| title= The Delta Flyers - DS9 Crossover 223| website=The Delta Flyers| last1=McNeill|first1=Robert Duncan|last2=Wang|first2=Garrett|last3=Shimerman|first3=Armin| date=14 October 2024| time=02:34:00| access-date=13 November 2024}} In 1984, she appeared in a season-two episode of ''[[Hunter (1984 U.S. TV series)|Hunter]].'' In 1985, Visitor made appearances on the television series ''[[MacGyver (1985 TV series)|MacGyver]],'' in the season-one episode "Hellfire" as Laura Farren, and in the season-two episode "DOA: MacGyver" as Carol Varnay. She also made an appearance in the fourth-season ''[[Remington Steele]]'' episode titled "Steele Blushing" the same year. In 1986, she appeared in "Hills of Fire", a fourth-season episode of ''[[Knight Rider (1982 TV series)|Knight Rider]],'' as well as third-season ''[[Highway to Heaven]]'' episodes "Love at Second Sight" and "Love and Marriage, Part II" as Margaret Swann. In 1987, Visitor appeared as Ellen Dolan in a failed [[television pilot]] for Will Eisner's pulp comic creation ''[[The Spirit (character)|The Spirit]],'' starring [[Sam J. Jones]] as the title character and [[Garry Walberg]] as her father, Commissioner Dolan. [[File:Nana Visitor STICCon 2004 crop.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Visitor at STICCon XVIII (2004)]] In 1988, she made an appearance on the sitcom ''[[Night Court]]'' as a mental patient who is obsessed with the movies. That same year, she made an appearance on the television series ''[[In the Heat of the Night (TV series)|In the Heat of the Night]]'' as the owner of the Sparta newspaper. She also made an appearance that year in an episode of ''[[Matlock (1986 TV series)|Matlock]].'' In 1989, Visitor appeared in the fifth episode of the television series ''[[Doogie Howser, M.D.]]'' as Charmagne, a rock star who has a throat nodule removed at Doogie's hospital, and as Miles Drentell's glamorous girlfriend, in "Success", a 1989 episode of ''[[Thirtysomething (TV series)|Thirtysomething]]''{{'}}s second season. In 1990, Visitor co-starred with [[Sandra Bullock]] in the short-lived sitcom ''[[Working Girl (TV series)|Working Girl]],'' which was based on the feature film of the same name. From 1993 to 1999, Visitor appeared in ''[[Star Trek: Deep Space Nine]]'' as Major (later Colonel) [[Kira Nerys]], a former freedom fighter/terrorist from the planet Bajor, who fought against the occupation of her world by the [[Cardassians]]. After the occupation ended, she was appointed as first officer of the series's eponymous space station, built by the Cardassians and turned over to [[Starfleet]]. She revisited the character, as a voice actress, in the third season of the animated series ''[[Star Trek: Lower Decks]]''.{{cite web |last1=Orquiola |first1=John |title="It Made No Sense": DS9 Actor Explains Her Plan To Also Play Star Trek: Voyager's Captain Janeway |date=June 18, 2025 |url=https://screenrant.com/star-trek-ds9-nana-visitor-voyager-janeway-both-roles/ |publisher=Screen Rant |access-date=21 June 2025}} She was also interested to play the character of [[Kathryn Janeway]] in the series ''[[Star Trek: Voyager]]'', filmed at the same time.{{cite web |last1=Pascale |first1=Anthony |title=Interview: Nana Visitor On Wanting To Play Janeway On 'Voyager' And The Future Of Kira Nerys In 'Star Trek' |url=https://trekmovie.com/2025/06/17/interview-nana-visitor-on-wanting-to-play-janeway-on-voyager-and-the-future-of-kira-nerys-in-star-trek/ |publisher=Trekmovie |access-date=21 June 2025}} [[File:Visitor and Auberjonois by Beth Madison, 2.jpg|thumb|left|Nana Visitor and [[Rene Auberjonois]] at the 2011 Star Trek convention in Las Vegas]] After ''DS9'' ended, Visitor had a recurring role as villain Dr. Elizabeth Renfro on the television series ''[[Dark Angel (2000 TV series)|Dark Angel]].'' Visitor then starred as Roxie Hart in both the touring and Broadway companies of the musical ''[[Chicago (musical)|Chicago]],''{{cite web|url=http://www.playbill.com/article/nana-visitor-is-foxy-roxie-hart-in-bways-chicago-beginning-may-8-com-96505|title=Nana Visitor Is Foxy Roxie Hart in Bway's ''Chicago'' Beginning May 8|last=Jones|first=Kenneth|date=8 May 2001|website=[[Playbill]]|access-date=28 July 2018}} including starring as Hart as curtains rose again after September 11, 2001. Visitor was then cast as Jean Ritter on the [[Freeform (TV channel)|ABC Family]] series ''[[Wildfire (2005 TV series)|Wildfire]],'' which premiered on June 20, 2005. In 2008, she appeared as Emily Kowalski, a dying cancer patient in "[[Faith (Battlestar Galactica)|Faith]]", an episode of the reimagined ''[[Battlestar Galactica (2004 TV series)|Battlestar Galactica]]''{{'}}s fourth season. Visitor had a small role as [[Pamela Voorhees]] in the 2009 version of ''[[Friday the 13th (2009 film)|Friday the 13th]].'' She has also lent her voice in a few appearances on the sitcom ''[[Family Guy]],'' such as Rita in the episode "[[Brian's Got a Brand New Bag]]", and as the voice of the [[USS Enterprise (NCC-1701)|''Enterprise'']] in "[[Extra Large Medium]]." In 2011, she had a small part in the Hammer Horror film ''[[The Resident (film)|The Resident]],'' playing the realtor. She appeared in ''[[Torchwood: Miracle Day]]'' episodes seven ("[[Immortal Sins]]") and eight ("[[End of the Road (Torchwood)|End of the Road]]").{{cite journal |title=Horror Flicks |date=June 2011| journal=[[Doctor Who Magazine]]| issue=435}} In 2012, she appeared as Dr. Patty Barker, a canine psychotherapist, in "An Embarrassment of Bitches", a [[List of Castle episodes#Season 4 (2011–12)|season-four episode]] of ABC's ''[[Castle (TV series)|Castle]]''.{{cite web|title=Ep 13 – An Embarrassment of Bitches|url=http://castletv.net/ep-13-an-embarrassment-of-bitches|date=December 1, 2011|publisher=Castle TV on ABC & TNT|access-date=November 1, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120915235756/http://castletv.net/ep-13-an-embarrassment-of-bitches/|archive-date=September 15, 2012|url-status=dead}} 2024 saw the publication of her book, "Star Trek: Open a Channel: A Woman's Trek", a look at the female characters of the Star Trek franchise, and the actors who portrayed them. ==Personal life== [[File:Nana Visitor by Gage Skidmore.jpg|thumb|Nana Visitor at the 2018 [[WonderCon]]]] Visitor was married to Nick Miscusi from 1989 to 1994.{{cite web|last=Lipton |first = Michael A.|url=http://www.people.com/people/archive/article/0,,20106069,00.html|title=Winner by a Nose|date=August 16, 1993|newspaper=[[People (magazine)|People]]|volume=40|number=7}} They have one son together.{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e0fN_VBIn8w |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211212/e0fN_VBIn8w| archive-date=2021-12-12 |url-status=live|title=TABNation PSA - Nana Visitor|first=James P. |last = Coree|date=18 May 2015|via=YouTube}}{{cbignore}} Visitor began dating her ''Star Trek: Deep Space Nine'' co-star [[Alexander Siddig]] and married him in June 1997. They divorced in April 2001. They also have a son together, and her pregnancy was incorporated into her character and the series storyline, beginning in the 1996 fourth season episode "[[Body Parts (Star Trek: Deep Space Nine)|Body Parts]]".{{cite book |last1 = Erdmann |first1 = Terry J. |last2 = Block |first2 = Paula M. |title = Star Trek: Deep Space Nine Companion |publisher = [[Pocket Books]] |year = 2000 |pages = 351–352 }}{{cite web |url = http://www.startrek.com/database_article/body-parts |title = Body Parts |work = StarTrek.com |access-date = August 12, 2013 }} She gave birth to her son on September 16, 1996, during production of the episode "[[The Assignment (Star Trek: Deep Space Nine)|The Assignment]]", though her character would remain pregnant until the fifth-season episode "[[The Begotten]]".{{harvp|Erdmann|Block|2000|p= 407|ps=.}} In early 2002, Visitor became engaged to Matthew Rimmer, previously company manager for the musical ''Chicago,'' and from 2017 chief operating officer of The Broad Stage in [[Santa Monica, California|Santa Monica]].{{cite web |title=Matthew Rimmer - Chief Operating Officer at BroadStage |url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/matthew-rimmer-a6196525?original_referer= |website=linkedin.com |publisher=Linkedin |access-date=8 February 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230208093423/https://www.linkedin.com/in/matthew-rimmer-a6196525?original_referer= |archive-date= 8 February 2023}}{{cite web |title=The Broad Stage Announces 2020/21 Season - Press Release, pp. 6-7 |url=https://issuu.com/thebroadstage/docs/final_the_broad_stage_announces_2020-1 |website=issuu.com |date=May 28, 2020 |publisher=Issuu Inc. |access-date=8 February 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230208093720/https://issuu.com/thebroadstage/docs/final_the_broad_stage_announces_2020-1 |archive-date= 8 February 2023}} They married in April 2003.{{cite web | title= Nana's Bio | url= http://nanavision.com/about/ | publisher= Nanavision | access-date= 2013-08-12 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20160317213249/http://nanavision.com/about/ | archive-date= March 17, 2016 | url-status= dead }} Their relationship ended in 2007.{{cite web | title= ‘Wildfire’ Real Life Relationships: Who From the Cast Is Married, Dating or Single | url= https://www.womansworld.com/entertainment/tv-shows/wildfire-cast-real-life-couples-marriages-and-relationships | author=Julianne MacNeill | publisher= Woman's World| date=2025-08-17 | access-date= 2026-10-16}} Visitor and her ''Star Trek: Deep Space Nine'' co-star [[Terry Farrell (actress)|Terry Farrell]] were honored in 2001 when [[William Kwong Yu Yeung]] named two [[small Solar System bodies]] he had discovered after them – asteroid [[26733 Nanavisitor]] and asteroid [[26734 Terryfarrell]].{{cite web|url=http://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/sbdb.cgi?sstr=26734+Terryfarrell#content|title=JPL Small-Body Database Browser|work=nasa.gov}}{{cite web|url=http://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/sbdb.cgi?sstr=26733+Nanavisitor#content|title=JPL Small-Body Database Browser|work=nasa.gov}} ==Filmography== {{Unreferenced|section|date=October 2026}} ===Film=== {| class="wikitable sortable" |- ! '''Thomas Randell Oglesby''' (born 1949) is an American actor, best known for his recurring role as [[Degra]] on ''[[Star Trek: Enterprise]]''. He is also known for his other ''Star Trek'' roles, including captain Trena'L in the ''[[Star Trek: Enterprise]]'' episode "[[Unexpected (Star Trek: Enterprise)|Unexpected]]", the Miradorn twins, Ah-Kel and Ro-Kel, in the ''[[Star Trek: Deep Space Nine]]'' episode "[[Vortex (Star Trek: Deep Space Nine)|Vortex]]", Silaran Prin in "[[The Darkness and the Light (Star Trek: Deep Space Nine)|The Darkness and the Light]]" and as the telepathic alien Kir in "[[Counterpoint (Star Trek: Voyager)|Counterpoint]]", a season 5 episode of ''[[Star Trek: Voyager]]''.

==Career==
Oglesby played Professor Seidel in the ''[[Angel (1999 TV series)|Angel]]'' episode "[[Supersymmetry (Angel)|Supersymmetry]]".

On ''[[Star Trek: The Next Generation]]'', Season 2 Episode 5, "[[Loud as a Whisper]]", aired January 9, 1989, he played one of three Interpreters known as Riva's Chorus.

Oglesby appeared in ''[[Independence Day (1996 film)|Independence Day]]'' (1996) as Mike Dodge. His most memorable moment is asking [[Randy Quaid]] if the aliens, who he claimed abducted him, did any "sexual things".

In 2000, he made a guest appearance as Reverend Mackee in the seventh season episode "Signs and Wonders" of ''[[The X-Files]]'', and as Joshua Vinten (the manager of formalwear rental shop) on the second last episode of TV series ''[[Columbo (TV series)|Columbo]]'' (''[[List of Columbo episodes#Season 10 and special episodes|Murder With Too Many Notes]]'').

Oglesby made a guest appearance on the ABC soap opera, ''[[General Hospital]]'' in the role of Huell on July 17, 2007. In the same year he played [[Bethlehem Steel]] executive Walter Veith in the ''[[Mad Men]]'' episode "[[New Amsterdam (Mad Men)|New Amsterdam]]".

He played Tom Jeter's father in ''[[Studio 60 on the Sunset Strip]]''.

In 2011, Oglesby played the role of Capt. Lachlan McKelty in the video game ''[[L.A. Noire]]'', that was developed by [[Team Bondi]] and [[Rockstar Games]].

In 2017, Oglesby played the role of Asa Leopold in the [[Netflix]] [[Limited series (comics)|limited series]] ''[[Godless (TV series)|Godless]]''.<ref>{{cite web |last=Petski |first=Denise |url=https://deadline.com/2016/09/godless-sam-waterston-kim-coates-cast-jeff-daniels-scoot-mcnairy-1201813565/|title='Godless' Adds Sam Waterston, Kim Coates, More; Scoot McNairy Confirmed|publisher=Deadline|date=September 6, 2016|accessdate=September 6, 2016}}</ref>

In 2021, he appeared as Dr. Stan Nielson in episode 3 of the [[Marvel Studios]] television miniseries ''[[WandaVision]]''.<ref>{{cite web |last=Hood |first=Cooper |url=https://screenrant.com/wandavision-episode-3-cast-marvel-character-guide/|title=WandaVision Episode 3 Cast Guide |publisher=ScreenRant |date=January 22, 2021 |accessdate=January 22, 2021}}</ref>

'''Vaughn Dale Armstrong''' (born July 7, 1950) is an American actor. He is noted for portraying many characters in the ''[[Star Trek]]'' franchise, in four [[Star Trek#Television series|''Star Trek'' television series]]. He is perhaps best known as the recurring character [[List of minor recurring characters in Star Trek: Enterprise#Maxwell Forrest|Admiral Maxwell Forrest]] in ''[[Star Trek: Enterprise]]''.<ref name="GuestStarProfileVaughnArmstrong">{{cite AV media |people=Vaughn Armstrong |date=April 9, 2003 |title=Guest Star Profile: Vaughn Armstrong |medium=DVD |time=7 seconds |publisher=Paramount |asin=B00062IDLA }}</ref><ref name="ign">{{cite web |date=September 14, 2001 |author=Ivan Sian |title=SciFi: Enterprise's Admiral |url=http://scifi.ign.com/articles/315160p1.html |website=[[IGN]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20020209174337/http://scifi.ign.com/articles/315160p1.html |archive-date=February 9, 2002 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He has played twelve Star Trek characters.<ref>{{cite web |date=January 1, 2017 |author=Juliette Harrisson |title=Star Trek Voyager: 10 Great Guest Performances |website=[[Den of Geek]] |url=https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/star-trek-voyager-10-great-guest-performances/ |access-date=April 1, 2021}}</ref>

In 1985, Armstrong portrayed drill instructor Sergeant Williams in a production of the play ''Tracers'' at the Coronet Theater in Los Angeles.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Mikulan |first1=Steven |title=The New 'Tracers' |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/63937280/la-weekly/ |access-date=November 24, 2020 |work=LA Weekly |date=December 5, 1985 |location=California, Los Angeles |page=72|via = [[Newspapers.com]] }}</ref> In 1989, he played Father Larkin, a priest-principal of a Catholic school, in ''Stand-up Tragedy'' at the Mark Taper Forum in Los Angeles.<ref>{{cite web |date=June 18, 1989 |first=Dan |last=Sullivan |title=An Old Story Brought Up to Speed : 'Stand-up Tragedy's' full-court press |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1989-06-18-ca-3770-story.html |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=An Old Story Brought Up to Speed |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/63937712/the-los-angeles-times/ |access-date=November 24, 2020 |work=The Los Angeles Times |date=June 18, 1989 |page=305|via = [[Newspapers.com]] }}</ref> In 1992 he appeared in an episode of ''[[Quantum Leap (1989 TV series)|Quantum Leap]]'' as [[Fred Trump]] (alongside his future ''Enterprise'' co-star [[Scott Bakula]]).<ref name="ign" /> In 2008, he had the role of Will Torrey, an American union representative in ''Ravensridge'' at the Fremont Centre Theatre in South Pasadena, California.<ref>{{cite news |last=Foley |first=F. Kathleen |title=Greed is native to every country |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/63938069/the-los-angeles-times/ |access-date=November 24, 2020 |newspaper=The Los Angeles Times |date=February 29, 2008 |page=72 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=February 25, 2008 |last=Mikulan |first=Steven |title=Ravensridge: Atlas Smirked |url=https://www.laweekly.com/ravensridge-atlas-smirked/ |website=[[LA Weekly]] }}</ref>

'''James Joseph Sloyan Jr.'''<ref name="aos obit" /><ref name="jjs obit" /> (February 24, 1941 – July 22, 2026) was an American character actor of stage and screen, as well as a much-employed voice actor, most notably via his two-decade tenure as the voice of [[Lexus]]. He is the father of [[Samantha Sloyan]].

==Early life and career==
Sloyan was born in [[Indianapolis]], Indiana, on February 24, 1941.<ref name="Legacy">{{cite web |title=James SLOYAN|website=legacy.com |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/latimes/name/james-sloyan-obituary?id=62497894 |date=September 20, 2026}}</ref> One of four children, two girls and two boys, born to James J. Sloyan and Annamae O'Brien<ref name="aos obit">[https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-indianapolis-star/193126257/ "Obituaries: Annamae Sloyan"]. ''The Indianapolis Star''. August 23 1985. p. 47. Retrieved March 12, 2026. "Services for Annamae O'Brien Sloyan, 82, Albany, N.Y., formerly of Indianapolis and mother of actor James Sloyan, will be l0 a.m. Saturday in Assumption-St. Paul Catholic Church, Mechanicville. N.Y. The widow of James J. Sloyan, she died Wednesday in Albany Medical Center. A native of Mechanicville, she had been an Indianapolis resident many years before moving to Albany 30 years ago. Her son, an Indianapolis native, has starred in several Broadway shows and two television series, including Oh Madeline with actress Madeline Kahn. [...] Survivors, besides her son. include a daughter. Judy Wilkes, and another son, Patrick J. Sloyan."</ref><ref name="jjs obit">[https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-indianapolis-star/193131953/ "SLOYAN]. ''The Indianapolis Star''. 1954. Sec. 3, p. 7. Retrieved March 12, 2026. "James J.. 3490 E. Fall Creek Pkwy., N. Dr.. husband of Annamae, father of Patrick J., James J. Jr., and Judy, also survived by 3 sisters. Anna Sloyan, Mrs. Josephine Grampp of New York. [...] [S]ervices and burial Monday at Mechanicsville, N.Y.."</ref> (another being [[Pulitzer Prize]]-winning journalist [[Patrick J. Sloyan]]<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-post-star/193130053/ "Obituaries: Ann Judith (Judy) Wilkes (Oct. 8, 1935—Jan. 11, 2022)"]. ''The Post-Star''. January 23, 2022. p. C6. Retrieved March 13, 2026. "Judy was born Oct. 8, 1935 to the late Annamae (O’Brien) and James Sloyan in Stamford, CT, and had three siblings: Pulitzer Prize winning journalist, Patrick Sloyan (d. 2019, m. Phyllis); Elizabeth Sloyan (d. 1949); stage/film/television actor, James Sloyan (m. Deirdre)."</ref>), Sloyan Jr. spent most of the next nine and a half years in Europe, namely Italy, Switzerland, Ireland, and—if only long enough to board the next ship bound for home—Paris, France,<ref>"New York, New York Passenger and Crew Lists, 1909, 1925-1958", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:24TG-L62 : Sun Apr 13 03:58:40 UTC 2025), Entry for James Sloyan, 1950.</ref> before dividing the remainder of his preteens/adolescence between three decidedly disparate New York State municipalities. 1) [[Mechanicville, New York|Mechanicville]], the birthplace of Sloyan's mother<ref name="aos obit"/>; 2) [[Albany, New York|Albany]], the state capitol, where, by his own count, Sloyan was "actually thrown out of five [or] six high schools"<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/article/st-louis-post-dispatch/193118358/ "Network Bio"]. ''St. Louis Post-Dispatch''. April 10, 1977. p. 56.</ref>, and  3) New York City, where in 1957, Sloyan embarked on his scholarship-subsidized two years of study at the [[American Academy of Dramatic Arts]].<ref name="STFAQ20"/> 

Sloyan's acting career was interrupted in 1962, when he was drafted into the [[United States Army]] during the [[Vietnam War]].<ref name="STFAQ20">Clark, Mark (2013). ''[https://www.google.com/books/edition/Star_Trek_FAQ_2_0_Unofficial_and_Unautho/dWBfAgAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=1940+February+24+%22James+sloyan%22&pg=PT198&printsec=frontcover Star Trek: FAQ 2.0: EVERYTHING LEFT TO KNOW ABOUT THE NEXT GENERATION, THE MOVIES AND BEYOND (UNOFFICIAL AND UNAUTHORIZED)]''. Milwaukee, WI: Applause Theatre & Cinema Books. {{ISBN|978-1-55783-793-6}}.</ref>

==Television==
Sloyan's television career includes numerous brief performances on daytime dramas ''[[The Young and the Restless]], [[General Hospital]]'', and ''[[Ryan's Hope]]'', and guest appearances on prime-time series ''[[Hawaii Five-O (1968 TV series)|Hawaii Five-O]]''; ''[[The Streets of San Francisco]]''; ''[[Wonder Woman (TV series)|Wonder Woman]]''; ''[[Baywatch]]''; ''[[Moonlighting (TV series)|Moonlighting]]''; ''[[Quantum Leap (1989 TV series)|Quantum Leap]]''; ''[[The X-Files]]''; ''[[MacGyver (1985 TV series)|MacGyver]]''; ''[[Party of Five]]''; ''[[Matlock (1986 TV series)|Matlock]]''; ''[[Murder, She Wrote]]''; and ''[[Dr. Quinn, Medicine Woman]]''. He appeared in the [[Made-for-television|television movies]] ''[[Blind Ambition (miniseries)|Blind Ambition]]'', ''[[Billionaire Boys Club (1987 film)|Billionaire Boys Club]]'', and ''My Son Is Innocent''.

In the fall of 1970, Sloyan, [[James Broderick]], and [[Reni Santoni]] were cast in the ''[[ABC Movie of the Week]]'' episode, "[[Panic on the 5:22]]", as a trio of underprivileged, disaffected, and somewhat desperate [[Bronx]] residents who board a suburbs-bound commuter train in [[Manhattan]] and, after donning ski masks and drawing guns, commandeer its [[parlor car|club car]] in hopes of making a quick killing.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/article/cumberland-evening-times/193803212/ "Hoods Menace Passengers"]. ''Cumberland Times-News''. Nov 9, 1974. p. 12. Retrieved March 20, 2026. "Three gunmen looking quick "score," hold-up affluent passengers aboard the club car of a swank New commuter train in "Panic The 5:22,' [...] Harvey Hart directed the Eugene Price screenplay that pits the trio of bumbling but dangerous hoodlums, frustrated graduates of a teenage gang in the Bronx, against a problem-ridden group of Manhattan business executives, a promiscuous high fashion New York model, a retired Army general, a brittle female cosmetic firm owner, a young attorney and a professional athlete."</ref><ref name="cameron">{{Cite news|title=Television Review: Panic on the 3:22|author=Cameron, Sue|date=November 21, 1974|work=The Hollywood Review|page=6|quote='Panic on the 5:22' is a 'disaster film' with a message. Instead of being held prisoner in a burning building or running from an earthquake, a group of wealthy people are held hostage and robbed at gunpoint in the club car of a commuter train. The three criminals represent the underprivileged slum people and the passengers represent everything the robbers want most and hate at the same time. In other words, it's a class confrontation on a train, with the robbery used as a tool for the message. It's a better-than-average MOW that just moves right along suspensefully. James Sloyan, Robert Walden and Reni Santoni give excellent performances as the crooks. [...] Quinn Martin was executive producer and Anthony Spinner produced. It was written by Eugene Price and directed by Harvey Hart.|id={{ProQuest|2931983431}}}}</ref><ref name="thomas">Thomas, Kevin (November 20, 1974). [https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-los-angeles-times/193304619/ "A Morality Play in 'Panic'"]. ''[[The Los Angeles Times]]''. pt. IV, p. 20. Retrieved March 20, 2026. "Robert Walden and his pals from long-ago teenage gang days, dim-witted Reni Santoni and nervous James Sloyan, board a train at Grand Central Station bound for Groton, Conn., [...] In the 35 minutes--minus commercials - before Walden and company don ski masks and draw their guns, Hart and Price show their wealthy would-be victims as largely unsympathetic types, for the most part arrogant, self-centered and, in a few instances, downright crooked. Thus, the difference between these rich passengers and the intruders is one of socio-economics rather than morals."</ref> Much to their dismay, these hopes are promptly dashed, and their desperation dramatically escalated, by the discovery that these affluent suburbanites carry nothing but credit cards.<ref>Halliwell, Leslie (1977). ''[https://archive.org/details/halliwellsfilmgu0000hall_e0p8/page/574/mode/2up?q=%22panic+on+the%22+%22w+eugene+price+d+harvey+hart%22 Halliwell's Film Guide : A Survey of 8,000 English-Language Movies]''. London: Granada Publishing. p. 574–575. {{ISBN|0246109823}}. "Wealthy passengers are terrorized by three incompetent hoodlums who are exasperated at finding credit cards instead of money. Smooth, odd little suspenser which goes on too long and submerges in cliche philosophy. Some smart moments, though."</ref> In 1972, Sloyan co-starred with [[James Coco]] in [[Neil Simon]]'s "The Greasy Spoon", one of five sketches that comprise his dark comedy, ''The Trouble With People'', presented by ''Bell System Television Theatre'' on [[NBC-TV]].<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-ouachita-citizen/193145336/ "Hooked by a Crook?"]. ''The Ouachita Citizen''. November 2, 1972. p. 7-B. Retrieved March 12, 2026. "'The Greasy Diner' has more than grease in store for James Coco as he finds out. Coco and Jim Sloyan star in 'The Greasy Diner,' one of the five sketches in the NBC-TV. Bell System Family Theatre presentation of Nell Simon's 'The Trouble With People,' which will be presented Sunday, Nov. 12, from 8-9 p.m."</ref> 

He appeared in a number of science fiction television series, including ''[[Buck Rogers in the 25th Century (TV series)|Buck Rogers in the 25th Century]]'', in which he portrayed Barnard "Barney" Smith in the episode "The Plot to Kill a City", and several roles in the ''[[Star Trek]]'' franchise. In ''[[Star Trek: The Next Generation]]'', he portrayed Alidar Jarok (a defecting Romulan admiral) in "[[The Defector (TNG episode)|The Defector]]", and [[Alexander Rozhenko]] (Worf's son) as an adult in the future, in "[[Firstborn (Star Trek: The Next Generation)|Firstborn]]" using the alias "K'mtar". In ''[[Star Trek: Deep Space Nine]]'', he portrayed the Bajoran scientist [[List of recurring characters in Star Trek: Deep Space Nine#Doctor Mora Pol|Doctor Mora Pol]], [[Odo (Star Trek)|Odo's]] guardian scientist in the episodes "[[The Begotten]]" and "[[The Alternate (Star Trek: Deep Space Nine)|The Alternate]]". The ''[[Star Trek: Voyager]]'' episode "[[Jetrel]]" features Sloyan as the title character.

==Film==
Sloyan is featured in ''[[The Sting]]'' as Mottola, who is used to illustrate the concept of a griftee, in a variation on the [[pigeon drop]] scam.

He played roles in ''[[The Traveling Executioner]]'' (1970),<ref>Hale, Ernest (September 27, 1970). [https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-columbus-ledger/193134067/ "Flicker Footnotes: 'Executioner' Is Sardonic Tale"]. ''The Columbus Ledger''. p .18. Retrieved March 13, 2026. "James J. Sloyan (r) as Deputy Warden Piquant, talks with prisoners in 'The Traveling Executioner'."</ref> ''[[The Gang That Couldn't Shoot Straight]]'' (1971), and ''[[Xanadu (film)|Xanadu]]'' (1980).

==Advertisements==
For 20 years, Sloyan was the [[voice-over|voice]] of Lexus. The company's first commercial, "[[Balance (advertisement)|Balance]]," aired in 1989 and went on to win several awards as well as homages in pop culture and media. Sloyan served as Lexus' sole voice actor until 2009.<ref name="STFAQ20"/> He later narrated ads for Mitsubishi.{{fact|date=September 2015}}
Sloyan was also a voice actor for [[Sprint Nextel]] long-distance services, and in film trailers for movies such as ''[[Jumper (2008 film)|Jumper]]'', ''[[The Shadow (1994 film)|The Shadow]]'', and ''[[How to Make an American Quilt]]''.<ref>[http://www.cedvoices.com/search_results.php?pageoffset=420&keyword=&mode=region&FileNameID=&search=5&subcat= CED Voices.com<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

==Personal life and death==
Sloyan and actress [[Deirdre Lenihan]] began dating in 1963 and became engaged five years later.<ref name="Cincinnati1973">{{cite news |last=Hoffman |first=Steve |title="TV and Radio: Lenihan May Be a New TV Sensation"|work=The Cincinnati Enquirer |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-cincinnati-enquirer/193113384/ |date=June 27, 1973 |page=20}}</ref> By 1973, they were openly living together, and seemed poised to take the plunge.<ref name="Boston1973">{{cite news |last=Shain |first=Percy |title=Deirdre Lenihan Proves Enchanting Newcomer |work=Boston Sunday Globe |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-boston-globe/193112784/ |date=November 25, 1973 |page=92}}</ref> They had two children, Daniel Sloyan and actress [[Samantha Sloyan]].<ref name="nse1977">{{cite news |last=Terry |first=Carol Burton |title=TV Line |work=Newsday (Suffolk Edition) |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/newsday-suffolk-edition/193184078/ |date=May 15, 1977 |page=337}}</ref><ref name="stpd1977">{{cite news |title=Sloyan Bio|work=St. Louis Post-Dispatch |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/st-louis-post-dispatch/193119924/ |date=April 10, 1977 |page=194}}</ref>

Sloyan died at his home in [[Sherman Oaks, California]], on July 22, 2026, at the age of 85.<ref name="Legacy"/><ref name="THR">{{cite news |last1=Barnes |first1=Mike |title=James Sloyan, Actor in ‘The Sting,‘ ‘Xanadu’ and ‘Oh Madeline,’ Dies at 85 |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/james-sloyan-dead-the-sting-oh-madeline-xanadu-1236706919/ |access-date=21 September 2026 |publisher=The Hollywood Reporter |date=21 September 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=MSN |url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/entertainment/general/star-trek-s-james-sloyan-dies-at-the-age-of-85/ar-AA2cHtYg?ocid=msedgntp&pc=NMTS&cvid=6ab1b35a8d374532b0ceaa967429163e&ei=10 |access-date=2026-09-21 |website=www.msn.com}}</ref>

Cromwell retained custody of their three children: Kate, now 18 and a freshman at Smith College, John, 16, and Colin, 14.}} He received his acting training at [[HB Studio]].{{cite web|url=https://hbstudio.org/about-hb-studio/alumni/ |publisher=HB Studio|title= Alumni|access-date=May 26, 2020|archive-date=May 12, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200512013549/https://hbstudio.org/about-hb-studio/alumni/|url-status=live}} ==Career== Cromwell's first television performance was in a 1974 episode of ''[[The Rockford Files]]'' playing Terry, a tennis instructor. A few weeks later,{{cite web |url=http://epguides.com/AllintheFamily/ |title=All in the Family (a Titles & Air Dates Guide) |publisher=Epguides.com |date=November 27, 2011 |access-date=February 28, 2012 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120308093536/http://epguides.com/AllintheFamily/ |archive-date=March 8, 2012 |df=mdy-all }} he began a recurring role as Stretch Cunningham on ''[[All in the Family]]''.{{cite news |last1=Winfrey |first1=Lee |title=Strike Series Puts 'Family' Back on Top |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-philadelphia-inquirer-james-cromwell/177551557/ |work=The Philadelphia Inquirer |date=October 11, 1974 |location=Philadelphia, PA |page=41 |access-date=July 27, 2025 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}} In 1975, he took his first lead role on television as Bill Lewis in the short-lived ''[[Hot l Baltimore]]'',{{cite news |title=Production Under Way on Series |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-south-bend-tribune-james-cromwell-b/177551725/ |work=The South Bend Tribune |date=December 14, 1974 |location=South Bend, IN |page=34 |access-date=July 27, 2025 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}} and appeared on ''[[M*A*S*H (TV series)|M*A*S*H]]'' as Captain Leo Bardonaro in the episode "Last Laugh". A year later, he made his film debut in [[Neil Simon]]'s classic detective spoof ''[[Murder by Death]]''.{{cite book |last1=Welsh |first1=James M. |last2=Whaley |first2=Donald M. |title=The Oliver Stone Encyclopedia |date=2013 |publisher=Scarecrow Press |isbn=978-0-8108-8352-9 |page=54 |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=a-yFqzSB1oUC&dq=James+Cromwell&pg=PA54 |language=en |chapter=Cromwell, James (1940–)}} Cromwell portrayed four different characters in four episodes of ''[[Barney Miller]]'' (1977–1981). In 1977, he appeared in the ''[[Three's Company]]'' episode "Chrissy's Night Out" as Detective Lannigan. In 1980, Cromwell guest-starred in the two-part episode "Laura Ingalls Wilder" of the long-running television series ''[[Little House on the Prairie (1974 TV series)|Little House on the Prairie]]''. He played Harve Miller, one of Almanzo Wilder's old friends.[https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0633037/characters/nm0000342/ IMDB] While Cromwell continued with regular television work throughout the 1980s, he made appearances in films with supporting roles in ''[[Tank (film)|Tank]]'', ''[[Revenge of the Nerds]]'', and ''[[Oh, God! You Devil]]'' (all 1984). He guest-starred on the sitcom ''[[Night Court]]'', playing a mental patient, along with [[Kevin Peter Hall]]. He had a starring role in the critically acclaimed film ''[[Babe (film)|Babe]]'' (1995), for which he received a nomination for the [[Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor]], and reprised his role in the sequel, ''[[Babe: Pig in the City]]'' (1998). Subsequent roles included ''[[Eraser (film)|Eraser]]'' (1996), ''[[The People vs. Larry Flynt]]'' (1996), ''[[The Education of Little Tree (film)|The Education of Little Tree]]'' (1997), ''[[L.A. Confidential (film)|L.A. Confidential]]'' (1997), ''[[Deep Impact (film)|Deep Impact]]'' (1998), ''[[The Green Mile (film)|The Green Mile]]'' (1999), ''[[The General's Daughter (film)|The General's Daughter]]'', (1999), ''[[Snow Falling on Cedars (film)|Snow Falling on Cedars]]'' (1999), ''[[Space Cowboys]]'' (2000), ''[[The Sum of All Fears (film)|The Sum of All Fears]]'' (2002), ''[[I, Robot (film)|I, Robot]]'' (2004), and ''[[The Longest Yard (2005 film)|The Longest Yard]]'' (2005). He also voiced the Colonel in [[DreamWorks Animation|DreamWorks]]' ''[[Spirit: Stallion of the Cimarron]]'' (2002).{{cite book |last1=Hamilton |first1=Jill |editor-last1=Tomassini |editor-first1=Christine |editor-last2=Schwartz |editor-first2=Carol |title=Magill's Cinema Annual, 2003 |date=2003 |publisher=Gale Group |isbn=978-1-55862-459-7 |page=447 |chapter-url=https://archive.org/details/magillscinemaann0000unse_o2u3/page/446/mode/2up?q=%22Stallion+of+the+Cimarron%22+cromwell+colonel |chapter=Spirit: Stallion of the Cimarron}} Cromwell's first ''[[Star Trek]]'' role was on ''[[Star Trek: The Next Generation]]'' in 1990, in the season 3 episode "[[The Hunted (Star Trek: The Next Generation)|The Hunted]]", followed by the 1993 episode "[[Birthright (Star Trek: The Next Generation)|Birthright, Part 1]]" as Jaglom Shrek. He also played Dr. [[Zefram Cochrane]] in ''[[Star Trek: First Contact]]'' (1996), the ''[[Star Trek: Enterprise]]'' pilot episode "[[Broken Bow (Star Trek: Enterprise)|Broken Bow]]", and the 2022 ''[[Star Trek: Lower Decks]]'' season 3 premiere episode, "Grounded". The ''Star Trek: Enterprise'' episode "[[In a Mirror, Darkly]]" reused some of the ''First Contact'' footage.{{cite web |url=http://www.trektoday.com/news/270405_02.shtml |title=StarTrek.com Offers Commentary on 'In a Mirror, Darkly' |publisher=TrekToday |date=April 27, 2005 |access-date=February 28, 2012 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120716180440/http://www.trektoday.com/news/270405_02.shtml |archive-date=July 16, 2012 |df=mdy-all }} Cromwell also appeared in a ''[[Star Trek: Deep Space Nine]]'' episode, "[[Starship Down]]", as Hanok. Cromwell's role as newspaper tycoon [[William Randolph Hearst]] in the television film ''[[RKO 281]]'' (1999) earned him an [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Supporting Actor – Miniseries or a Movie|Emmy Award nomination for Outstanding Supporting Actor in a Television Movie]]. The following year, he received his second Emmy Award nomination for playing Bishop Lionel Stewart on the [[NBC]] medical drama series ''[[ER (TV series)|ER]]''. In 2003, he appeared in the [[HBO]] miniseries ''[[Angels in America (miniseries)|Angels in America]]''. In 2004, he guest-starred as former president D. Wire Newman in ''[[The West Wing]]'' episode "[[The Stormy Present]]". From 2003 to 2005, Cromwell played [[George Sibley (Six Feet Under)|George Sibley]] in the HBO drama series ''[[Six Feet Under (TV series)|Six Feet Under]]'', which earned him his third Emmy Award nomination in 2003. Along with the rest of his castmates, he was also nominated for two [[Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by an Ensemble in a Drama Series|Screen Actors Guild Awards for Best Ensemble in a Drama Series]] in 2005 and 2006. The following year, Cromwell played [[Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh]] in ''[[The Queen (2006 film)|The Queen]]'' (2006), that earned [[Helen Mirren]] an [[Academy Award for Best Actress]]. He also guest-starred as [[List of 24 characters#Phillip Bauer|Phillip Bauer]], father of lead character [[Jack Bauer|Jack]], in the [[24 season 6|sixth season]] of the [[Fox Broadcasting Company|Fox]] thriller drama series ''[[24 (TV series)|24]]''.{{cite book |last1=Bellafante |first1=Ginia |author-link=Ginia Bellafante |chapter=In ''24'''s World, Family Is the Main Casualty |editor1-last=Burstein |editor1-first=Dan |editor2-last=de Keijzer |editor2-first=Arne J. |title=Secrets of ''24'' |date=2007 |publisher=Sterling |isbn=978-1-4027-5396-1 |pages=64–65 |chapter-url=https://archive.org/details/secretsof24unaut0000unse/page/64/mode/2up?q=%22phillip+bauer%22+cromwell}} In October 2007, Cromwell played the lead role of James Tyrone Sr. in the [[Druid Theatre Company]]'s production of [[Eugene O'Neill]]'s ''[[Long Day's Journey into Night]]'', at the [[Gaiety Theatre, Dublin|Gaiety in Dublin]] as part of the [[Dublin Theatre Festival|Ulster Bank Dublin Theatre Festival's]] 50th Anniversary.[http://www.gaietytheatre.ie/shows/LongDaysJourneyIntoNight.htm Gaiety Theatre Dublin, Ireland – Irish Theatre] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070928104050/http://www.gaietytheatre.ie/shows/LongDaysJourneyIntoNight.htm |date=September 28, 2007 }} That same year he received the King Vidor Memorial Award from the [[San Luis Obispo International Film Festival]] for his artistic achievements in film. He also starred as [[George Stacy|Captain George Stacy]] in [[Sam Raimi]]'s ''[[Spider-Man 3]]'' (2007). Cromwell played [[George H. W. Bush]] in [[Oliver Stone]]'s ''[[W. (film)|W.]]'' (2008), that chronicles the rise to power of [[George W. Bush|Bush's son]] up until the [[2003 invasion of Iraq]].{{cite web |title=W: James Cromwell vs. George Bush Snr. |url=http://suicidegirls.com/interviews/W%3A+James+Cromwell+vs.+George+Bush+Snr.+/ |publisher=[[SuicideGirls]] |date=October 15, 2008 |access-date=October 15, 2008 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081017103224/http://suicidegirls.com/interviews/W%3A+James+Cromwell+vs.+George+Bush+Snr.+/ |archive-date=October 17, 2008 |df=mdy-all}} Cromwell played the Older Canter in the sci-fi thriller ''[[Surrogates]]'' (2009), starred as horse owner [[Ogden Phipps]] in [[Disney]]'s ''[[Secretariat (film)|Secretariat]]'' (2010), portrayed Clifton in the [[Academy Award]]-winning ''[[The Artist (film)|The Artist]]'' (2011), and starred in the romantic drama ''[[Still Mine]]'' (2012). From 2012 to 2013, he appeared in the HBO series ''[[Boardwalk Empire season 3|Boardwalk Empire]]''. Cromwell also provided the voice of the main villain Professor Robert Callaghan/Yokai in the Disney movie ''[[Big Hero 6 (film)|Big Hero 6]]'' (2014). His subsequent film roles have included ''[[The Promise (2016 film)|The Promise]]'' (2016), ''[[Marshall (film)|Marshall]]'' (2017), and ''[[Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom]]'' (2018). In 2015, Cromwell executive produced the documentary ''[[Imminent Threat]]'' which tackles the War on Terror's impact on civil liberties.{{Cite web |date=July 2, 2015 |title=James Cromwell Champions Docu 'Imminent Threat' and Actor/Activist Has Stories to Tell |url=https://deadline.com/2015/07/james-cromwell-imminent-threat-documentary-1201467391/}} In 2016, Cromwell starred in [[HBO]]'s series ''[[The Young Pope]]'' alongside [[Jude Law]] and [[Diane Keaton]].{{cite web |last=Anderson |first=Ariston |title=James Cromwell on 'The Young Pope', 'Radical Politics', America's Need for 'Revolution' (Q&A) |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/james-cromwell-young-pope-radical-politics-americas-need-revolution-q-a-943358 |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |access-date=27 March 2021 |date=November 4, 2016}} In 2018, he appeared in [[HBO]]'s ''[[Succession (TV series)|Succession]]'', and [[Starz]]'s ''[[Counterpart (TV series)|Counterpart]]''.{{Cite web |last=Feinberg |first=Scott |date=2023-06-19 |title=From 'The Last of Us' to 'Succession': The Stacked Race for Drama Guest Actor |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/emmys-2023-race-drama-guest-actor-1235513790/ |access-date=2024-01-07 |website=The Hollywood Reporter |language=en-US}} In 2020, Cromwell starred in the Australian comedy-drama film ''[[Never Too Late (2020 film)|Never Too Late]]'',Maddox, Garry (16 April 2019) [https://www.smh.com.au/entertainment/movies/life-is-still-busy-over-70-for-stars-of-new-triumph-over-ageing-film-20190408-p51bxg.html Life is still busy over 70 for stars of new 'triumph over ageing' film], ''[[The Sydney Morning Herald]]''. Retrieved 20 February 2020. and in the historical drama film ''[[Emperor (2020 film)|Emperor]]''.{{Cite web|url=https://variety.com/2020/film/reviews/emperor-review-shields-green-1234734920/|title='Emperor' Review: A Runaway Slave Joins the Raid on Harpers Ferry in Forgotten Tale of Black Heroism|first=Peter|last=Debruge|date=August 15, 2020|website=Variety}} Cromwell starred in ''[[Operation Buffalo (TV series)|Operation Buffalo]]'', an Australian television comedy-drama series about the atomic bomb tests in outback Australia, which screened on [[ABC TV (Australian TV network)|ABC]] from 31 May 2020. He is currently featured in the [[HBO Max]] show ''[[Julia (2022 TV series)|Julia]]'', as Julia Child's father, John McWilliams.{{Cite web|url=https://tvovermind.com/meet-the-cast-of-julia/|title = Meet the Cast of "Julia"|date = March 30, 2022}} In 2021, Cromwell executive produced the psychedelic comedy ''[[Mondo Hollywoodland]]'', directed by Janek Ambros, who also directed ''Imminent Threat''.{{Cite web |date=July 9, 2021 |title=James Cromwell Production 'Mondo Hollywoodland' Sets Release |url=https://deadline.com/2021/07/james-cromwell-production-mondo-hollywoodland-sets-release-1234789557/}} ==Activism== Cromwell has long been an advocate of progressive causes, particularly regarding [[animal rights]]. They were charged with disorderly conduct after police said they disrupted a meeting of the Texas A&M University System Board of Regents. The two were part of a demonstration by PETA, protesting A&M's use of dogs for medical research. Both were released after posting bonds of $5,000 each.{{Cite news |title='Succession,' 'Green Mile' star James Cromwell arrested at Texas A&M protest |newspaper=Associated Press |url=https://eu.usatoday.com/story/entertainment/celebrities/2019/11/01/succession-star-james-cromwell-arrested-texas-a-m-regents-protest/4121008002/}} In May 2022, Cromwell superglued his hand to the counter of a Manhattan [[Starbucks]] to protest the surcharge for plant-based milks.{{cite web |date=May 11, 2022 |title='Succession' star James Cromwell glues his hand to a Starbucks counter in a protest |url=https://www.npr.org/2022/05/11/1098162254/succession-actor-james-cromwell-glues-hand-starbucks-counter-protest |website=NPR}} Later that year, PETA named him their 2022 Person of the Year.Jamie Burton, "[https://www.newsweek.com/james-cromwell-interview-succession-peta-animal-rights-offensive-unpopular-1769914 James Cromwell Happy to Be 'Offensive' and 'Unpopular' On PETA's Behalf]," ''Newsweek'', 28 January 2022. In April 2023, he helped rehome a pig destined for slaughter to the Indraloka Animal Sanctuary and named the pig "Babe".{{cite web |last1=Christian |first1=Charlotte |title=Vegan James Cromwell Names Rescued Pig "Babe" |url=https://www.top10films.co.uk/77293-vegan-james-cromwell-names-rescued-pig-babe/ |website=Top 10 Films |date=April 9, 2023 |access-date=9 April 2023}} ==Personal life== Cromwell married Ann Ulvestad in 1977.{{cite web|url= https://www.tcm.com/tcmdb/person/41341%7C0/James-Cromwell/|title=James Cromwell > Companions|publisher=[[Turner Classic Movies]]|access-date=May 26, 2020|archive-date=December 11, 2019|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20191211133326/https://www.tcm.com/tcmdb/person/41341%7C0/James-Cromwell/|url-status= dead}} They divorced in 1986. Together the couple had three children: Kate, John and Colin. Cromwell married actress [[Julie Cobb]] on May 29, 1986; they divorced in 2005.{{cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/life/people/2005-01-14-cromwell-divorce_x.htm |title=James Cromwell files for divorce|agency=[[Associated Press]]|via=[[USA Today]]|date=January 14, 2005|archive-date=September 22, 2018| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180922121217/https://usatoday30.usatoday.com/life/people/2005-01-14-cromwell-divorce_x.htm|url-status=live}} James Cromwell dated drama teacher Joan MacIntosh from 2005 until 2009. On January 1, 2014, Cromwell married actress [[Anna Stuart]] at the home of Stuart's former ''[[Another World (TV series)|Another World]]'' co-star [[Charles Keating (actor)|Charles Keating]].{{cite magazine|url=http://www.closerweekly.com/posts/emmy-winner-james-cromwell-marries-soap-star-anna-stuart-19048|title=Emmy Winner James Cromwell Marries Soap Star Anna Stuart!|date=January 9, 2014|magazine=[[Closer (magazine)|Closer]]|access-date=May 7, 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180302104237/http://www.closerweekly.com/posts/emmy-winner-james-cromwell-marries-soap-star-anna-stuart-19048|archive-date=March 2, 2018|df=mdy-all}}{{cite web |url=https://www.daytimeconfidential.com/.amp/2014/01/09/another-worlds-anna-stuart-marries-james-cromwell-in-charles-keatings-home |title=Another World's Anna Stuart Marries James Cromwell in Charles Keating's Home! | Daytime Confidential |access-date=2018-03-04 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180305063108/https://daytimeconfidential.com/.amp/2014/01/09/another-worlds-anna-stuart-marries-james-cromwell-in-charles-keatings-home |archive-date=March 5, 2018 |df=mdy-all }} Cromwell lives in [[Warwick, New York]].{{cite web | url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/entertainment/ct-xpm-2013-07-25-ct-mov-0726-chicago-closeup-20130725-story.html | title=James Cromwell: A bundle of contradictions | website=[[Chicago Tribune]] | date=July 25, 2013 }} At {{height|ft=6|in=7}}, Cromwell is the tallest actor nominated for an Academy Award. His son John is taller, at {{height|ft=6|in=8}}.{{cite magazine|last=Ellis|first= Cynthia|url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/cynthia-ellis/tribeca-film-festival-int_b_561477.html|title=Tribeca Film Festival Interview: John and James Cromwell of ''A .45 at 50th''|magazine=[[HuffPost]]|date=May 4, 2010|archive-date= May 26, 2020|archive-url= https://archive.today/20200526211551/https://www.huffpost.com/entry/tribeca-film-festival-int_b_561477|url-status=live|quote=John is 6'8 to James' already very tall 6'7. }} In the 2012 film [[Memorial Day (2012 film)|''Memorial Day'']], John played the young Bud Vogel, while James played him as a grandfather.{{cite web|url=http://www.movieweb.com/movie/memorial-day-2012|title=Memorial Day|access-date=June 16, 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160512205920/http://movieweb.com/movie/memorial-day-2012/|archive-date=May 12, 2016|df=mdy-all}} Both Cromwells appear as the same character at different ages in ''[[American Horror Story: Asylum]]'' (2012) and the first season of ''[[Betrayal (American TV series)|Betrayal]]'' (2013). === Political views === Cromwell's experiences of the [[Civil Rights Movement]] while on a theatre tour through several [[Deep South]] states in 1964 had a profound effect on him. The courage of local campaigners and visiting activists – Cromwell had played high school football with civil rights worker [[Michael Schwerner|Mickey Schwerner]], who was [[murders of Chaney, Goodman, and Schwerner|murdered]] with two of his colleagues in Mississippi in 1964 – convinced him to become an activist. He subsequently became involved in the [[Opposition to United States involvement in the Vietnam War|anti-Vietnam War]] movement,{{Citation |last=TYT Interviews |title=James Cromwell Interview with Cenk Uygur on The Young Turks |date=May 25, 2017 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cVnH0y2zSRI |df=mdy-all |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170714153606/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cVnH0y2zSRI |access-date=May 30, 2017 |archive-date=July 14, 2017 |url-status=live}} and by the late 1960s, Cromwell was a member of the Committee to Defend the Panthers, a group organized to defend 13 members of the [[Black Panther Party]] who had been imprisoned in New York on charges of conspiracy. All 13 were eventually found innocent and released. In a 2004 interview with [[CNN]], Cromwell praised the Panthers.{{cite news |date=June 18, 2004 |title=Black Panther, drunk priest, kind farmer |publisher=CNN |url=http://www.cnn.com/2004/SHOWBIZ/TV/06/18/james.cromwell/index.html |url-status=live |access-date=March 23, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080601221343/http://www.cnn.com/2004/SHOWBIZ/TV/06/18/james.cromwell/index.html |archive-date=June 1, 2008 |df=mdy-all}} In an October 2008 interview, Cromwell criticized the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican Party]] and the [[George W. Bush]] administration, saying that their foreign policy would "either destroy us or the entire planet". He supported the [[Bernie Sanders presidential campaign, 2016|presidential campaign]] of [[Bernie Sanders]] in the [[2016 United States presidential election|2016 U.S. presidential election]].{{cite web |title=James Cromwell on Twitter | work=Twitter |url=https://mobile.twitter.com/jamesocromwell/status/722884255089471489?lang=en |access-date=August 11, 2018 }} ==Filmography== {{Main|James Cromwell filmography}} ==Awards and nominations== {{Main|List of awards and nominations received by James Cromwell}} {| class="wikitable unsortable" |- !| Year !| Award !| Category !| Nominated work !| Result ! Tallman''' (born September 4, 1957) is an American [[actress]], [[stunt performer]], and [[studio executive]] best known for her roles in ''[[Night of the Living Dead (1990 film)|Night of the Living Dead]]'', ''[[Star Trek]]'' and ''[[Babylon 5]]''. == Early life and education == Patricia Tallman is the daughter of Jerry Tallman, a radio entertainer.{{Cite web|title=Patricia Tallman Biography (1957-)|url=http://www.filmreference.com/film/2/Patricia-Tallman.html|access-date=2012-10-10|website=www.filmreference.com}} After graduating from [[Glenbard West High School]] in [[Glen Ellyn, Illinois]] in 1975,{{Cite web|title=1975 Glenbard West High School|url=https://www.classmates.com/yearbooks/Glenbard-West-High-School/63247?page=150|access-date=2014-08-27|website=[[classmates.com]]}} she joined the theater arts program of [[Carnegie Mellon University]], which awarded her a [[Bachelor of Fine Arts]] degree.{{Cite book|last=Tallman|first=Patricia|title=Pleasure Thresholds|publisher=Publishing 180|year=2011|isbn=978-0-9821005-2-3}}{{Rp|19}}{{Cite news|last1=Arar|first1=Yardena|date=1990-10-24|title=Tallman Tumbles into Big-Time Role – 'Living Dead' Actress Dislikes Horror Pictures|page=L21|work=[[Los Angeles Daily News]]|url=https://infoweb.newsbank.com/apps/news/document-view?p=NewsBank&docref=news/0EF60E7DDF4EEC47&f=basic|access-date=2018-07-20}} == Career == In television, Tallman worked on the soap opera ''[[Generations (U.S. TV series)|Generations]]''. Later, she had guest-starring roles on ''[[Tales from the Darkside]]'', as well as the science-fiction shows ''[[Star Trek: The Next Generation]]'', ''[[Star Trek: Deep Space Nine]]'', and ''[[Star Trek: Voyager]]''. As an actress and stunt performer, she worked on 50 episodes across the ''Star Trek'' franchise. Tallman played [[Lyta Alexander]] in the ''Babylon 5'' series pilot, recurring in seasons two and three, and starring in seasons four and five.{{Cite news|last1=Pierce|first1=Scott D.|date=1990-10-25|title='Babylon 5' full of surprises|page=S3|work=[[Deseret News]]|url=https://infoweb.newsbank.com/apps/news/document-view?p=NewsBank&docref=news/0F364C8890C6697A&f=basic|access-date=2018-07-20}} Tallman collaborated with fellow Carnegie Mellon alumnus [[George A. Romero]] on several films, including ''[[Knightriders]]'', ''[[Monkey Shines (film)|Monkey Shines]]'', and ''[[Creepshow 2]]'' (in which Tallman performed stunts).{{Cite web|last=Mennenga|first=Michael R.|date=2005-07-28|title=Slice of SciFi #17: Interview with Patricia Tallman|url=http://www.sliceofscifi.com/2005/07/28/slice-of-sci-fi-017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070927190834/http://www.sliceofscifi.com/2005/07/28/slice-of-sci-fi-017|archive-date=2007-09-27|access-date=2012-10-10|website=www.sliceofscifi.com}} In 1990, Tallman starred as Barbara in the [[Tom Savini]]-directed [[Night of the Living Dead (1990 film)|remake]] of the 1968 film ''[[Night of the Living Dead]]''.{{Cite web|date=2009-10-21|title=TRINITY OF TERRORS Updates & More!|url=http://www.fangoria.com/eventsmain/weekend-of-horrors/woh-updates/118-las-vegas-2009/4350-trinity-of-terrors-updates-a-more.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091021083314/http://www.fangoria.com/eventsmain/weekend-of-horrors/woh-updates/118-las-vegas-2009/4350-trinity-of-terrors-updates-a-more.html|archive-date=2009-10-21|access-date=2021-02-21|website=[[Fangoria]]}} In 1992, she played the Possessed Witch under heavy make-up in the cult classic ''[[Army of Darkness]]'', as well as the Witch in the modern day scenes.{{citation needed|date=December 2018}} In 1993, Tallman's most notable stunt work came as stunt double for [[Laura Dern]] throughout [[Steven Spielberg]]'s ''[[Jurassic Park (film)|Jurassic Park]]''. In addition, she served as stunt double for [[Laurel Holloman]], who portrayed [[vampire hunter]] [[Justine Cooper (Angel)|Justine Cooper]] in the series ''[[Angel (1999 TV series)|Angel]]''; a photo of Tallman was also used as the photo of Justine Cooper's dead twin sister. In a 2001 episode of the TV series ''[[Sheena (TV series)|Sheena]]'', she guest-starred as the villain Caroline Dula. Tallman appeared in the 2002 psychological horror short ''Jennifer Is Dead'', the black comedy ''For Pete's Wake!'', and guest spots on ''[[Without a Trace]]'' and ''[[Castle (TV series)|Castle]]''. Tallman appeared in ''[[InAlienable]]'' (2008) and the horror film ''[[Dead Air (2009 film)|Dead Air]]'' (2009). Tallman played Holly in ''[[Atlas Shrugged: Part II]]'' (2012). Tallman has performed voice roles including playing the leading part of evil detective Jean Richmond in the Radio Repertory Company of America's production of ''Lives of the Cat'' and in some of the Anne Manx sequels (sold as radio plays on CD).{{Cite web|title=Radio Repertory Company of America|url=http://www.rrca.com/lives.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200126140509/http://www.rrca.com/lives.html|archive-date=2020-01-26|access-date=2012-02-25|website=www.rrca.com}} In 2011, Tallman published her autobiography ''Pleasure Thresholds'', the title inspired by the scene she auditioned to earn the role of Lyta Alexander. In 2012, Tallman became CEO and executive producer of [[Studio JMS]] in partnership with her then-boyfriend, [[J. Michael Straczynski]], the creator of ''[[Babylon 5]]''.{{Cite news|last=Dave|first=McNary|date=2013-02-01|title=Motion Picture Capital backs 'Flickering Light'|newspaper=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|url=https://variety.com/2013/film/news/motion-picture-capital-backs-flickering-light-1118065553/|access-date=2013-02-17}} In 2013, she left the company.{{Cite web|title=The Team|url=http://www.studiojms.com/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130603164034/http://www.studiojms.com/|archive-date=2013-06-03|access-date=2021-02-21|website=studiojms.com}} In May 2014, Tallman played the male role of Lespere in a theatrical production of Ray Bradbury's ''[[The Illustrated Man#"Kaleidoscope"|Kaleidoscope]]'' at Sci-Fest LA 2014, a theater festival.{{Cite news|last=Sutton|first=Angie Fiedler|date=2014-05-08|title=Science Fiction … Theatre?: Sci-Fest Launches With a [[University of Washington]] ([[Bachelor of Fine Arts|BFA]]) | occupation = Actor | years_active = 1971–present | spouse = Alice Cadogan{{cite web |title= - 17th July 1996 Actor Jeffrey Combs and wife Alice Cadogan -|url=https://www.alamy.com/universal-city-california-usa-17th-july-1996-actor-jeffrey-combs-and-wife-alice-cadogan-attend-universal-pictures-the-frighteners-premiere-at-cineplex-odeon-universal-city-cinemas-on-july-17-1996-in-universal-city-california-usa-photo-by-barry-kingalamy-stock-photo-image554643364.html |website=alamy.com |publisher=[[Alamy]] |access-date=19 December 2025}}{{cite web |title=Jeffrey Combs... and wife Alice attend the "Star Trek: Enterprise" Finale Party ...April 13, 2005 |url=https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/news-photo/actor-jeffrey-combs-and-wife-alice-attend-the-star-trek-news-photo/52628134 |website=gettyimages.com |publisher=[[Getty Images]] |access-date=19 December 2025}} }} '''Jeffrey Alan Combs''' (born September 9, 1954) is an American actor. He is best known for starring as [[Herbert West]] in the [[H.P. Lovecraft]] adaptation ''[[Re-Animator]]'' (1985) and portraying a number of characters in the ''[[Star Trek]]'' universe, most notably [[Liquidator Brunt|Brunt]] and the various [[List of Star Trek: Deep Space Nine characters#Weyoun|Weyouns]] on ''[[Star Trek: Deep Space Nine]]'' (1994–1999), and [[List of Star Trek: Enterprise characters#Thy'lek Shran|Shran]] on ''[[Star Trek: Enterprise]]'' (2001–2005). Combs has been a prominent figure within the [[horror film|horror genre]] through most of his career, acting in eight films directed by ''Re-Animator'' director [[Stuart Gordon]] such as ''[[From Beyond (film)|From Beyond]]'' (1986), ''[[The Pit and the Pendulum (1991 film)|The Pit and the Pendulum]]'' (1991), and ''[[Castle Freak]]'' (1995). Other horror film appearances include ''[[Necronomicon (film)|Necronomicon]]'' (1993), [[Peter Jackson]]'s ''[[The Frighteners]]'' (1996), ''[[I Still Know What You Did Last Summer]]'' (1998), ''[[House on Haunted Hill (1999 film)|House on Haunted Hill]]'' (1999), and ''[[Would You Rather (film)|Would You Rather]]'' (2012). As a voice actor, Combs is best known as the voice of [[Question (character)|Question]] on ''[[Justice League Unlimited]]'' (2004–2006) and Ratchet on ''[[Transformers: Prime]]'' (2010–2013).{{cite web|title=Jeffrey Combs|url=https://www.nytimes.com/movies/person/14373/Jeffrey-Combs/filmography|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402181008/http://www.nytimes.com/movies/person/14373/Jeffrey-Combs/filmography|url-status=dead|department=Movies & TV Dept.|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=2015|archive-date=April 2, 2015}} ==Early life== Combs was born in [[Oxnard, California]], the fifth of nine children{{cite web | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bQZduhlbM1A?t=483 | title=Shuttlepod Episode 004: "That's Shrantastic!" with Jeffrey Combs | website=[[YouTube]] |last1=The Shuttlepod Show |date=Mar 13, 2022 |url-status=live |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20230927160731/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bQZduhlbM1A |archive-date= Sep 27, 2023 }} born to Jean Owens (formerly Sullins; 1921–1986) and Eugene "Gene" Combs (1922–1999), and raised in [[Lompoc, California|Lompoc]]. Both of his parents were from the [[Ozarks]] region of [[Arkansas]].{{cite web | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bQZduhlbM1A?t=473 | title=Shuttlepod Episode 004: "That's Shrantastic!" with Jeffrey Combs | website=[[YouTube]] |last1=The Shuttlepod Show |date=Mar 13, 2022 |url-status=live |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20230927160731/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bQZduhlbM1A |archive-date= Sep 27, 2023 }} A graduate of [[Lompoc High School]], as a senior, Combs played the lead role of Captain Fisby in a stage production of ''[[The Teahouse of the August Moon (play)|The Teahouse of the August Moon]]''. Combs then attended [[Santa Maria, California|Santa Maria]]'s [[Pacific Conservatory of the Performing Arts]] at [[Allan Hancock College]], and later developed his acting skills in the [[University of Washington School of Drama#Acting|Professional Actor's Training Program]] at the [[University of Washington]] from which he graduated in the late 1970s.{{Cite book|last=Olson|first=Christopher J.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=yUdODwAAQBAJ&q=University+of+Washington+Jeffrey+Combs%3A&pg=PA186|title=100 Greatest Cult Films|date=April 12, 2018|publisher=Rowman & Littlefield|isbn=978-1-4422-1104-9|language=en}} In 1980, after several years performing in playhouses on the [[West Coast of the United States|West Coast]], Combs moved to Los Angeles. He landed his first role in the film ''[[Honky Tonk Freeway]]'' (1981), playing an unnamed drive-in teller. His first horror film role came two years later in ''[[Frightmare (1981 film)|Frightmare]]'' (1983).{{Cite book|last=Rowan|first=Terry|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BjyyCQAAQBAJ&q=Frightmare+Jeffrey+Combs%3A&pg=PA36|title=The Book of the Undead A Zombie Film Guide|date=August 16, 2014 |publisher=Lulu.com|isbn=978-1-312-43947-4}}{{self-published source|date=May 2020}}{{self-published inline|date=February 2020}} ==Career== Combs's best-known horror role is [[Herbert West]], the main character in the film ''[[Re-Animator]]'' (1985),{{cite web|work=[[The New York Times]]|title=Re Animator (1985) SCREEN: STUART GORDON DIRECTS 'RE-ANIMATOR'|author-link=Janet Maslin|first=Janet|last=Maslin|date=October 18, 1985|url=https://www.nytimes.com/movie/review?res=9E04EED91E39F93BA25753C1A963948260}} and its two sequels. He portrayed author [[H. P. Lovecraft]] (creator of the Herbert West character) in the film ''[[Necronomicon (film)|Necronomicon: Book of the Dead]]'' (1993) and has starred in eight adaptations of Lovecraft's works. Other film credits include ''The Attic Expeditions'' (2001), ''[[FeardotCom]]'' (2002), ''[[House on Haunted Hill (1999 film)|House on Haunted Hill]]'' (1999), ''[[I Still Know What You Did Last Summer]]'' (1998) and ''[[The Frighteners]]'' (1996).{{cite web| last=Mcivar| first=Brice| title=Q&A: Jeffrey Combs| url=http://www.fangoria.com/new/exclusive-qa-jeffrey-combs-on-motivational-growth/| work=[[The New York Times]]| date=August 9, 2011| access-date=August 9, 2011| archive-date=February 17, 2015| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150217235118/http://www.fangoria.com/new/exclusive-qa-jeffrey-combs-on-motivational-growth/| url-status=dead}} Combs has had roles in many science fiction television series. He starred as the telepath Harriman Gray in first-season episode "[[Eyes (Babylon 5)|Eyes]]" (1994) of ''[[Babylon 5]]''. In 2001, he played the sinister Dr. Ek in ''The Attic Expeditions''. In August 2005, he appeared for the first time on the science fiction series ''[[The 4400]]'' as [[Kevin Burkhoff|Dr. Kevin Burkhoff]] which became a recurring role by 2006. In early 2007, he played a highly fictionalized [[Edgar Allan Poe]] in "[[The Black Cat (Masters of Horror episode)|The Black Cat]]" episode of ''[[Masters of Horror]]''.[http://www.ugo.com/channels/filmtv/features/mastersofhorror/combs.asp Jeffrey Combs, Star of "The Black Cat"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080622075642/http://www.ugo.com/channels/filmTv/features/mastersofhorror/combs.asp |date=June 22, 2008 }}, [[UGO Networks|UGO]] In the 2012 miniseries ''[[Dorothy and the Witches of Oz]]'' (sometimes called ''The Witches of Oz''), he had a small role as a fictionalized version of [[L. Frank Baum]]. [[File:Jeffrey Combs (21268215296).jpg|thumb|upright|Combs in 2015]] Combs has also worked as a voiceover artist. His voiceover roles include the [[Scarecrow (DC Comics)|Scarecrow]] in ''[[The New Batman Adventures]]'', the [[Question (character)|Question]] in ''[[Justice League Unlimited]]'', Ratchet in ''[[Transformers: Prime]]'', the [[Leader (character)|Leader]] in ''[[The Avengers: Earth's Mightiest Heroes]]'', the [[Rat King (Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles)|Rat King]] in ''[[Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (2012 TV series)|Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles]]'', and [[Brainiac]] in ''[[Injustice 2]]''. He also narrated the 25th anniversary of ''[[Re-Animator]]'' at the [[Fantasia Festival|2010 FanTasia]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.dreadcentral.com/news/38586/fantasia-2010-days-5-9|title=Fantasia 2010: Days 5 Through 9|date=July 16, 2010 }} In July 2009, Combs returned to his stage roots and reprised his role as Edgar Allan Poe in a one-man theatrical show, ''Nevermore...an Evening with Edgar Allan Poe,'' at [[The Steve Allen Theater]] in Hollywood, California.[http://www.steveallentheater.com/nevermore Stebe Allen Theater – Nevermore] Although it was supposed to run for only a month, it enjoyed much success and sold-out crowds, and was extended four times, until closing in Los Angeles on December 19, 2009. The show had its East Coast debut on January 23 and 24, 2010 at Westminster Hall in Baltimore, Maryland, Poe's final resting place.[http://www.poebicentennial.com/events.html Baltimore Poe Bicentennial Celebration] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091228194129/http://poebicentennial.com/events.html |date=December 28, 2009 }} A tour of the Saturn Award-nominated{{Cite web|url=http://www.dreadcentral.com/news/38614/fantasia-2010-days-10-and-11|title=Fantasia 2010: Days 10 and 11|date=October 18, 2012}} ''Nevermore'' was subsequently planned.{{Cite web|url=http://www.dreadcentral.com/news/35577/nevermore-heading-san-diego-two-performances|title=Nevermore Heading to San Diego for Two Performances|date=July 18, 2012}} Combs starred with [[Andrew Divoff]] in the 2012 Screen Media Films release ''[[Night of the Living Dead 3D: Re-Animation]]'', a prequel to the 2006 film ''[[Night of the Living Dead 3D]]'' directed by [[Jeff Broadstreet]]. In 2012, he also played the sadistic Dr. Lambrick in another horror-thriller, ''[[Would You Rather (film)|Would You Rather]]''. ===''Star Trek''=== On television, Combs enjoyed popular success playing a number of alien characters on the various modern ''Star Trek'' incarnations, beginning with ''[[Star Trek: Deep Space Nine]]'' in 1994, and continuing to ''[[Star Trek: Voyager]]'' in 2000, ''[[Star Trek: Enterprise]]'' in 2001 and ''[[Star Trek: Lower Decks]]'' in 2021. He has played nine onscreen roles in the ''Star Trek'' universe. His largest science-fiction role to date was his regular guest role on ''Deep Space Nine'' as the [[Vorta]] clone [[Weyoun]]. Combs has said that Weyoun was his favorite ''Star Trek'' role, and that he had considerable input in developing the character.{{cite video |people=Jeffrey Combs |year=2004 |title=StarTrek.com First Person |url= https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FjA-hvKiCk0&feature=endscreen&NR=1 |publisher=Paramount Pictures |access-date=May 12, 2012}} On the same series, Combs had a recurring role as the [[Ferengi]] character [[List of Star Trek: Deep Space Nine characters#Brunt|Brunt]]. During the ''DS9'' episode "[[The Dogs of War (Star Trek: Deep Space Nine)|The Dogs of War]]", he appeared as both Weyoun and Brunt, becoming one of the few ''Star Trek'' actors to play two characters in the same episode (others including [[Patrick Stewart]], [[Brent Spiner]], and [[Brian Markinson]]).Peter Durst and Sulan, see [[Brian Markinson#Filmography|the Filmography section]]Jean-Luc Picard and Michael Williams, see ''[[The Defector (Star Trek: The Next Generation)|The Defector]]'' Combs wanted the characters to appear in the same scene, but the logistics and expense worked against it.{{cite web |title=Star Trek Online Community Q&A with Jeffrey Combs! |url=https://www.arcgames.com/de/games/xbox/star-trek-online/news/detail/10887074-community-q%2526a-with-jeffrey-combs%2521 |date=April 24, 2018 |access-date=May 13, 2020}} On ''Enterprise'', Combs had a recurring role as [[Shran]], an [[Andorian]] military officer. ''Enterprise'' producer [[Manny Coto]] once said in an interview that he had hoped to make Combs a regular on ''Enterprise'' had the series been renewed for a fifth season.{{cite web|url=http://trekmovie.com/2009/08/10/vegascon09-braga-coto-talk-enterprise-season-5-star-trek-2009-more/|last=Pascale|first=Anthony|title=VegasCon09: Braga & Coto Talk Enterprise Season 5 + Star Trek 2009 & more|publisher=[[TrekMovie.com]]|location=[[Las Vegas, Nevada]]|date=August 10, 2009|access-date=June 13, 2017}} In addition to his recurring ''Star Trek'' roles, Combs had non-recurring roles as human police officer Kevin Mulkahey,[http://www.startrek.com/database_article/far-beyond-the-stars Startrek.com Deep Space Nine – Far Beyond the Stars] alien Tiron on ''Deep Space Nine,'' alien [[Penk (Star Trek)|Penk]] on ''Voyager,'' and Ferengi pirate Krem on ''Enterprise''. Along with many other actors, writers and creators of the show, Combs also had a cameo appearance as a holographic patron in Vic's Lounge in the final episode of ''Deep Space Nine''. He also voices the character of Romulan Commander Suldok for the ''[[Star Trek: Elite Force II]]'' video game.{{Cite web |last=Webb |first=Andy |date=September 9, 2023 |title=Every Star Trek Character Played by Jeffrey Combs, Ranked |url=https://www.startrek.com/news/every-star-trek-character-played-by-jeffrey-combs-ranked |access-date=2025-07-04 |website=www.startrek.com |language=en}} In 2021, he had a guest voice role as AGIMUS, an evil computer, in episode 7, season 2 of ''[[Star Trek: Lower Decks]]'', which he reprised in seasons 3 and 4.{{Cite web |date=September 27, 2021 |title=Catching Up With Jeffrey Combs |url=https://www.startrek.com/news/catching-up-with-jeffrey-combs |access-date=2025-07-04 |website=www.startrek.com |language=en}} ==Filmography== ===Film=== {| class="wikitable sortable" |- !
